report.topic: The Wokwi ecosystem for running and testing the autopark ESP32-S3 Arduino/PlatformIO firmware without the board: simulator engine, VS Code and JetBrains front ends, CLI and CI, Python and pytest clients, custom chips. State checked on 2026-09-29.

candidates.name: Wokwi Simulator (wokwi.com) and its ESP32 simulation engine
candidates.license: Proprietary SaaS from Wokwi B.V. The ESP32 engine is closed source. The docs repo (wokwi-docs) is MIT.
candidates.latest_version: Rolling web service with no public version numbers. The ESP32 docs page reflects the wokwi-docs push of 2026-09-16, and the self-hosted engine image wokwi/wokwi-ci-server was rebuilt on 2026-09-27.
candidates.summary: Browser simulator. Its closed ESP32 engine also powers Wokwi for VS Code, the CLI/CI service and the Python/pytest clients, so the coverage below applies to every candidate. For ESP32-S3 it simulates the cores, GPIO, IOMUX, UART, USB CDC, USB-Serial-JTAG (serial only), I2C master, SPI, LEDC, PCNT, DMA, timers, watchdog, ADC and RNG. It also has a parts library, an 8-channel logic analyzer and custom chips, and accepts uploaded .bin, .elf or .uf2 firmware.

capabilities.detail: Closed-source SaaS. The ToS forbids decompiling or reverse engineering the Service software. Only Wokwi's AVR (avr8js) and RP2040 (rp2040js) engines and its UI elements are MIT; no ESP32 engine source is published.

Simulated on S3: cores, GPIO with interrupts, IOMUX, PSRAM, UART, USB (CDC), USB Serial+JTAG (serial only), I2C (master), SPI, LEDC, PCNT, DMA, WiFi, timers, watchdog, ADC, RNG and AES/SHA/RSA. Partial: RTC (pull-ups/pull-downs only), TWAI, RMT (TX only). Not implemented: I2S, MCPWM, Bluetooth, ULP. Boards: ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 and XIAO ESP32-S3. The flashSize attribute accepts 2 to 32 MB (default 4).

Runs any compiled Arduino build. Espressif's report generated 2026-09-29 shows its arduino-esp32 master (3.x) validation suite passing on Wokwi ESP32-S3, for example gpio 1/1, timer 8/8, ticker 19/19, uart 25/25, i2c_master 8/8, multitasking 10/10 and nvs 78/78. Wokwi's PlatformIO examples use an unpinned espressif32 platform, which means Arduino 2.0.x. 2.0.17 on S3 was not specifically verified.

Manual only in the browser: F1 > 'Upload Firmware and Start Simulation…' takes a .bin, .elf or .uf2 such as .pio/build/esp32s3/firmware.bin. The docs recommend a single esptool merge_bin image. An image without a bootloader is loaded at 0x10000. No project or CI integration.
The browser has only its own Serial Monitor (text input with a configurable newline, plus plotter and terminal modes). RFC2217 serial forwarding is documented only for Wokwi for VS Code and the CLI.

Setting the board attribute 'serialInterface':'USB_SERIAL_JTAG' routes the serial monitor to USB-Serial-JTAG: serial works, JTAG does not, and the $serialMonitor wires must be removed. USB OTG CDC (TinyUSB) is also listed for S3. Wokwi's nightly tests run ESP-IDF's usb_serial_jtag test app on esp32s3 with this attribute. Arduino HWCDC on S3 is unproven: HWCDC only transmits while its FreeRTOS tick hook keeps seeing the USB SOF interrupt bit (HWCDC.cpp in 2.0.17). arduino-esp32 uses HWCDC on Wokwi only for local ESP32-P4 runs and forces UART0 in CI (PR #12875, merged 2026-09-15). Only one serial stream can be exposed (issue #732, open).

LEDC is simulated ('Used by analogWrite(), Servo, Buzzer'), and there is a servo part. The 8-channel logic analyzer samples at 1 GHz, supports triggers and channel names, and writes a VCD file for PulseView or GTKWave when the simulation stops. Earlier LEDC bugs (#585, duty above 4094; #570, S3 servo) are closed.

Interactive only. Pushbuttons respond to clicks and keyboard shortcuts, Ctrl-click latches them, and 'bounce':'0' disables bounce; slide and DIP switches are also available. INPUT_PULLUP with a button to GND is verified on ESP32-S3 by arduino-esp32's Wokwi gpio test. Scripted control needs the CLI or the Python API.

Built-in I2C/SPI parts include MPU6050 (with automation controls), BMP180, DS1307, SSD1306, SH1107, MFRC522 and HX711. There is no AS5600, VL53L1X, BNO085 or MT6701 part. Custom chips can add them, and a community AS5600 custom-chip project exists. The public BNO085 and VL53L0X projects on wokwi.com contain no sensor model. I2C is master-only with no 10-bit addressing.

Timers and the watchdog are simulated. Wokwi's nightly tests run ESP-IDF's [task_wdt] Unity group on esp32s3, and arduino-esp32's Ticker test (esp_timer, 19/19) and timer test (8/8) pass on Wokwi S3. RTC support is only partial. Unknown and undocumented: panic/abort handling, the esp_restart path, esp_reset_reason() values, and whether LEDC keeps running across a CPU-only reset. By default ('cpuFrequency':'auto') instructions run at about 8 MHz while peripheral timing stays exact, so CPU-bound latencies such as the panic hook's time-to-low are not realistic unless you set a MHz value or 'max'. A TWDT false-timeout bug with tickless idle (#1075) is closed.
Interactive browser tool. Automation goes through the CLI, the CI action or the Python clients.
Runs in a desktop browser. The FAQ says Chrome is usually faster than Firefox.
Cannot flash or test boards. Wokwi's esptool-js fork (wokwi/flasher-esp32) is archived.

candidates.fit: Useful as a zero-install first look. Upload the PlatformIO build of the PWM-enabled variant to an ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 diagram with a logic analyzer on the ESC/servo pins and a pushbutton as the E-stop, then check boot, pulse widths and E-stop behaviour by eye. It cannot carry the COBS link from autopark.transport or automate anything, so it is only a smoke test. Its engine limits carry over to every other Wokwi tool: closed source, HWCDC unproven, reset behaviour undocumented.
caveats: The engine is closed and unversioned, so behaviour can change between deployments without notice.
The simulated clock can run slower than wall-clock time when simulation speed is below 100% (documented in the WiFi guide: https://docs.wokwi.com/guides/esp32-wifi).
Free-tier projects are public; unlisted projects need a paid plan.
The binary COBS protocol shows up as garbage in the text serial monitor.
candidates.cost_notes: Free (Community tier) for personal, non-commercial use under the ToS. Paid plans with annual billing: Hobby €5.6/mo, Hobby+ €8.1/mo, Pro €20/seat/mo. Classroom is priced on request.

candidates.name: Wokwi for VS Code (extension)
candidates.license: Proprietary and closed source, as its license file states. A license is required after the free trial. Open-source projects get a free, renewable 30-day license.
candidates.latest_version: 3.7.0 (2026-08-28), on both the VS Marketplace and Open VSX
candidates.summary: Runs the Wokwi engine locally inside VS Code from wokwi.toml and diagram.json; the README says 'Your code never leaves your computer'. It reloads the firmware on rebuild and provides an RFC2217 serial server, a GDB server, logic-analyzer VCD export, custom chips and a private IoT gateway. The interactive diagram editor needs a paid license.

capabilities.detail: The license file says 'Wokwi for VS Code is a proprietary (closed source) software', and the ToS forbids reverse engineering.
Same engine and ESP32-S3 coverage as wokwi.com. ESP32 ROMs are bundled with the extension, and GDB debugging is listed for S3.
Runs any compiled Arduino-ESP32 build. Arduino 3.x on S3 is backed by Espressif's Wokwi results; 2.0.17 on S3 was not specifically verified.

In wokwi.toml, set firmware='.pio/build/esp32s3/firmware.bin' and elf='.pio/build/esp32s3/firmware.elf', the same pattern Wokwi's PlatformIO examples use. Auto-reload for PlatformIO was fixed in 2.3.7. An app-only firmware.bin runs behind Wokwi's own bootloader and partition table; for the real 8 MB layout, use a merged image and set 'flashSize':'8'.

Setting rfc2217ServerPort = 4000 (since 1.3.0, 2023-02-16) lets Python open serial.serial_for_url('rfc2217://localhost:4000'), which SerialVehicleIO can use directly. The simulation pauses if the simulator tab is hidden (docs) or if VS Code is in the background (#899, open since 2024-10-19). A 2023 report of binary data loss over RFC2217 (#545) was closed with no documented fix.

Same engine behaviour: 'serialInterface':'USB_SERIAL_JTAG' gives serial but not JTAG, and Arduino HWCDC on S3 is unverified. RFC2217 forwards the single serial-monitor stream, so UART0 boot/panic logs and the USB CDC link cannot both be exposed (#732).
LEDC is simulated. The logic-analyzer capture is saved automatically as wokwi.vcd, or to the vcdFile path (option added in 3.2.0, 2026-01-25), when the simulation stops.
Interactive clicks and keyboard only. The extension has no scenario runner or control API, so scripted E-stop toggling needs the CLI or the Python client.
Built-in parts, plus custom chips via [[chip]] entries in wokwi.toml; 3.6.1 (2026-08-26) fixed chip loading and reloading. There are no built-in AS5600, VL53L1X, BNO085 or MT6701 models.

Same engine fidelity as wokwi.com: timers and TWDT are covered by test suites, while panic, restart, reset reason and LEDC across a reset are undocumented. With gdbServerPort set, 'Start Simulator and Wait for Debugger' lets you break in the panic hook and step the GPIO register writes.

Not headless: it needs the VS Code GUI with the simulator tab visible. It works for local host-in-the-loop scripts over RFC2217, but not for CI. It needs an internet connection except in the Pro offline mode.
Runs in VS Code on Windows; the docs give the Windows path to PlatformIO's xtensa gdb. Also published on Open VSX.
Cannot flash or test boards. A host test written against pyserial can later switch from rfc2217://localhost:4000 to the board's COM port, with PlatformIO doing the flashing.

candidates.fit: The best local, interactive loop on Windows. It reads the .pio outputs directly, reloads on rebuild, gives the Python host package a real serial link over RFC2217, and adds GDB and VCD capture. The free license covers only public, OSI-licensed GitHub projects. autopark's remote (github.com/thbn12082/autopark) returns 404 to anonymous requests and the repo has no LICENSE file, so this means Hobby+ (€8.1/mo, annual billing) or opening the repo. Not usable for CI.
caveats: The simulation stalls when the tab is hidden or VS Code is in the background (#899), which also stalls RFC2217 host tests.
Needs internet for licensing; offline mode is Pro only.
Collects telemetry (opt out with telemetry.enableTelemetry), and the ToS allow usage analysis to check license compliance.
The diagram editor needs a paid license; otherwise edit diagram.json by hand.
All engine caveats apply: HWCDC, reset semantics, the ~8 MHz CPU cap.
candidates.cost_notes: The free 30-day renewable personal license applies only to open-source projects, which the ToS define as public on github.com, OSI-licensed and not commercialized. Hobby+ (€8.1/mo, annual billing) includes Wokwi for VS Code. Pro (€20/seat/mo, annual billing) covers commercial use and the offline plug-in.

candidates.name: Wokwi CLI (wokwi-cli) with automation scenarios
candidates.license: MIT per the repo LICENSE; the package.json license fields say ISC. Includes the @wokwi/client JS library and the @wokwi/rfc2217 package. The simulation itself runs on the proprietary Wokwi Simulation API: the cloud by default, or a self-hosted server named in WOKWI_CLI_SERVER.
candidates.summary: Headless runner. It uploads the diagram, firmware, ELF and custom chips to the simulation server and streams serial output. It exits on expected or failure text, on timeout (exit code 42) or when the scenario completes. YAML scenarios (alpha) support delay, wait-serial, write-serial, set-control, expect-pin, expect-chip-output, take-screenshot and touch steps. Other features: --vcd-file export, the rfc2217ServerPort serial bridge, a GDB server (-g), lint, init, chip compile and an experimental MCP server.

capabilities.detail: The client is MIT, but the engine it drives is closed and remote (default wss://wokwi.com/api/ws/beta).
Same engine. Wokwi's own nightly ESP32-S3 tests (task_wdt, usb_serial_jtag) are run through wokwi-cli.
Works with any firmware. Wokwi's PlatformIO/Arduino example runs through the CLI in GitHub Actions, and Espressif's Wokwi results show Arduino 3.x working on S3.

`wokwi-cli init` detects platformio.ini and sets firmware and elf to .pio/build/<first env>/firmware.bin and .elf. It also accepts a merged .bin, .uf2, .elf, or an ESP-IDF-style flasher_args.json with several flash sections. The official example runs `pio run`, then `wokwi-cli . --scenario button.test.yaml`.

With rfc2217ServerPort set in wokwi.toml, the CLI opens a local RFC2217 server bridged both ways to the simulated serial monitor. It escapes the 0xFF (IAC) byte, so binary data passes intact, and pyserial's rfc2217:// URL can feed SerialVehicleIO directly. Also available: --interactive (stdin to serial) and --serial-log-file. Pass --timeout 0 for open-ended sessions; the default is 30 s of simulated time. The docs still describe RFC2217 as a VS Code feature, but the CLI source implements it.
'serialInterface':'USB_SERIAL_JTAG' works through the CLI, as Wokwi's S3 USB-Serial-JTAG test shows. Arduino HWCDC on S3 is unverified, and only one serial stream is available.

--vcd-file exports the logic-analyzer capture after the run, so a Python parser can check 1000–2000 µs pulses at 50 Hz offline. expect-pin only samples the level at one instant. Custom-chip log lines are printed as [chip] ... and can be asserted with expect-chip-output.

The set-control step drives the pushbutton's 'pressed' control (0/1), plus potentiometer, MPU6050, joystick, HX711, photoresistor and custom-chip controls; delays are in simulated time. To model the E-stop, wire a pushbutton from the pin to GND with 'bounce':'0': hold it pressed for a closed circuit, release it for an open circuit.
Loads [[chip]] entries from wokwi.toml. `wokwi-cli chip compile` downloads WASI-SDK and wokwi-api.h automatically. There are no built-in AS5600, VL53L1X, BNO085 or MT6701 models.
Same engine fidelity as wokwi.com. GDB (gdbServerPort in wokwi.toml or -g, v0.27.0+) starts the simulation paused so you can break on the panic path; the server must advertise the 'gdb' feature.

Headless with exit codes, so it fits any CI. It needs WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN (starts with wok_, 44 characters) from a free account's CI dashboard. Monthly quota in simulated minutes: Free 50, Hobby/Hobby+ 200, Pro 2000. Firmware goes to Wokwi's cloud and is deleted after the run; on-premise deployment is by arrangement. Scenarios are alpha, and the docs' expect-pin example uses 'expected:' although v0.27.1 reads 'value:'.
Every release ships a native wokwi-cli-win-x64.exe, and there is a PowerShell installer (iwr https://wokwi.com/ci/install.ps1 | iex). chip compile fetches the x86_64-windows WASI-SDK.
Cannot flash or test boards. Host tests that use pyserial over the RFC2217 bridge can later point at the real COM port, with PlatformIO doing the flashing.

candidates.fit: The main automation entry point, and it runs natively on Windows. It uses the same wokwi.toml and diagram.json as VS Code without an extension license. Scenarios can press and release the E-stop and check serial text, and VCD export lets you measure ESC and servo pulses. Since v0.23.0 its RFC2217 bridge also lets the existing autopark.transport code drive the real firmware. The limits are cloud round-trip time, the 50-minute free monthly quota (counted in simulated time) and possible drift between simulated and wall-clock time for the 10 ms / 20 Hz protocol.
caveats: Firmware is uploaded to Wokwi's cloud. Latency is undocumented, and so is whether cloud runs are throttled to real time.
The default 30 s simulated-time timeout needs --timeout 0 (or larger) for host-in-the-loop sessions, and every simulated minute counts against the quota.
The scenario format is alpha, and the docs lag the code.
Only one serial port can be exposed per simulation (#732).
Raw binary protocol output is echoed to stdout; use -q and --serial-log-file.
candidates.cost_notes: The CLI is free but needs a Wokwi account token. Monthly simulated-minute quotas: Free 50, Hobby (€5.6/mo) 200, Hobby+ (€8.1/mo) 200, Pro (€20/seat/mo) 2000, with prices for annual billing. Larger quotas are available by contract.

candidates.name: Wokwi CI GitHub Action (wokwi/wokwi-ci-action)
candidates.license: MIT (Copyright 2023 CodeMagic LTD). The simulation runs on the proprietary Wokwi cloud engine.
candidates.latest_version: v1.2.0 (2024-11-13). The v1 tag moves, and each run downloads the latest wokwi-cli-linuxstatic-x64.
candidates.summary: Composite GitHub Action that installs wokwi-cli and runs one simulation from wokwi.toml. Inputs: token, path, timeout (default 10000 ms), expect_text, fail_text, scenario, diagram_file, elf and serial_log_file.

capabilities.detail: The wrapper is MIT; the simulation runs on the closed Wokwi service.
Engine support is the same as in the wokwi.com entry.
Works with any firmware, and Wokwi's PlatformIO/Arduino example uses it.
Reads a wokwi.toml pointing at the .pio/build outputs; the example repo builds with PlatformIO in the same workflow.
No input for it, and the step blocks while the simulation runs. For host-in-the-loop tests in CI, call wokwi-cli (RFC2217) or the Python client directly.
Set through the diagram attribute; engine limits are the same.
The engine simulates LEDC, but the action has no --vcd-file input; run wokwi-cli directly to export a VCD.
Through the scenario input (set-control).
Custom chips from wokwi.toml work, but their .chip.wasm files must be built in an earlier step.
Engine fidelity is the same as in the wokwi.com entry.
GitHub Actions only. Needs a WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN secret, and runs count against the monthly quota.
The composite steps use bash, wget into /usr/local/bin and the Linux static binary, so it needs a Linux runner. On Windows, use wokwi-cli directly.
Simulation only.

candidates.fit: Handy later for regression runs on every push, as one step after `pio run`. It adds nothing that plain wokwi-cli lacks and has fewer options (no VCD, no RFC2217). Not needed for local work on Windows.
caveats: The CLI version is not pinned, so behaviour can change between runs.
The default timeout is 10 s of simulated time.
Linux runners only.
candidates.cost_notes: The action is free; simulated minutes are charged to the token owner's Wokwi plan (50, 200 or 2000 per month).

candidates.name: Wokwi CI Server (self-hosted Docker image wokwi/wokwi-ci-server plus wokwi-ci-server-action)
candidates.license: Proprietary or undocumented. The Docker image has no description or license, and the action repo has no LICENSE file.
candidates.latest_version: Docker tag 20260927 (2026-09-27), with new tags every few days and about 198k pulls. The action's v1 tag was updated 2026-02-05.
candidates.summary: Runs the Wokwi simulation server in a container on the CI runner. The action runs `docker run -p 9177:3000 -e GITHUB_ACTIONS=1` and sets WOKWI_CLI_SERVER=ws://localhost:9177, so wokwi-cli and wokwi-client talk to the container instead of the cloud. Wokwi's esp32-test-binaries nightly tests and Espressif's arduino-esp32 Wokwi jobs both use it.

capabilities.detail: No source or license; it is the closed engine in a container.
Wokwi's nightly ESP32-S3 tests and Espressif's S3 Wokwi jobs run against it.
arduino-esp32's Wokwi test job, which covers Arduino 3.x, uses wokwi-ci-server-action.
Consumes whatever firmware and ELF the clients upload from wokwi.toml.
The CLI's RFC2217 bridge and the Python client's serial API are client-side, so they work with any server set in WOKWI_CLI_SERVER.
Wokwi's nightly S3 USB-Serial-JTAG test runs through it; Arduino HWCDC is not verified.
Same engine, but whether the self-hosted server has every cloud feature (for example sim:read-vcd for VCD export) is not documented. The CLI prints a warning when a server lacks the 'gdb' feature.
control:set works: arduino-esp32's Wokwi gpio test presses a button through this setup.
arduino-esp32's i2c_master test (built-in DS1307) runs through it; custom chips are uploaded by the clients.
Wokwi's nightly S3 task_wdt test runs through it; otherwise the engine caveats apply.
Built for GitHub Actions (it sets GITHUB_ACTIONS=1). Both known users still pass a WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN. Nothing is published about use outside GitHub, quota accounting or plan requirements.
Only a linux/amd64 image is published. Running it on Windows would need Docker Desktop with WSL2, which is not documented.
Simulation only.

candidates.fit: It would remove the cloud round trip and the firmware upload, which matters for timing-sensitive host-in-the-loop tests, and Wokwi and Espressif already use it in CI. But it is undocumented, closed, Linux-only and its terms are unknown. Ask Wokwi first; their docs say on-premise Wokwi CI is available on request.
caveats: No public documentation or terms.
It may lag behind or differ from the cloud feature set.
Needs Docker with amd64 Linux containers.
candidates.cost_notes: Unknown. The docs only say that on-premise deployment of Wokwi CI is available on request.

candidates.name: Wokwi Python Client (wokwi-client)
candidates.license: MIT for the client. It drives the proprietary Wokwi Simulation API.
candidates.summary: Typed Python SDK with an async WokwiClient and a blocking WokwiClientSync. It uploads the diagram, firmware, ELF and chips, then starts, pauses, resumes for N ns, waits until a given simulated time and restarts the simulation. It also streams serial bytes and writes serial, provides set_control, read_pin, listen_pin (pin:change events stamped in simulated ns) and gpio_list, reads or saves VCD, and captures the framebuffer. The server can be changed with WOKWI_CLI_SERVER.

capabilities.detail: The SDK is MIT; the engine is closed and remote.
Same engine as wokwi.com.
Works with any firmware. It is the transport inside pytest-embedded-wokwi, which runs Espressif's Arduino 3.x Wokwi tests.

Upload .pio/build/esp32s3/firmware.bin and the ELF with upload_file, then call start_simulation(firmware=..., elf=...). upload_idf_firmware handles flasher_args.json. There is no PlatformIO auto-detection.

serial_write(bytes) and the serial_monitor callback carry raw bytes in-process, with no TCP. A thin adapter with read, write and in_waiting can give SerialVehicleIO a pyserial-like object. The CLI's RFC2217 bridge is the alternative.
Uses the engine's serialInterface attribute; Arduino HWCDC is unverified.

read_vcd and save_vcd were added in 0.3.0 (2026-01-26). listen_pin emits pin:change events whose messages carry a simulated 'nanos' timestamp, enough to compute ESC and servo pulse widths without a VCD. read_pin returns the current level.
set_control(part, control, value) drives pushbuttons and custom-chip controls. arduino-esp32's S3 gpio test uses exactly this call.
start_simulation(chips=[...]) loads uploaded custom chips (.chip.json plus binary); built-in parts come from the diagram.

Engine fidelity is unchanged. What the client adds is deterministic time control (pause, resume with pause_after in ns, wait_until_simulation_time, restart_simulation), so tests can lock-step the host protocol to simulated time and avoid wall-clock drift.
Built for pytest-style scripts. Needs WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN and uses the same simulated-time quota as the CLI; runs in the cloud by default.
Pure-Python package (Python 3.9 or later). The pytest plugin built on it documents Windows PowerShell setup. Not run here.
Simulation-only API. Sharing tests with a real board needs your own abstraction, such as a pyserial-like adapter, or pytest-embedded.

candidates.fit: The best match for autopark's Python test stack. A pytest fixture can upload the PlatformIO outputs, start paused and advance simulated time in 10 ms steps. Between steps it exchanges raw COBS bytes, toggles the E-stop and timestamps ESC edges, which makes the 20 Hz telemetry and 100 ms guard logic deterministic. With a small pyserial-like adapter, SerialVehicleIO can run unchanged.
caveats: The API is pre-1.0, and pin:change events arrive through the transport's event mechanism with no high-level iterator.
Token and cloud quota work as for the CLI.
It does not ship a pyserial adapter.
candidates.cost_notes: The library is free; simulated minutes are billed to your Wokwi plan (Free 50, Hobby 200, Pro 2000 per month).

candidates.name: pytest-embedded-wokwi (Espressif pytest-embedded plugin)
candidates.license: MIT (Espressif). Depends on wokwi-client and the proprietary Wokwi service.
candidates.latest_version: 2.9.3 (2026-08-31, PyPI); requires wokwi-client>=0.4.0
candidates.summary: pytest-embedded service used as '--embedded-services arduino,wokwi' or 'idf,wokwi'. It runs ordinary Dut.expect/Dut.write tests on Wokwi and exposes wokwi.client (set_control, read_pin, serial_write). It can generate or load diagram.json and uploads custom chips from wokwi.toml or a chips/ folder. '--wokwi-usb-serial-jtag true' switches the board to USB-Serial-JTAG. Espressif's arduino-esp32 CI uses it.

capabilities.detail: The plugin is MIT; the engine is closed.
Target esp32s3 maps to board-esp32-s3-devkitc-1. arduino-esp32's Wokwi ESP32-S3 column is all green in the 2026-09-29 report.
The Arduino 3.x validation suite runs through it, including gpio, timer, ticker, uart, i2c_master, spi, nvs, psram and wifi.

ArduinoApp expects arduino-cli output: <sketch>.ino.bin or .ino.merged.bin, <sketch>.ino.elf, build.options.json (with the fqbn) and flash_args. PlatformIO outputs need a small shim that renames them and writes those two files.

Dut.expect*/write run over the simulated serial, alongside wokwi.client.serial_write. The Dut is pexpect-based and text-oriented, so the binary COBS protocol needs raw-byte regexes or direct client calls.
--wokwi-usb-serial-jtag sets serialInterface=USB_SERIAL_JTAG and removes the $serialMonitor wires. arduino-esp32 turns it on only for local ESP32-P4 runs and forces UART0 in CI (PR #12875).
Available through wokwi.client (read_vcd, listen_pin). arduino-esp32's own adc_pwm test is disabled on Wokwi because SigmaDelta is not simulated, not because of LEDC.
wokwi.client.set_control('btn1','pressed',1). arduino-esp32's S3 gpio test checks INPUT_PULLUP reads and interrupts this way.
Uploads custom chips from wokwi.toml [[chip]] entries or from chips/*.chip.json plus .wasm. The i2c_master test uses the built-in DS1307.
Engine fidelity applies. The Ticker (esp_timer) test passes 19/19 and the timer test 8/8 on Wokwi S3; panic and reset behaviour are undocumented.
Standard pytest. arduino-esp32 runs it in GitHub Actions with wokwi-ci-server and a WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN.
The README shows Windows PowerShell setup for the token, and pytest-embedded's log reader has a non-POSIX path. Not run here.

The same pytest files run on real boards through pytest-embedded-serial-esp (the 'esp,arduino' services: esptool flashing plus serial). arduino-esp32 publishes Hardware and Wokwi results for the same tests. Wokwi-only calls such as set_control and read_pin need hardware equivalents or skips.

candidates.fit: The most direct route to one test suite shared by the simulator and the board, and Espressif already does this on ESP32-S3. For autopark it needs a shim that presents the PlatformIO outputs as an arduino-cli build, and extra care with the binary protocol in the expect-based Dut. Worth adopting once the board arrives and you want hardware-in-the-loop runs of the same tests.
caveats: Not PlatformIO-native.
Binary-protocol tests need raw-byte handling.
Token and quota work as for the CLI.
Espressif's Arduino docs say Wokwi is not maintained by the Arduino core team (https://docs.espressif.com/projects/arduino-esp32/en/latest/third_party/wokwi.html).
candidates.cost_notes: The plugin is free. Wokwi minutes are billed per your plan; hardware runs need only the board.

candidates.name: Wokwi Custom Chips API (C/WebAssembly, experimental Verilog)
candidates.license: Chip code is yours. Wokwi's template (inverter-chip) is MIT, and wokwi-api.h is published without a license notice. Chips run inside the proprietary engine, and the API is in beta.
candidates.latest_version: Chips API beta (API version 1 in wokwi-api.h). `wokwi-cli chip compile` exists since v0.20.0 (2026-01-13), and VS Code 3.6.1 (2026-08-26) fixed chip loading and reloading.
candidates.summary: Write your own simulated parts in C or any language that compiles to WASM; Verilog is experimental. The APIs cover GPIO with pin_watch edge callbacks, ns timers and get_sim_nanos, an I2C device, an SPI device (manual CS), UART, analog in/out, attributes with range controls, a framebuffer and printf logging. Chips are loaded through [[chip]] entries in wokwi.toml and placed in diagram.json as chip-<name>.

capabilities.detail: The template is MIT, but the runtime is closed.
Chips are parts that do not depend on the MCU, so they work in ESP32-S3 diagrams.
Chips do not depend on the firmware framework.
Declared in the same wokwi.toml as the .pio firmware. Compile with `wokwi-cli chip compile`, with Docker (wokwi/builder-clang-wasm) or with the template's GitHub Action.
The API has no networking; it covers pins, timers, I2C, SPI, UART, analog, attributes and framebuffer only. Chips can only log: printf goes to the Chips Console, or to [chip] lines in the CLI.
No USB API. An untested idea: a chip using uart_init on the UART0 TX pin (GPIO43) could relay boot and panic text to the chip log while the serial monitor is on USB-Serial-JTAG.

pin_watch(BOTH) plus get_sim_nanos() gives edge timing to the nanosecond. An RC-ESC or servo input model can check 1000–2000 µs pulses at 50 Hz, react to neutral or loss of signal, and print results for expect-chip-output. Community PWM and oscilloscope chips exist.

A chip can drive pins (OUTPUT_LOW or OUTPUT_HIGH) or float them (INPUT) to model an E-stop wire break. Its range controls can be driven by set-control; Wokwi's ESP32-C6 example sets the 'lux' control of chip-bh1750 from a scenario.

The I2C device API (7-bit address with connect, read, write and disconnect callbacks), the SPI device API and analog output are enough to model sensors. A community AS5600 chip project exists on wokwi.com. VL53L1X, BNO085 (SHTP/SH-2 over I2C with an INT pin) and MT6701 would have to be written. The analog reference is fixed at 5 V for every MCU, which skews ADC voltage-sensing scale.
Does not apply to MCU internals. A chip can, however, timestamp what the ESC pin does before and after a panic or esp_restart, for example how long LEDC pulses continue.

Chips build headlessly (the CLI fetches WASI-SDK, and there is a GitHub Action template). Their controls are driven by set-control or the Python client, and their output can be asserted with expect-chip-output (CLI v0.20.0+).
`wokwi-cli chip compile` downloads the x86_64-windows WASI-SDK and uses clang.exe.
Simulation models only.

candidates.fit: This is how to model the parts Wokwi lacks. Build them in this order: an ESC input monitor that doubles as a simple plant, then a wheel encoder (quadrature or MT6701 ABZ output) driven by the ESC command for the PCNT/encoder code, then an AS5600 register model. VL53L1X and especially BNO085 are large modelling jobs; their drivers are better tested against recorded data on the PC or on the real sensor. The API is beta, so keep chips small and versioned in the repo.
caveats: The API is beta, and init functions (pin_init, timer_init, i2c_init and so on) may only be called from chip_init.
The 5 V analog reference makes ADC tests unrealistic without compensation.
You maintain the sensor models, and their fidelity is only as good as you make it.
candidates.cost_notes: Free to write and use in any Wokwi front end: the web free tier needs no license, VS Code needs a license, and CLI runs use your minutes.

candidates.summary: Runs the Wokwi simulator in a JetBrains IDE window. It reuses the VS Code extension's wokwi.toml configuration, restarts the simulation on rebuild and supports debugging in CLion. Its README roadmap still lists a writable console and serial port forwarding as not done.

capabilities.detail: The plugin source is MIT; the engine is closed.
'Supports the same platforms' as the VS Code extension, since it uses the same engine.
Same engine, so it works with any firmware.
It uses VS Code-style wokwi.toml, so it can point at the .pio outputs; PlatformIO is not specifically documented.
The README roadmap has 'Make Console writable' and 'Add Serial Port forwarding' still unchecked.
The engine attribute works in diagrams, but the console is read-only.
The engine simulates LEDC, but VCD export is not documented for the plugin.
Interactive clicks only.
Custom chip support was added in 0.11.0; built-in parts are available.
Engine caveats apply; debugging works in CLion.
IDE only.
The plugin docs do not say.
Simulation only.

candidates.fit: Not a fit. With no serial forwarding and a read-only console, the COBS link cannot be exercised. It needs the same Wokwi license, and the project uses VS Code with PlatformIO anyway. Listed for completeness.
caveats: Community-maintained, so features lag behind the official VS Code extension.

report.notes:
Scope: every Wokwi piece that matters for running the unmodified PlatformIO ESP32-S3 firmware without the board. Checked on 2026-09-29 against the primary sources cited per aspect. Nothing was run on Wokwi and no token was used.

Main conclusions for autopark:

(1) Coverage. In this area, only Wokwi runs the compiled ESP32-S3 Arduino firmware with all of the following together: LEDC, GPIO input, esp_timer, TWDT, a host serial link and test automation. Espressif's arduino-esp32 3.x suite passes on Wokwi ESP32-S3 (report generated 2026-09-29: https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/blob/gh-pages/runtime-test-results/RUNTIME_TEST_RESULTS.md).

(2) Licensing by piece.
- Closed: the simulation engine, wokwi.com, the VS Code extension and the wokwi/wokwi-ci-server Docker image.
- Open: wokwi-cli, including @wokwi/client and @wokwi/rfc2217 (MIT per LICENSE; the package.json fields say ISC); wokwi-ci-action (MIT); wokwi-python-client (MIT); wokwi-docs (MIT); the inverter-chip template (MIT); pytest-embedded-wokwi (MIT, Espressif); the IntelliJ plugin (MIT, community); idf-wokwi (Apache-2.0).

(3) Cost.
- A free account gets a token and 50 simulated minutes per month for the CLI, CI and Python clients.
- The VS Code extension is free only for projects that are public on GitHub, OSI-licensed and non-commercial.
- github.com/thbn12082/autopark returns 404 to anonymous requests, and the repo root has no LICENSE file. VS Code would therefore need Hobby+ (€8.1/mo, annual billing) or an opened repo. The CLI and Python route stays within the free tier.

(4) Biggest unknowns to smoke-test first:
- Arduino HWCDC over Wokwi's USB-Serial-JTAG on S3. HWCDC only transmits while it sees USB SOF interrupts, and Espressif uses HWCDC on Wokwi only for local ESP32-P4 runs, with UART0 in CI. Fallback: a sim-only env with -DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=0 and $serialMonitor wired to UART0.
- Panic handling, esp_restart, esp_reset_reason() and LEDC state across a CPU-only reset are all undocumented.
- The default ~8 MHz CPU cap; set 'cpuFrequency' to '240' for more realistic timing.
- Drift between simulated and wall-clock time, plus cloud latency, for the 10 ms / 20 Hz link. Prefer lock-stepping with wokwi-client pause/resume.

(5) Suggested first experiment:
1. Build the PWM-enabled variant with dummy pins.
2. Write wokwi.toml with firmware/elf = .pio/build/esp32s3/firmware.bin and .elf, and rfc2217ServerPort = 4000.
3. In diagram.json: board-esp32-s3-devkitc-1 with attrs flashSize '8' and serialInterface 'USB_SERIAL_JTAG'; a logic analyzer and a wokwi-servo on the ESC/servo pins; a pushbutton with bounce '0' from the E-stop pin to GND.
4. Run `wokwi-cli . --timeout 0` (or VS Code) and pass serial.serial_for_url('rfc2217://localhost:4000') to SerialVehicleIO.
5. Export a VCD and check 1000–2000 µs pulses and the neutral output after E-stop, a loop stall and a panic.
6. Later, move to pytest with wokwi-client and custom chips: an ESC monitor, an encoder and an AS5600.
Real-board checks stay mandatory for electrical timing, panic-hook latency and HWCDC.

Checked but not listed as candidates:
- idf-wokwi 1.1.0 (2026-02-19, Apache-2.0): adds `idf.py wokwi`, requires ESP-IDF 6.0 or later, so it does not apply to PlatformIO/Arduino.
- Wokwi MCP server: `wokwi-cli mcp`, experimental, same token.
- MabezDev/wokwi-server: archived, last release v0.2.0 on 2022-10-17.
- wokwi/flasher-esp32: archived esptool-js fork.

Method: the GitHub REST API was rate-limited, so the facts come from:
- the wokwi-docs source files;
- shallow git clones of wokwi-cli, wokwi-python-client, esp32-test-binaries and pytest-embedded, plus a sparse checkout of arduino-esp32;
- GitHub release Atom feeds;
- the PyPI, Docker Hub, VS Marketplace, Open VSX and JetBrains Marketplace APIs.

Side note: the claude.ai connectors for Asana, Atlassian, Datadog, GitHub, Linear, Notion, PagerDuty, Slack, ClickUp and Monday are still waiting for authorization. They were not needed for this research. To enable them, authorize them in claude.ai connector settings or through /mcp.

verification.topic: Adversarial fact-check of the 'Wokwi ecosystem' report (engine, VS Code, CLI/CI action, self-hosted CI server, Python client, pytest-embedded-wokwi, custom chips, IntelliJ) for the autopark ESP32-S3 Arduino 2.0.17 / PlatformIO firmware. Checked 2026-09-29 against Wokwi docs source (wokwi-docs @96fec01, 2026-09-16), wokwi-cli @v0.27.1, wokwi-client 0.4.0 wheel, pytest-embedded @2633b01, esp32-test-binaries @7ccaa66, arduino-esp32 2.0.17/master, PyPI, Docker Hub, Open VSX/VS Marketplace APIs, wokwi.com pricing/terms. I also ran one local test of the real @wokwi/rfc2217 server code against pyserial 3.5.

checks.claim: S3 simulates cores, GPIO+interrupts, IOMUX, PSRAM, UART, USB CDC, USB Serial+JTAG (serial only), I2C master (no 10-bit), SPI, LEDC, PCNT, DMA, WiFi, timers, watchdog, ADC, RNG, AES/SHA/RSA; partial RTC/TWAI/RMT-TX; no I2S/MCPWM/BT/ULP; boards ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 and XIAO ESP32-S3; flashSize 2-32 MB, default 4
cpuFrequency default 'auto' caps the CPU at about 8 MHz; peripheral timing is unaffected; can be set to a MHz value or 'max'
checks.correction: Wokwi's own S3 nightly tests override it per test (gptimer 16, uart 20, spi_master 100, usb_serial_jtag 16 MHz), which shows timing-sensitive code needs a raised cap: https://github.com/wokwi/esp32-test-binaries/tree/main/test

checks.claim: Panic/abort handling, esp_restart, esp_reset_reason() and LEDC across a CPU-only reset are undocumented
checks.correction: Also untested publicly. The nightly hello_world test only waits 2 s for 'Restarting in 9 seconds...', so it never exercises esp_restart.

checks.claim: Wokwi nightly runs ESP-IDF's [task_wdt] Unity group on esp32s3; TWDT/tickless-idle bug #1075 is closed
Attribute serialInterface='USB_SERIAL_JTAG' routes the serial monitor to USB-Serial-JTAG (serial works, JTAG not); $serialMonitor wires must be removed
Wokwi's nightly tests run ESP-IDF's usb_serial_jtag test app on esp32s3 with this attribute
checks.correction: The S3 diagram also sets cpuFrequency '16'. The app has only 3 test cases (print from several tasks, fsync, ROM printf after driver install), and none calls usb_serial_jtag_is_connected(), the SOF monitor. Passing it does not show that HWCDC's connection detection works.

checks.claim: In Arduino 2.0.17, HWCDC only transmits while its FreeRTOS tick hook keeps seeing the USB SOF interrupt bit
checks.correction: Precisely: at boot it assumes a connection; it declares 'unplugged' after about 5 ticks with no sof_int_raw. From then on write()/cdc0_write_char only push into the TX ring buffer (oldest bytes dropped) and nothing reaches the FIFO.

checks.claim: PR #12875 (merged 2026-09-15): arduino-esp32 uses HWCDC on Wokwi only for local ESP32-P4 runs and forces UART0 in CI
checks.correction: This is misleading as a negative signal. The diff's own comment says 'CI hardware runners talk to UART0, so CDC on boot must be Disabled ... Local and Wokwi use USB Serial/JTAG, so Enabled (CDCOnBoot=cdc)'. UART0 in CI comes from the hardware runners, not from a Wokwi limit. Espressif treats HWCDC-over-Wokwi (P4, core 3.3.x) as a working local setup, which is indirect evidence that Wokwi's USJ model satisfies the SOF check. S3 with 2.0.17 is still untested.

checks.claim: Only one serial stream can be exposed (issue #732 open)
USB OTG CDC (TinyUSB) is also available for S3
checks.source: https://docs.wokwi.com/guides/esp32 (row 'USB: Support for UART over USB (CDC)') ; https://github.com/wokwi/wokwi-cli/blob/v0.27.1/packages/cli/src/project/boards.ts (S3 offers uart/usb/usb-serialjtag) ; https://github.com/wokwi/esp32-test-binaries/blob/main/test/test_usb_otg.py
