candidates.name: sigrok (sigrok-cli + libsigrokdecode pwm/timing decoders) with fx2lafw FX2 logic analyzers
candidates.license: libsigrok, sigrok-cli and libsigrokdecode: GPL-3.0-or-later. The pwm and timing decoders: GPL-2.0-or-later. fx2lafw firmware: GPL-2.0-or-later.
candidates.latest_version: Last formal releases: sigrok-cli 0.7.2 (tag 2021-03-01), libsigrok 0.5.2 (2019-12-25), libsigrokdecode 0.5.3 (2019-12-11), PulseView 0.4.2 (2020-03-31), fx2lafw 0.1.7. Nightly Windows installers are published on sigrok.org. libsigrok master's last commit is 2025-11-20.
candidates.summary: Command-line capture and protocol decoding. Cheap 24 MHz 8-channel FX2 'Saleae clone' analyzers run the open fx2lafw firmware. `-P pwm:data=D0` annotates duty cycle and period. `-P timing:data=D0:edge=any:format=terse-us` prints the time between edges, which gives the servo/ESC pulse width directly. sigrok can also read VCD files, so the same decoder works on Wokwi logic-analyzer exports.

capabilities.detail: GPL-3.0-or-later and GPL-2.0-or-later.
It measures real signals; it does not run firmware.
Not applicable: independent of the firmware framework.
No integration.
It has a UART decoder but does not provide a host serial link.
Not applicable.

The pwm decoder gives duty cycle and period; the timing decoder gives µs between edges. 1000–2000 µs pulses at 50 Hz are easily resolved at 1–4 MS/s. FX2 analyzers reach 24 MS/s on up to 8 channels, close to the USB 2.0 limit. The VCD input (with a downsample option) decodes Wokwi captures the same way.
FX2 logic analyzers are input-only.
It cannot simulate sensors. It can decode real I2C/SPI traffic to check sensor transactions.

It is the measurement tool for the real-silicon questions: time from panic to ESC pin low, whether LEDC keeps pulsing after a CPU-only reset, and the output-guard reaction time. This needs triggers plus a way to provoke the event.
Scriptable CLI (--time/--samples, -P, -A, --protocol-decoder-samplenum). No account needed. labgrid wraps it (SigrokDriver). Real hardware must be connected.

Release 0.7.2 and nightly Windows installers exist for sigrok-cli and PulseView. FX2 devices need the WinUSB driver installed with Zadig, and sigrok warns about the poor-quality USB cables often bundled with them.
This is its purpose.

candidates.fit: This is the measurement half of the later hardware plan. candidates.cost_notes: Software is free. FX2 clone analyzers are a few USD to around 15 USD; no licence is needed.
caveats: The formal releases are old (2019–2021); use nightlies for current decoders.
Decoding a 1 GHz Wokwi VCD needs the sigrok VCD input's downsample option.

report.notes:
CONCLUSION: For this project, pytest with pytest-embedded 2.9.3 is the harness that lets one test suite run on the simulator now and on the real board later.
- Now: Wokwi (arduino,wokwi services; --wokwi-usb-serial-jtag true; custom diagram with the E-stop switch and a logic analyzer). It needs WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN; the free plan gives 50 CI minutes/month.
- Also now: QEMU (qemu service). It only works for a separate build with UART0 console and DIO flash mode, so it is limited to protocol and timing logic.
- Later: the real board, either `esp,arduino --port COMx` plus a PlatformIO-to-Arduino-layout shim, or `pio run -t upload` followed by the serial service.
- Hardware-dependent steps go behind a thin project fixture layer, with per-platform markers the way arduino-esp32 uses ci.yml:
  - transport: dut.serial.proc (inside disable_redirect_thread) for SerialVehicleIO, or an adapter over wokwi.client for Wokwi;
  - estop: wokwi.client.set_control, or a relay/GPIO adapter on hardware;
  - pwm_probe: Wokwi save_vcd or an FX2 capture, both decoded by the same sigrok-cli pwm/timing step.
- PlatformIO `pio test` complements this for Unity on-target tests: it ran in QEMU on Windows, and the same sources run on the board with `pio test -e esp32s3`.
- labgrid, OpenHTF, Robot Framework, tbot and HardPy are hardware-only (labgrid and tbot are POSIX-only) and add nothing for simulation.

VERIFIED on this Windows 11 PC, 2026-09-29, with Python 3.12.10, pytest-embedded 2.9.3, Espressif QEMU 9.2.2 (esp_develop_9.2.2_20260417) and PlatformIO 6.2.0. All files are under %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\d--xetulai\<phiên>\scratchpad\hilx\.
(1) pio2arduino_layout.py turns .pio/build/esp32s3 into the layout ArduinoApp accepts (target esp32s3, 4 flash files, merged 8 MB image in shim_out\).
(2) qtest\test_boot.py: the qemu service booted that image (ROM banner, then QMP reset) and passed.
(3) qtest\test_capture.py: the unmodified project build asserts in esp_flash_init_default_chip (ESP-IDF v4.4 startup.c:328) and boot-loops with rst:0xc. App output on USB-CDC is invisible under QEMU.
(4) qtest\run_socket.py: the serial service over socket:// to QEMU passed. dut.serial.proc is a pyserial socket object. The expect path ran at about 20 B/s because pyserial's socket in_waiting returns at most 1.
(5) pio_q\ (platformio.ini with test_testing_command pointing at QEMU, merge_for_qemu.py, test\test_harness\test_main.cpp):
- `pio test --without-uploading` gave 3/3 PASS in 8.4 s and wrote junit.xml.
- Without DIO flash mode the run hung (killed after 100 s; no timeout option).
- The same image run through pytest-embedded's qemu service with expect_unity_test_output passed 4 out of 4 runs, with per-case JUnit (qtest\test_unity_from_pio.py).
- Intermittent QEMU stalls right after the bootloader: 5 of 24 boots, on a host loaded by other agents.
(6) The arduino+wokwi services load on Windows and stop at the missing token. The Wokwi path itself was NOT run.

NOT VERIFIED: Wokwi HWCDC (USB_SERIAL_JTAG) with Arduino 2.0.17; whether Wokwi faithfully simulates the panic-hook GPIO register writes and LEDC after a CPU reset (only real hardware plus a logic analyzer can answer that); pio test on a real ESP32-S3 over USB-CDC; sigrok decoding of a Wokwi VCD.

OUT OF SCOPE here, covered by other areas: Wokwi CLI scenario runner, Wokwi VS Code RFC2217 server (would allow `--port rfc2217://localhost:4000` from pytest-embedded; wokwi-cli support is undocumented), QEMU/Renode peripheral fidelity. Zephyr Twister does span QEMU and hardware but only for Zephyr apps. Saleae Logic 2 automation needs proprietary software.

checks.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/master/.github/scripts/tests_build.sh ('--arduino-cli  Use arduino-cli for compilation instead of arduino_cmake.py') ; .../.github/scripts/sketch_utils.sh (L410-431) ; .../.github/workflows/tests_build.yml (calls tests_build.sh without --arduino-cli)

The output layout ($HOME/.arduino/tests/<target>/<sketch>/build.tmp with merged.bin and flash_args) is as described. The conclusion (reimplement a small Python runner for PlatformIO on Windows) still holds.

checks.claim: PlatformIO Core 6.2.0 (2026-09-05) fixed Unit Testing failing on Windows because of Serial.end(), and the test-suite status being hard-coded as PASSED.

test_testing_command has documented simulator examples (QEMU, Renode, simavr) used with --without-uploading. There is no timeout option for the testing stage. GoogleTest runs on-target only on espressif8266/32; doctest is native-only. The Unity docs advise delay(2000).
checks.correction: Note: PlatformIO's QEMU example is a SiFive HiFive1 (RISC-V) board, not an ESP32.

checks.claim: The test_port reader uses serial_for_url. The native runner uses the Proactor event loop on Windows. PIO Remote needs a free PlatformIO account.
26.0 was released 2026-06-06. License is LGPL-2.1. The maintainer (2023-03-01) said labgrid expects POSIX and recommended WSL.
There is no ESP32/esptool driver. QEMUDriver uses if=pflash and a serial link over a UNIX socket. FlashScriptDriver is documented as a 'last resort'. SigrokDriver has capture() and analyze().

PyPI 1.6.1 (2025-03-05). master pyproject says 1.6.2; last commit 2026-09-09. Apache-2.0. SerialCollectionPlug uses serial.Serial with readline().decode(). CI runs on ubuntu; user_input has a Windows code path.

RF 7.5 (2026-09-14). SerialLibrary 0.4.3 (2022-06-02), last commit 2022-05-16. The LICENSE file is BSD-3-Clause while PyPI metadata says Apache-2.0. Add Port uses serial_for_url. RF describes itself as 'operating system and application independent'.
v0.10.10 (2025-11-25), GPL-3.0. The PyPI name 'tbot' is an unrelated package from 2012. The subprocess channel imports pty, termios and fcntl.
0.25.2 (PyPI, 2026-06-09), GPL-3.0-or-later. storage_type can be json or couchdb. The changelog has a Windows StandCloud authorization fix.

sigrok-cli 0.7.2 (2021-03-01), libsigrok 0.5.2 (2019-12-25), libsigrokdecode 0.5.3 (2019-12-11), PulseView 0.4.2 (2020-03-31), fx2lafw 0.1.7. libsigrok master's last commit is 2025-11-20. Licenses: libsigrok GPL-3, the pwm and timing decoders GPL-2.0-or-later, fx2lafw GPL-2. Nightly Windows installers are on sigrok.org.
checks.correction: Extra dates: the fx2lafw 0.1.7 tag is 2019-11-14; libsigrokdecode master's last commit is 2024-10-01.

checks.claim: The timing decoder has format=terse-us and edge=any. The VCD input has a downsample option, usable to decode Wokwi 1 GHz captures.
checks.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigrokproject/libsigrokdecode/master/decoders/timing/pd.py ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigrokproject/libsigrok/master/src/input/vcd.c ; https://docs.wokwi.com/guides/logic-analyzer (recommends a downsample factor of 50 for PulseView)

checks.claim: esp-develop-9.2.2-20260417 (published 2026-04-19) is the latest release. It added SDMMC for ESP32-S3. The official docs were last changed 2025-08-29 / 2025-09-11 and still list SD/MMC as unsupported on S3. QEMU is GPL-2.0.
Not emulated on ESP32-S3: LEDC, GPIO matrix/IOMUX, I2C, GP SPI, RMT, USB. Emulated: UART, timer groups, SysTimer, RNG, eFuse, flash, crypto, GDMA, TWAI, OpenCores Ethernet, RGB framebuffer.
Espressif's Wokwi page warns: 'Simulation results may differ from real hardware.'

missed_facts.candidate: Espressif QEMU / pytest-embedded qemu / PlatformIO QEMU env
missed_facts.fact: Watchdog tests cannot be done on the ESP32-S3 QEMU machine. The timer-group model applies stage settings only when CONF_UPDATE_EN is written, and ESP-IDF's S3 HAL never writes it, so the TWDT and IWDT never fire. The docs say the RTC WDT is not emulated at all. Yet the docs claim 'Timer Group watchdog timers are emulated', which is misleading for S3. The project's TWDT timeout test, and any 'hung loop() causes a reset' test, need Wokwi or real hardware.

Wokwi's ESP32-S3 support table covers more than the report credits. Simulated: Watchdog, Timers, PCNT (quadrature encoder), ADC (voltage sensing), GPIO with interrupts, IOMUX, LEDC, SPI, I2C (master only, no 10-bit addressing), DMA, RNG, and USB Serial/JTAG (serial only). Partial: RMT (TX only), TWAI, and RTC (only pull-up/pull-down). Not simulated: MCPWM. Because RTC is partial, esp_reset_reason()-based behaviour may be unfaithful on Wokwi; arduino-esp32 excludes its reset-reason/TWDT test from Wokwi for that reason. In the hands-on QEMU run, reset reasons came out correctly (POWER_ON, PANIC, SOFTWARE).

Wokwi's default flashSize is '4' (4 MB). An Arduino 2.0.17 image with an 8 MB header would then fail IDF 4.4's size check: 'Detected size smaller than the size in the binary image header' returns ESP_ERR_FLASH_SIZE_NOT_MATCH, which hits the same startup.c:328 assert. The diagram's board part must set "flashSize": "8". pytest-embedded passes flash_size only on the IDF path (added in 2.7.0). The Arduino path uploads the bare .ino(.merged).bin without it.

Wokwi publishes a conformance suite, wokwi/esp32-test-binaries. It runs ESP-IDF test apps under wokwi-cli, including usb_serial_jtag on ESP32-S3 with serialInterface USB_SERIAL_JTAG and host-to-device writes, task_wdt, pcnt, gpio, gptimer and uart. The 'Test in Wokwi' workflow passed on 2026-09-28 (run 1065). These are the best public evidence for S3 USB-Serial-JTAG and TWDT fidelity, though they are built with IDF 'latest', not 4.4.

Wokwi's Terms of Service (last updated 2026-04-14) say: 'You may use the Service for your personal non-commercial purposes only.' Using it at no cost for commercial purposes without explicit consent is not allowed. The pricing page labels Community as 'For open source projects' and Pro as 'For commercial projects'. The Wokwi for VS Code extension, needed for the RFC2217 route, is free only for open-source projects on a renewable 30-day license; Hobby+ includes it. The 50-minute free CI tier is therefore only valid for personal or non-commercial use.

None of the planned sensors (AS5600, MT6701, BNO085, VL53L1X) is a built-in Wokwi part; they would need custom chips (Chips API/WASM, which pytest-embedded uploads since 2.8.0). Useful built-in stand-ins: KY-040 rotary encoder (quadrature, for PCNT), slide switch or pushbutton (E-stop), potentiometer (ADC voltage), micro servo, MPU6050 (I2C IMU), and the 8-channel logic analyzer.

QEMU writes flash changes (NVS, core dumps) back to the -drive image file. The hands-on run found a core dump at 0x7F0000 after an emulated panic. pytest-embedded's qemu service uses the --qemu-image-path file in place and regenerates only IDF images, so Arduino/PlatformIO tests should copy a fresh image for each run.
missed_facts.source: hands-on evidence JSON (flash image write-back check) ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/espressif/pytest-embedded/main/pytest-embedded-qemu/README.md (--skip-regenerate-image applies only to IDF auto-merge)

missed_facts.fact: wokwi-cli is MIT, latest v0.27.1 (2026-09-16), with a PowerShell installer for Windows. It runs YAML scenarios (wait-serial, write-serial, set-control, pin expectations) with a default 30 s timeout. Wokwi documents a PlatformIO flow: 'pio run' followed by 'wokwi-cli . --scenario x.yaml' (wokwi-docs PR #248, merged 2025-11-05). This is a lighter Wokwi path that needs no pytest-embedded shim, but it is text-oriented and simulation-only.

pytest-embedded 2.0.0 (2025-09-23) requires Python 3.10+ and esptool >=5.1.dev1,<6. It also removed the old wokwi-cli wrapper in favour of wokwi-python-client. This is compatible with the project's Python 3.12. The latest wokwi-client is 0.4.0 (2026-02-19).

PlatformIO 6.1.19 (2026-02-04) fixed fully-qualified serial URLs such as rfc2217://host:port being treated as wildcard patterns (issue #5225). This matters if test_port or upload_port points at a simulator's RFC2217 server.

pyserial's latest release is still 3.5 (2020-11-23). The select-based socket:// in_waiting (0 or 1) is not going to change upstream. Use rfc2217:// or a small draining adapter; the hands-on CountingPort adapter took the non-blocking loop from 2 of about 40 telemetry frames to 40 of 40.

arduino-esp32 has open history of HWCDC TX data loss on ESP32-S3. #9378 (C3/C6/S3) was fixed by PR #9401 for 3.0.0-RC1. #11959, opened 2025-10-28 against 3.x, reports missing chunks with Serial.write(). Whether 2.0.17 is affected was not established. Simulation will not reproduce this, so hardware runs of the COBS/CRC protocol should assert on frame-error counters, not only on functional results.

verification.overall:
The report holds up well. Every version and date checked out, including pytest-embedded 2.9.3 and its sub-releases, Espressif QEMU esp-develop-9.2.2-20260417, arduino-esp32 master and tags, PlatformIO 6.2.0, labgrid 26.0, OpenHTF, Robot Framework and SerialLibrary, tbot, HardPy, sigrok, and Wokwi pricing. All licenses checked out too. So did the source-level mechanisms that decide feasibility: serial_for_url, the 50 ms read_all loop, pyserial socket in_waiting being 0 or 1, the Wokwi USB-Serial-JTAG diagram override, VCD/set_control/read_pin, QMP reset, Wokwi hard reset not implemented, espemu being RISC-V only, and QEMU having no HWCDC, LEDC, GPIO or I2C on S3.

Two claims are wrong:
1. arduino-esp32 does not build its test sketches with arduino-cli by default. The default is tools/arduino_cmake.py, and arduino-cli is optional. The report's conclusion is unaffected.
2. DIO flash mode is not required to boot the unmodified QIO build in QEMU. The failure comes from the 8 MB image being given a gd25q64 flash model with no quad-enable support. Padding the image to 16 MB (is25lp128) boots it. A UART0 console is still required.

Two claims stay unclear. Whether the Arduino 2.0.17 HWCDC firmware works on Wokwi has not been verified, although Wokwi's own S3 USB-Serial-JTAG conformance test passes on current IDF. The '5 of 24 boots stalled' observation is local only.

Important gaps in the report:
- QEMU S3 watchdogs can never fire; this is source-confirmed. TWDT and 'hung loop' tests therefore need Wokwi or real hardware.
- Wokwi documents Watchdog, PCNT and ADC as simulated on S3. Its RTC is partial, so reset-reason fidelity is uncertain there.
- Wokwi defaults to 4 MB flash. An 8 MB 2.0.17 image will assert unless the diagram sets flashSize '8'.
- Wokwi's free plan is limited to personal non-commercial use under its Terms of Service.
- Real-hardware HWCDC data-loss history is worth guarding against.

The report's main recommendation stands with these caveats. Use pytest plus pytest-embedded as the single harness: Wokwi for HWCDC, E-stop, PWM and WDT scenarios; open-source QEMU only for a UART0 build testing protocol, timing, panic and reset-reason logic; and later the real board through esp,arduino or the serial service.

Separately, several MCP connectors (asana, atlassian, datadog, github, linear, notion, pagerduty, slack, clickup, monday) need authorization in claude.ai connector settings or via /mcp. None were needed for this check.

report.topic: Renode and other ESP32 / ESP32-S3 simulators and emulators (not Wokwi, not Espressif's QEMU fork). Checked 2026-09-29 against the autopark esp32_vehicle firmware: ESP32-S3, Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17, HWCDC over USB-Serial-JTAG, LEDC servo/ESC, E-stop GPIO, esp_timer guard, task WDT and panic hook.

candidates.name: Renode (Antmicro)
candidates.license: MIT (Renode framework). The CPU backend tlib is LGPL and derived from QEMU. Everything is open source.
candidates.latest_version: 1.17.0 (GitHub release 2026-09-07; CHANGELOG entry 2026-09-06). ESP32-S3 peripheral models exist only on master/nightly, since 2026-09-25.
candidates.summary: Open-source SoC/board simulator (C#/.NET plus tlib) with Robot Framework testing. Renode 1.14 (2023) added Xtensa core configurations for esp32, esp32s2 and esp32s3 ('translation support for Espressif ESP32 chips'). On 2024-11-25 a maintainer stated this 'concerns the core only, so not the SoC and peripherals… ESP32_UART… not the whole platform yet'. On 2026-09-25 (ticket #100525) Antmicro committed LX7 decode tables plus the ESP32_USBSerialJTAG, ESP32S3_EXTMEM, ESP32_TIMG, ESP32_RTC_CNTL and ESP32_SPIController models. There is still no ESP32/ESP32-S3 platform (.repl): renode master has only xtensa-sample-controller.repl, and there are no ESP32 GPIO/IO_MUX, interrupt-matrix, SYSTIMER, LEDC or I2C models.

capabilities.detail: Renode is MIT-licensed. tlib is LGPL (QEMU-derived). The whole stack is public.

No release or master branch can boot an ESP32-S3 image. Only these building blocks exist: the esp32s3 core config in tlib (2023-07-26, with LX7 decode tables added 2026-09-25) and 5 peripheral models (nightly, 2026-09-25). There is no platform description and no interrupt matrix, SYSTIMER or GPIO.
No ESP32 machine exists, so no Arduino-ESP32 image (2.0.x or 3.x) can run. No reports of Arduino on Renode ESP32 were found.

PlatformIO ships tool-renode (debug_tool = renode). Its test_testing_command example loads firmware.elf with 'sysbus LoadELF'. The documented boards are SiFive/OpenHW only; there is no espressif32 board.

The framework can expose any UART as a TCP server on every OS ('emulation CreateServerSocketTerminal <port>'), which pyserial socket:// can use. PTY terminals work on Linux/macOS only. ESP32_UART and ESP32_USBSerialJTAG are UARTBase models and could be attached this way, but there is no S3 machine to run.

ESP32_USBSerialJTAG (added 2026-09-25, nightly only) implements only EP1 RDWR_BYTE and the EP1_CONF flags; SERIAL_IN_EP_DATA_FREE is always true. INT_RAW/ST/ENA/CLR are listed but not implemented, so the interrupt-driven Arduino HWCDC is unlikely to work yet.
There is no ESP32 LEDC model. The only ESP32 files are ESP32_UART, ESP32_USBSerialJTAG, ESP32_TIMG, ESP32_RTC_CNTL, ESP32_SPIController, ESP32S3_EXTMEM and ESP32Generation.
Renode can drive GPIO from the Monitor or Robot on supported SoCs, but it has no ESP32 GPIO, IO_MUX or GPIO-matrix model.
Renode has generic I2C sensor models, but there is no ESP32 I2C controller model to attach them to.

ESP32_TIMG models only the general timers and RTC calibration, with no MWDT. ESP32_RTC_CNTL always reports the power-on reset cause. Without SYSTIMER or an interrupt matrix, the FreeRTOS tick, esp_timer, task WDT, panic and esp_restart cannot be exercised.

renode-test runs Robot Framework suites headless, supports parallel runs (-j) and RENODE_CI_MODE failure snapshots, and has UART keywords such as 'Wait For Line On Uart'. It is free and needs no account. This is framework-level only: there is nothing to run for ESP32-S3 yet.
1.17.0 ships renode-1.17.0.setup.exe and a windows-portable.zip. PTY terminals are not available on Windows; use the socket terminal.
Renode is a pure simulator. Its Robot tests target emulated machines only, with no flashing or HIL runner for real boards.

candidates.fit: Not usable for this firmware today. Renode cannot boot any ESP32-S3 image because it has no platform and no GPIO, LEDC, interrupt-matrix or SYSTIMER models, even though its generic tooling (Robot Framework, TCP UART, Windows installer, PlatformIO test hook) is excellent. Antmicro started ESP32-S3 peripheral work on 2026-09-25 (#100525), so it is worth re-checking after the next release.
caveats: The Renode 1.14 line 'translation support for Espressif ESP32 chips' means CPU cores only (maintainer comment, 2024-11-25).

Sean 'xobs' Cross's community ESP32-S3 badge port had only UART and memory working; SPI, I2C and the interrupt controller were missing (talk at p.xobs.io/c23). Its repo git.xobs.io/xobs/renode-esp32s3 returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-29.
The new ESP32 models are on master/nightly only, not in 1.17.0.
A third-party ESP32-C3 Renode platform exists (mithro/renode-espemu, separate entry).
candidates.cost_notes: Free (MIT). Antmicro offers commercial support and custom model development.

candidates.name: Espressif esp-emulator (esp-emu, Beta)
candidates.license: The repo (installer, docs, helper tools) is Apache-2.0. The emulator itself ships as prebuilt binaries only and its source is unpublished; issue #10 asks about publication and has no answer.
candidates.summary: Espressif's Rust-based emulator (Beta) for ESP32-C3/C5/C6/H2/P4/S31 and, since 0.43.0, ESP32-S3. On S3 it runs two LX7 cores and boots the real mask ROM, then the IDF bootloader, then the app. It runs merged flash images. It adds TCP bridges for UART0 and UART1 and a TCP control channel (reset, erase or write flash). It also has a GDB stub, a Perfetto trace, WiFi/BLE and a WASM browser build.

capabilities.detail: The Apache-2.0 LICENSE covers the repo contents only; the emulator ships as binaries. Issue #10 (2026-09-06), 'Will esp-emulator's source be published, and under what terms?', is still open.

From the 0.43.0 notes: 'Stock ESP-IDF images boot through the real ROM and bootloader to a dual-core app_main. Timers, interrupts, GPIO, PCNT, MCPWM, GDMA, eFuse and flash encryption are modelled… USB-OTG is not modelled.'

The docs show only ESP-IDF images (idf.py merge-bin). Arduino and PlatformIO are not mentioned in the README, the guides or the 0.42–0.44 notes, and an issue search for 'arduino' returns nothing. Arduino 2.0.17 (IDF 4.4) images are untested.
No integration. --firmware takes a merged flash binary (with optional --elf), so PlatformIO's bootloader, partitions, boot_app0 and firmware binaries must first be merged with esptool merge_bin.

--uart-tcp HOST:PORT turns UART0 into a TCP server that esptool and pyserial socket:// can use. --uart1-tcp does the same for UART1, and stdin is forwarded to UART RX. DTR/RTS do not cross TCP, so reset goes through --control-tcp ('reset', 'reset --soft'). USB-Serial-JTAG is not on the TCP bridge; issue #11 says only --uart-tcp and stdout are visible to the host.

The peripheral is modelled, and on S3 esptool/espefuse work over socket:// in USB-Serial-JTAG download mode (0.43.0). Open issue #11 (C6) reports SOF always asserted, INT_CLR not clearing it, and no USB channel on the host side. Whether the host can feed the app's HWCDC RX is undocumented.

LEDC appears in the README's general peripheral list but not in the S3 release notes. There is no VCD, logic-analyzer or GPIO-event output for measuring pulses; a GPIO bridge is only a request (#5). Register writes can only be seen indirectly in the RUST_LOG=debug/trace peripheral-access logs.
There is no CLI or TCP way to drive input pins; only --strap-mode at reset. Open issue #5 (2026-09-02) requests a two-way GPIO event bridge.

The HP I2C master is modelled on every chip, with one built-in 24Cxx-style EEPROM slave at 0x50. That slave can only be swapped inside the emulator (I2c::set_slave). There is no interface for external or custom sensors (#5).

Systimer, timer groups and the TIMG and RTC watchdogs are modelled. 0.44.0 fixed three problems: task-WDT timing (the [task_wdt] group passes on C3/C5/P4; S3 is not listed), esp_timer and tick drift after clock changes, and reboots after esp_restart(). An S3 panic or abort prints a full backtrace with source lines (0.43.0), and reset causes are reported for some chips. How LEDC behaves across a CPU-only reset is undocumented.

Headless CLI with --timeout, --exit-on <string> (exits with code 0), --inject/--inject-on and --control-tcp, which was designed for pytest-embedded hard_reset() and erase. No account or token needed; the binaries are free.

Binaries exist only for Linux x86_64/arm64, macOS arm64 and a WASM browser bundle. install.sh aborts on MINGW/MSYS/CYGWIN ('Build from source under WSL or native Windows'). On this machine, use WSL2 or the browser build.

It is an emulator only, but it copies the hardware workflow: esptool, espefuse and idf.py flash over socket://, and pytest-embedded resets through the control channel. The same pytest-embedded suite can target the emulator or a real board by changing the port.

candidates.fit: The best-maintained ESP32-S3 emulator in this area: vendor-made, with weekly releases, real ROM boot and a TCP serial bridge. The binary protocol could run over TCP only if a simulation build routes Serial to UART0, because the bridge does not carry USB-Serial-JTAG. It cannot drive the E-stop pin or measure LEDC pulses from outside, Arduino images are untested, it is a closed-source beta, and it needs WSL2 on this Windows 11 machine. So it suits boot, protocol and watchdog smoke tests, not PWM or E-stop tests.
caveats: Beta: behaviour changed a lot between 0.42 and 0.44 (September 2026).
Since 0.44.0 the S3 PSRAM default is 8 MB; use --psram-size 0 to match a no-PSRAM esp32-s3-devkitc-1.
USB-OTG is not modelled on S3.
Open issues: #5 (external-device bridges), #10 (source and licence), #11 (USB-Serial-JTAG SOF).
candidates.cost_notes: Free download. The licence terms of the binary itself are not stated (issue #10).

candidates.name: Velxio (open-source browser simulator, QEMU-based for ESP32)
candidates.license: The web app is AGPL-3.0, dual-licensed with a commercial option (CLA required). The QEMU libraries are GPL-2.0, but the source of Velxio's modified tree is distributed via a licence-key endpoint (free personal key). velxio-cli is MIT. The CI engines (esp32js, esp32s3js) sit in a non-public 'pro' overlay.
candidates.latest_version: v3.0.5 (2026-09-02); master active on 2026-09-28. velxio-cli 0.2.x (last commit 2026-09-21).
candidates.summary: Browser simulator with a hosted site (velxio.dev), a self-hosted Docker image and a paid desktop app. ESP32, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-C3 run on a Velxio-modified lcgamboa QEMU (libqemu-xtensa, machine esp32s3-picsimlab). A Python worker bridges GPIO, ADC, UART, I2C, SPI, RMT and LEDC to the canvas. Sketches are compiled server-side with arduino-esp32 3.3.10 on IDF 5.5.4, and you can upload your own .bin. velxio-cli runs Wokwi-compatible scenarios in CI on Velxio's runners.

capabilities.detail: The app is AGPLv3. The S3 machine it uses (esp32s3-picsimlab, esp32s3_gpspi.c) is not in upstream lcgamboa/qemu; its GPL-2.0 source comes as a tarball behind a licence-key endpoint. The CI JS engines are in a private 'pro' overlay.
ESP32-S3 DevKit, XIAO ESP32-S3 and Arduino Nano ESP32 are available both self-hosted (QEMU) and on velxio.dev.

The built-in toolchain is arduino-esp32 3.3.10 on IDF 5.5.4. The docs say 2.0.17 images 'still boot on libqemu', though the sketch UI needs 3.x APIs. 'Upload firmware' accepts a .bin (merged or app-only).
No PlatformIO integration. velxio-cli takes a merged image, flasher_args.json, or app.bin with bootloader and partition siblings. A bare app.bin is refused with a merge_bin hint.

There is a browser serial monitor, and velxio-cli streams serial to stdout and forwards stdin (--interactive). There is no TCP, RFC2217 or PTY endpoint for pyserial; the CLI warns that rfc2217ServerPort is unsupported.

Velxio forces ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1 for CDC-on-boot builds; its code comment says 'the engine models the Serial-JTAG console; the OTG device stack it does not', and UART0 and USB are merged into one monitor. The upstream lcgamboa S3 USB-Serial-JTAG is a stub (reads return 0), and no bridge code is visible in the open-source repo, so this needs checking before relying on it.

LEDC duty is polled from QEMU internals about every 50 ms and routed to pins through a GPIO-matrix SignalRouter. You get duty percentage only, with no pulse timing or VCD. The signal-ID table covers ESP32-classic LEDC (HS 71-78, LS 79-86); no S3-specific LEDC mapping is evident.
Buttons and switches work in the UI. velxio-cli scenarios have set-control (press/release) and expect-pin steps, and the worker sets pins with qemu_picsimlab_set_pin.

The I2C callback is synchronous. Python slave models exist for MPU6050, BMP280, DS1307 and DS3231, and users can write custom chips in C compiled to WASM (velxio-chip.h). No AS5600, BNO085, VL53L1X or MT6701 models were found.

Timer and watchdog models come from the Espressif/lcgamboa QEMU. On Xtensa, -icount is off (guest time follows host time) except for sensor-timing runs. The fidelity of the task WDT, panic and reset reason is not documented.

velxio-cli and a GitHub Action run scenarios (wait-serial, write-serial, set-control, expect-pin) and return exit codes. They need a login token and a paid plan: Free has no CI minutes, Maker (USD 5.75/month) gives 200, Pro (USD 15.75/month) gives 2,000. CI runs on Velxio's JS engines, not the open-source QEMU. The self-hosted image has no documented headless runner.
Works in a browser or Docker Desktop. Velxio Desktop has a signed Windows installer but needs a paid plan (30-day trial). velxio-cli has a PowerShell installer.
v3.0.4 added 'Flash to real board' through Web Serial, and a hardware-serial monitor hook exists. There is no shared HIL test runner.

candidates.fit: Good for interactive experiments with ESP32-S3 and sensors in a browser, and it can be self-hosted. It is weak for this project's automated tests. No pyserial-reachable port exists, and CI runs on a different closed engine that costs paid minutes. LEDC is only visible as duty % with the ESP32-classic mapping, and S3 HWCDC and watchdog fidelity are undocumented.
caveats: Single-maintainer project with a fast release cadence.
Building the ESP32-S3 QEMU from source needs the key-gated source archive; upstream lcgamboa/qemu lacks esp32s3-picsimlab.
A code comment says the S3 QEMU machine models no radio (WiFi).
The AGPL network clause applies if you modify and host it.
candidates.cost_notes: Web use and self-hosting are free (AGPL). Maker costs USD 5.75/month (69/year) and Pro USD 15.75/month (189/year); both include the desktop app and CI minutes. A commercial licence is available on request.

candidates.name: PICSimLab (QEMU-based ESP32 / ESP32-C3 boards)
candidates.license: GPL-2.0. Its QEMU backend (lcgamboa/qemu, branch picsimlab-esp32) is also GPL-2.0.
candidates.summary: Desktop multi-MCU board simulator. Its ESP32-DevKitC (ESP32, LX6) and ESP32-C3-DevKitC-02 boards run on lcgamboa's QEMU fork, loaded as libqemu-xtensa/riscv32. There is no ESP32-S3 board. It includes many parts (I2C sensors, quadrature encoder, servo, oscilloscope, VCD dump), a TCP remote-control interface (port 5000) with a Python wrapper, and serial through com0com or tty0tty.

capabilities.detail: GPL-2.0, as is the QEMU fork.
Only the ESP32-DevKitC and ESP32-C3-DevKitC-02 boards exist (0.9.3 manual). The lcgamboa fork carries Espressif's plain esp32s3 machine, but PICSimLab has no S3 board.
Arduino-built ESP32 and C3 binaries can be flashed 'as a real ESP32 board' from the Arduino IDE or esptool over the virtual serial port. Only DIO/DOUT flash modes are supported. No S3.
The Project Wizard uses PlatformIO IDE for ESP32 boards. The manual documents platformio.ini upload via esptool to the virtual COM port and GDB debugging on port 1234.
The board's UART is connected to a host serial port ('HWSerial') through a com0com (Windows) or tty0tty (Linux) null-modem pair, so pyserial can open the other end. A DSR-reset option is available.
ESP32 has no USB-Serial-JTAG. For C3, the fork's USB-Serial-JTAG device is a stub: reads return 0 and writes are ignored.

The fork's ESP32 LEDC model computes duty % and frequency from registers but generates no waveform. PICSimLab exposes the pin mean value (0-200) through rcontrol 'get pinm[n]', oscilloscope measurements ('oscmeasures') and VCD Dump parts. Exact pulse timing is unverified.
Inputs can be driven with rcontrol 'set pin[n] v' or 'set part[x].in[y] v', with push-button and switch parts, or from the pip package PICSimLab_rcontrol.

ESP32 I2C is forwarded to PICSimLab parts: ADXL345, BMP180/BMP280, DS1621, MPU6050, a rotary quadrature encoder, HC-SR04 and others. New parts need C++ inside PICSimLab. None of this project's sensors (MT6701, AS5600, BNO085, VL53L1X) exist; the encoder part can stand in for ABZ signals.

Timers come from QEMU. The watchdog is disabled by default (ConfDisableWdt = 1, configurable), and the instruction count (MIPS) is configurable, so timing is not real-time. Panic and reset-reason fidelity is undocumented.

Tests can be scripted over the rcontrol TCP protocol (loadhex, reset, sim start/stop, set/get pins, oscilloscope) or the Python wrapper. It is a GUI application with no documented headless mode. Free.
Official win32 and win64 installers (0.9.3). On Windows the backend loads lib/qemu/libqemu-xtensa.dll with LoadLibrary.
Simulation only, although the host workflow (esptool or pyserial on a COM port) is the same as with a real board.

candidates.fit: Cannot run ESP32-S3 firmware. It could run an ESP32-classic build of the Arduino glue, with Serial on UART0, natively on Windows. The E-stop pin and PWM duty could then be scripted through rcontrol and pyserial via com0com. That would be a partial logic smoke test of main.cpp, with no S3 fidelity (HWCDC, S3 LEDC, panic-hook registers).
caveats: Board models are simplified: reset, serial and crystal only.
The QEMU flash supports DIO/DOUT only.
The watchdog is off by default.
It is a GUI application.

candidates.name: SimulIDE (official, Arcachofo/SimulIDE-dev) – experimental ESP32
candidates.license: GPLv3. Files authored by Santiago González are AGPLv3 (copyright.txt).
candidates.latest_version: SimulIDE 2.0.0 tester build R260501 (2026-05-01; Windows 64 and Linux 64) with experimental ESP32. Stable SimulIDE 1.x has no ESP32.
candidates.summary: Real-time circuit simulator (Qt). Since late 2025 it has an experimental ESP32-classic core running on a custom QEMU machine (esp32-simul) synchronised through shared memory. On 2026-04-07 the developer wrote: 'experimental implementation of Esp32. Should be working (at least partially): GPIO, SPI, I2C, Uart, Wifi, LED PWM, Timers.' There is no ESP32-S3 or C3 support.

capabilities.detail: GPLv3 or AGPLv3 depending on the file.
Only an ESP32-classic core exists (src/microsim/cores/qemu/esp32, peripheral base 0x3FF00000).
It loads ESP32-classic flash images (merged .bin); support is experimental.
No documented PlatformIO integration in the official project.
The 'Serial Port' component connects a simulated UART to a real or virtual PC port (for example com0com). UART routing to MCU pins was added in late 2025.
ESP32-classic only; no USB-Serial-JTAG.
'LED PWM' is listed as at least partially working. The output can be viewed with SimulIDE's oscilloscope and 8-channel logic analyzer, which exports VCD. This is a GUI tool, not an API.
Switches and buttons can be operated interactively in the circuit, but there is no external scripting API for tests.
I2C is listed as working. The component library has a few I2C parts (DS1621, DS1307, SSD1306, I2C RAM).
QEMU is started with '-global driver=timer.esp32.timg,property=wdt_disable,value=true' and -icount, so the TIMG watchdog is off and time is virtual. Panic and reset behaviour are undocumented.
GUI application; no headless or CLI test runner is documented.
The tester build is available for Windows 64-bit (and Linux 64-bit).
Simulator only.

candidates.fit: Not relevant. It supports only ESP32 classic, is experimental and GUI-only, and runs with the watchdog disabled.
caveats: In December 2023 the developer said there were no ESP32 plans; ESP32 work began in late 2025.
The tester branch is marked 'can be very unstable'.

candidates.name: SimulIDE-dev fork by Sergey Sasykin (ESP32-S3 / C3 via QEMU bridge)
candidates.license: GPLv3/AGPLv3, inherited from SimulIDE. The QEMU fork (SKSasykin/SimulIDE-qemu) is GPL-2.0.
candidates.latest_version: No releases; build from source. Last commit 2026-09-24. Personal fork (0 stars).
candidates.summary: Fork of official SimulIDE-dev that adds ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3 and ESP8266 through a QEMU fork with a SimulIDE shared-memory bridge. The S3 model covers the UART (FIFOs and interrupts), GPIO matrix with electrical pulls, 2 polling I2C masters, 2 SPI masters, ADC, and LEDC with real output toggling into the circuit. It also has a virtual WiFi NIC and BLE demos, and a bundled S3 Arduino blink image.

capabilities.detail: GPLv3/AGPLv3 app plus a GPL-2.0 QEMU fork.
Runs QEMU '-M esp32s3' with a bridge and boots bundled S3 firmware (blink, WiFi HTTP, BLE GATT). It is a young personal fork.
Ships a bundled S3 blink.ino.merged.bin, and the README says the UART model covers behaviour 'used by ESP-IDF and Arduino'. The Arduino version is not stated. The BLE demos were built with IDF 5.5.5.

The README says an app-only PlatformIO firmware.bin is auto-merged with the sibling bootloader.bin and partitions.bin into a 4 MB image. This is described with the classic layout (bootloader at 0x1000); it is unverified for S3.
The UART can reach the host only through SimulIDE's Serial Port component, for example with com0com. No TCP API.
USB-Serial-JTAG is not modelled or mentioned; the S3 console is UART0.

The S3 LEDC model (8 channels, 4 timers, register base 0x60019000) models frequency exactly, takes duty from DUTY>>4 and drives the pin into the circuit, so pulses can be seen on the oscilloscope or logic analyzer (VCD). Not implemented: HPOINT, fade, LEDC interrupts, and XTAL/RC clock sources.
Inputs are driven interactively through circuit parts, and pulls are modelled as nominal 45 kΩ conductances. There is no scripting API.
Polling-mode I2C masters (command list, ACK/NACK, interrupt delivery) connect to SimulIDE's I2C parts. Slave mode and DMA are not implemented.

The S3 is launched with '-global driver=timer.esp32c3.timg,property=wdt_disable,value=true' and '-icount shift=4', and the model's clock stamp is 40 MHz. The task WDT therefore never fires and time is virtual.
tests/run-tests.sh runs source-contract checks and IDE smoke boots of the bundled firmware. There is no user-facing headless test API.
Build instructions cover Linux and macOS (Qt5 plus the QEMU submodule). There are no Windows binaries or releases.
Simulator only.

candidates.fit: It shows realistic S3 LEDC waveforms in a circuit. It is unsuitable here: no USB-Serial-JTAG, the watchdog is forced off, it is GUI-only, it has no Windows build, and it is an unreleased personal fork.
caveats: A single-author fork with 0 stars and no releases.
The S3 WiFi uses a custom SLC NIC transport, not the real WiFi driver (not needed by this project).

candidates.name: esp32sim (joakimeriksson) – Rust ESP32-S3/C3/C6 emulator
candidates.license: MIT
candidates.latest_version: No tagged releases. main branch at 2026-09-23 (1,125 commits since 2026-08-25). A live WASM demo runs on GitHub Pages.
candidates.summary: Instruction-level Rust emulator. ESP32-S3 is described as mature; ESP32-C3 and C6 are drafts. It boots the real mask ROM, then the 2nd-stage bootloader, then an unmodified app. USB Serial/JTAG and GPIO are modelled in full, and I2C, PCNT, RMT and I2S partly or fully. There is no LEDC, and the TIMG watchdog is a stub. The RTC watchdog reset and the reset cause are modelled. Other features: timed host-action scripts, VCD of GPIO edges, a WebSocket UI protocol, a WASM build, and JTAG lock-step differential tests against a real S3. Its default demo is a PlatformIO Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17 firmware with HWCDC.

capabilities.detail: MIT, by Joakim Eriksson and Alice.
Boots ROM, bootloader, FreeRTOS and the app on two LX7 cores. JTAG lock-step against a real S3 showed 0 divergences over 3000 bootloader steps (2026-08-25).

The default demo, atech-firmware, is built with PlatformIO espressif32@6.9.0 (Arduino core 2.0.17) for board esp32-s3-devkitc-1 with ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1 and ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=1. That is the same configuration as this project. Arduino 3.x is untested.
It takes --bootloader, --ptable and --app (PlatformIO's bootloader.bin, partitions.bin and firmware.bin), or --flash-image, plus --flash-at for otadata or data partitions. No PlatformIO integration.

There is no TCP, PTY or RFC2217 port. Input goes in through --serial TEXT, timed 'serial' script lines, or the --web WebSocket JSON protocol ('key' and 'serial' messages; native clients may omit Origin). Output goes to stdout (--console usb|uart0|both) or WebSocket 'serial' events. JSON text framing makes arbitrary binary (COBS) bytes uncertain.
The peripheral table lists USB Serial/JTAG as 'full': 'TX/RX FIFOs, interrupts (IDF console and Arduino Serial)'.
The peripheral table lists LEDC (with ADC, SPI3, TWAI, SDMMC and USB-OTG) as not modelled. --vcd records GPIO edges, but LEDC produces none.

Pins can be driven at emulated times with script lines such as 'gpio 17 0', 'press btn1 150' and 'release 16', or with the WebSocket message 'gpio {pin, level}'. GPIO edge and level interrupts are modelled.

I2C0/1 are 'full' for the IDF i2c_master driver (command list, FIFOs, NACK/END/COMPLETE interrupts). Devices are Rust board models (BoardModel::i2c_devices), so custom sensors need Rust code. The legacy IDF 4.4 I2C driver used by Arduino 2.0.17 is unverified.

Systimer is full, so esp_timer should work, and TIMG timers have alarms. But the 'timer-group watchdog registers are stubs and never fire', so the task WDT cannot trigger. RTC watchdog reset stages, software resets and the reset cause are modelled, and reboots go through ROM (for example rst:0xc RTC_SW_CPU_RST). CPU-reset vs LEDC behaviour cannot be tested because there is no LEDC.
Headless CLI with --max-seconds, --script, --console, --vcd and --no-reboot. The project's own CI on GitHub Actions runs golden-output regression tests. No account; free.

CI runs only on ubuntu-latest and ubuntu-24.04-arm, and there are no Windows build instructions (WSL2 is the likely route). The JIT is AArch64-only; x86_64 uses the interpreter. The WASM build runs in any browser, and the live page can load your own firmware.
The hw/ scripts run JTAG lock-step differential tests against a real ESP32-S3 over its USB-Serial/JTAG (OpenOCD), plus console diffs for C3/C6. This is not a general HIL test runner.

candidates.fit: The closest open-source match in this area. It already runs a PlatformIO Arduino 2.0.17 S3 firmware with HWCDC in the same configuration as this project, and it can script the E-stop GPIO and serial input at emulated time and record GPIO edges as VCD. That makes it plausible for checking that the panic hook drives the ESC pin low and that the reset reason is right. It cannot test LEDC pulses (not modelled) or the task WDT (TIMG watchdog stub), and pyserial would need a WebSocket or new TCP adapter. The MIT licence allows adding these pieces.
caveats: Young (about 5 weeks), 2 authors, 8 stars, no releases or stability guarantees.
ESP32-S3 peripheral MMIO must be aligned 32-bit; the emulator faults on byte or halfword accesses.
The GPIO release and pull-up semantics for an INPUT_PULLUP E-stop are unverified.

candidates.name: esp32s3-emulator (danish9661) – Rust→WASM ESP32-S3 emulator
candidates.license: None declared: there is no LICENSE file at the repo root, only tools/qemu-ref/LICENSE. The README says the intended outcome is GPL-compatible. Legally the code is all rights reserved until a licence is added.
candidates.latest_version: No releases. The repo was created on 2026-09-21; last commit 2026-09-29 (99 commits).
candidates.summary: From-scratch ESP32-S3 emulator (Xtensa LX7 core plus SoC) in Rust, compiled to WASM for the browser, with a Rust example runner (run_flash). It claims 117 of 117 validation cases booting real arduino-cli (core 3.3.10) firmware. It models USB-Serial-JTAG CDC, LEDC, the MWDT and RWDT watchdogs, I2C and more.

capabilities.detail: The code is public but has no licence.
The README claims boot of real ESP-IDF and Arduino firmware through ROM stubs and the second-stage loader, with P0–P6 complete. The project is only 8 days old.
Validated with arduino-cli esp32 core 3.3.10 images. Arduino 2.0.17 is untested.
Needs a merged .bin (bootloader, partitions and app). No PlatformIO support.
There is no TCP or PTY serial port. Serial goes through the WASM API (uart_read, uart_inject_rx, usb_inject_rx) or the browser UI. TCP is used only for the GDB stub.
Functional CDC model with TX/RX FIFOs and the SERIAL_OUT_RECV_PKT and SERIAL_IN_EMPTY interrupts. The host is modelled as always present.

The LEDC model is a comparator: output is high while count < duty>>4, routed to GPIO-matrix signals 73+n. Output can only be observed through gpio_output() and events; no measurement or VCD tooling is documented.
The WASM API exposes gpio_output(), and touch, ADC, UART, I2C and SPI injection, but has no GPIO-input setter.
i2c_inject_rx(chan, bytes) injects raw bytes; there are no sensor models.
Systimer, TIMG with MWDT, and RTC with RWDT are modelled. The README says the model clock is approximate: '1 global tick per 2 instructions for all domains'.
cargo test machine tests boot firmware and assert on serial output. There is no user-facing CLI test runner or scenario format. Free.
Not documented. It is Rust with a browser WASM build.
Emulator only.

candidates.fit: Only worth watching. It is 8 days old, unlicensed and has one author, and it lacks a GPIO-input API and a host serial port.
caveats: The same author has danish9661/esp32-emulator (ESP32-classic, MIT) and esp-emulator-wasm (RISC-V only); neither covers S3.
candidates.cost_notes: Free to view. No licence has been granted.

candidates.license: Proprietary (closed source). Free tier plus a paid membership.
candidates.latest_version: Hosted web app. The ESP32-S3 simulator was announced on 2026-05-05.
candidates.summary: Browser-based circuit designer with an instruction-accurate ESP32-S3 emulator in Rust/WASM that boots through Espressif's ROM and bootloader. Arduino sketches are compiled on Cirkit's server. It claims GPIO, UART, partial USB-Serial/JTAG, LEDC, I2C, timers, watchdogs and WiFi (open networks only).

capabilities.detail: Closed source; features are unlocked by membership.
'Cirkit supports ESP32-S3 simulation today'. It executes real Xtensa instructions through the ROM and bootloader.
Sketches are compiled server-side, and the core version is not documented. Uploading your own .bin or .elf is not documented.
Not documented.
Only a browser serial monitor; no host port or API.
The docs say 'Serial TX output works. RX input not fully exposed', so this project's HELLO/ARM/COMMAND RX path could not be driven.
LEDC PWM is 'used by analogWrite(), Servo, tone/buzzer'. No measurement API is documented.
Buttons can be pressed interactively; no scripting API is documented.
2 I2C controllers work with Wire and the catalog's sensors and displays. Custom models are not documented.
The docs claim 'MWDT and RWDT with standard ESP-IDF/Arduino usage'; fidelity is not documented.
No CLI, API or CI is documented.
Browser-based.
'Upload firmware to supported hardware when you are ready to build'. There is no shared test runner.

candidates.fit: Not suitable. It is closed source, has no automation, and USB-Serial/JTAG RX is not exposed, which breaks this project's host protocol.
caveats: WiFi supports open networks only; Bluetooth is not supported.

candidates.name: ESP-IDF Linux target / 'Running ESP-IDF Applications on Host'
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (ESP-IDF).
candidates.latest_version: ESP-IDF v6.1 (2026-08-27). The Linux/POSIX target is still a 'preview target'.
candidates.summary: Builds ESP-IDF apps as native Linux/macOS executables using the FreeRTOS POSIX/Linux simulator (single-core scheduling) plus CMock mocks. It is not chip emulation, and only listed components are supported: driver, esp_timer and spi_flash are mock-only, while freertos, esp_event, nvs_flash, log and esp_system are simulated. The docs state that simulating and mocking 'does not fully represent the target device'.

capabilities.detail: Part of ESP-IDF (Apache-2.0).
Host build only. There is no ESP32-S3 instruction or peripheral emulation, and firmware binaries do not run.
The app must set COMPONENTS to main and use only Linux-supported or mockable components. arduino-esp32 is not among them.
No PlatformIO support for the IDF Linux target is documented.
There is no emulated UART or USB peripheral; the app is a host process that uses stdio.
Not simulated.
The driver component is mock-only (CMock), with no LEDC behaviour.
Inputs can only be faked through CMock expectations or stubs on driver APIs; there is no pin model.
Mock-level only: sensor replies can be faked by mocking driver calls. There are no device models.
FreeRTOS scheduling is simulated with POSIX signals, which has documented limitations. esp_timer is mock-only, and there is no WDT or panic hardware.
Produces a normal executable, and the docs describe running test batteries in CI/CD. Ruby is needed for mocks. Free.
Requires 'a recent enough Linux or macOS version and GCC compiler'; use WSL on Windows.
The same Unity test code can be built for the chip target and run on hardware, but the Linux target itself is host-only.

candidates.fit: Not applicable to the Arduino glue in main.cpp. It duplicates what the project already does: the portable C++ core is tested on the PC with CMake/g++. Use it only if parts of the firmware moved to pure ESP-IDF.

report.notes:
Checked 2026-09-29. Out of scope for this area and only mentioned where other tools reuse them: Wokwi and Espressif's official QEMU fork.

BOTTOM LINE: No tool in this area can run this firmware today with every feature observable (ESP32-S3, Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17, HWCDC over USB-Serial-JTAG, LEDC 50 Hz servo/ESC, INPUT_PULLUP E-stop, esp_timer guard, task WDT, panic hook).

Closest options, in order:
1. esp32sim (joakimeriksson, MIT).
   - Its demo firmware is a PlatformIO espressif32@6.9.0 build (Arduino 2.0.17, esp32-s3-devkitc-1, ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1, CDC_ON_BOOT=1), the same configuration as this project.
   - It models USB-Serial/JTAG in full, GPIO scripting at emulated time, VCD of GPIO edges, and the RTC watchdog with reset cause.
   - It lacks LEDC and a firing TIMG watchdog (so no task-WDT test), and it has no TCP serial port (only a WebSocket/JSON protocol).
2. Espressif esp-emulator 0.44.0 (closed-source Beta).
   - Has had ESP32-S3 support since 2026-09-18.
   - It offers a UART0/UART1 TCP bridge usable with pyserial socket://, a control channel for resets, and pytest-embedded-style CI flags.
   - HWCDC is not on the TCP bridge, there is no GPIO or LEDC host interface (issue #5), Arduino is untested, and it runs only on Linux/macOS (WSL2 on this PC). Use --psram-size 0 for a no-PSRAM board.
3. Velxio (AGPL app, key-gated GPL QEMU).
   - Has ESP32-S3 boards and scriptable scenarios.
   - Its CI needs paid minutes and uses closed JS engines, there is no pyserial port, and LEDC is visible as duty % only.
4. PICSimLab 0.9.3 (GPL, native Windows).
   - Supports ESP32-classic and C3 only.
   - Has rcontrol TCP scripting, com0com serial and I2C/encoder parts, and could smoke-test an ESP32-classic UART0 build variant.

Renode 1.17.0 (2026-09-07) cannot boot ESP32-S3 at all. Antmicro began S3 peripheral work on master on 2026-09-25 (#100525: ESP32_USBSerialJTAG without interrupts, TIMG without WDT, RTC_CNTL, EXTMEM, SPI), with no platform (.repl) yet, so re-check after the next release.

Not usable for this project:
- SimulIDE official: ESP32-classic only, experimental, watchdog disabled.
- SimulIDE fork by SKSasykin: has S3 LEDC waveforms but no USB-Serial-JTAG, watchdog disabled, GUI-only, no releases.
- Cirkit Designer: closed; USB-Serial/JTAG RX not exposed.
- Proteus: ESP32-S3 only for MicroPython.
- Tinkercad: no ESP32.
- ESP-IDF Linux target: host build; no Arduino; drivers are mocks only.

Implication for any UART-only emulator (esp-emu TCP bridge, PICSimLab, SimulIDE): a simulation build environment with ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=0 (Serial → UART0) would be needed. The laptop side can then use SerialVehicleIO with serial_for_url('socket://…').

Other findings with evidence:
- Unicorn Engine has no Xtensa. Its supported list is ARM, ARM64, m68k, MIPS, PowerPC, RISC-V, S390x, SPARC, TriCore and x86; the latest release is 2.1.4 (2025-09-09); issue #2306 'Xtensa CPU support' has been open since 2026-03-06. No Unicorn-based ESP32-S3 emulator was found.
- Ebiroll/qemu_esp32 (Apache-2.0, QEMU 9.2 base, updated Feb 2026) covers ESP32-classic only; S2 has regressed.
- danish9661/esp32-emulator (MIT, WASM) covers ESP32-classic only. danish9661/esp-emulator-wasm is RISC-V only and explicitly has no S3.
- The community Renode ESP32-S3 repo (git.xobs.io/xobs/renode-esp32s3) returned HTTP 404.
- Flowcode (Matrix TSL): no primary evidence found that it runs ESP32 binaries. Virtual Breadboard: no primary evidence of ESP32 support. Neither was evaluated further.

The binary's help, however, says --strap-mode 0x04 (USB-Serial/JTAG download) is 'pair[ed] with --uart-tcp' and needs ESPTOOL_USB_VID_PID=303a:1001, and the strings include 'USB-Serial/JTAG download console active … bytes read over EP1'. So in ROM download mode the TCP bridge does carry USB-Serial-JTAG. For app-mode HWCDC no route is documented. In my CDC_ON_BOOT=1 run, stdout showed only the UART0 ROM banner, and --inject feeds only UART RX. The HWCDC build therefore cannot be driven from the host; a UART0 build variant is needed, and it works.

checks.source: pyserial 3.5 serial/urlhandler/protocol_socket.py (in_waiting = len(select.select([sock],[],[],0)[0]), i.e. 0 or 1); D:\xetulai\autopark\autopark\autopark\transport\vehicle_io.py lines 856-868 (_pump reads transport.in_waiting bytes once per poll); Windows test script scratchpad\win_vehicleio_client.py
checks.correction: The unmodified SerialVehicleIO over socket:// reads only 1 byte per poll(), because pyserial's socket handler reports in_waiting as 0 or 1. In my Windows→WSL test, connect() and arm() succeeded, but TELEMETRY_STALE fired about 1 s later (and also with telemetry_timeout_s=2.0). Wrapping the transport so in_waiting returns the real byte count (recv(MSG_PEEK)) fixed it: with the default 0.3 s timeout the run reached RUNNING with 75 telemetry frames, no safety events, and 50 ms command echo. An rfc2217:// transport (which keeps a real queue) or a pump loop would also avoid the problem.
