verification.overall:
The report is mostly accurate: about 45 checked claims were confirmed, including every Renode, esp32sim, Velxio, Proteus, ESP-IDF, Unicorn and date/version claim that matters. The bottom line for Renode stands: it cannot boot any ESP32-S3 image today. There are, however, several material corrections.

1. The report says Arduino images are "untested" on Espressif's esp-emulator. I tested them on this PC: esp-emu 0.44.0 in the already-installed WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04 boots the project's own Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17 S3 build to loop(). A UART0 variant (CDC_ON_BOOT=0) passed the full binary protocol over --uart-tcp: HELLO_ACK, 20 Hz telemetry, ARM, RUNNING with the speed ramp, then the command and link timeouts. Reset reasons are correct: POWER_ON on cold boot and SOFTWARE after a soft reset. The emulator ran at about 0.5–0.6× real time.

2. The "SerialVehicleIO + serial_for_url('socket://…')" route in the report (and in the project facts) fails as-is. pyserial's socket handler reports in_waiting as 0 or 1, so the host reads one byte per poll and raises TELEMETRY_STALE. A MSG_PEEK in_waiting adapter fixed it.

3. esp-emulator issue #10 was answered: the source-publication decision is undecided.

4. The esp-emu TCP bridge does carry USB-Serial-JTAG in ROM download mode (strap 0x04). App-mode HWCDC is still unreachable from the host, so the UART0 build variant remains necessary.

5. The claim that LEDC register writes show up in RUST_LOG is doubtful: only unhandled offsets are logged, and GDB register reads are the practical route.

6. Renode's ESP32_TIMG models only RTC calibration, not the general timers.

7. PICSimLab does have a headless NOGUI build and automated ESP32 self-tests.

8. The danish9661 emulator's history starts 2026-08-14, not 2026-09-21.

Unverified or open: task-WDT firing on S3 under esp-emu, LEDC pulses and E-stop pin input (GDB-level only), and esp32sim with this image (it needs a Rust build and cargo is not installed).

Net effect on the ranking: esp-emulator should now come first, because it is proven on this machine today for boot, protocol and reset-reason tests (with a UART0 build and the host fix). esp32sim remains the only candidate that models HWCDC, GPIO scripting and VCD, but it is unproven here.

verified.title: Host-side testing of the Arduino/ESP-IDF glue code without any chip

report.topic: Host-side (PC) testing of the ESP32-S3 Arduino/ESP-IDF glue (src/main.cpp) with no chip: fakes/mocks and Arduino-on-desktop layers (checked 2026-09-29)

candidates.name: PlatformIO Unit Testing on the native platform (Unity / GoogleTest / Doctest runners)
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (PlatformIO Core, platform-native); bundled runners: Unity MIT, GoogleTest BSD-3-Clause, doctest MIT
candidates.latest_version: PlatformIO Core 6.2.0 (2026-09-05, PyPI); platform native 1.2.1 (2022-05-28); bundled Unity 2.6.1 / GoogleTest 1.17.0 / Doctest 2.4.12 since Core 6.1.19 (2026-02-04). Upstream is now Unity 2.7.0, GoogleTest 1.18.0, doctest 2.5.3.
candidates.summary: `pio test -e native` compiles test suites with the host GCC and runs them on the PC. For embedded envs the same command builds, uploads and runs the suites on a real board. It ships no Arduino or ESP-IDF fakes, so main.cpp's Arduino-ESP32 and ESP-IDF calls must be covered by user fakes (fff, ArduinoFake or gMock wrappers).

capabilities.detail: Core and platform-native are Apache-2.0; the runners are MIT/BSD; nothing is closed. Only the optional PIO Remote service needs a (free) PlatformIO account.

Native tests are x86-64 Windows executables; no ESP32-S3 CPU or peripheral is emulated. An emulator can only be attached through test_testing_command plus --without-uploading (the docs show QEMU, Renode and SimAVR in general terms), which belongs to the emulator area.

There is no Arduino core on native. Verified 2026-09-29 (PoC): the unmodified src/main.cpp compiles and runs on the PC against hand-written fakes, for both its Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17 branch and its 3.x branch.

Built in (platform = native; test_framework = unity|googletest|doctest|custom). Verified here with an isolated PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR: native 1.2.1 + tool-scons 4.41101.0 + Unity 2.6.1 PASSED; an ArduinoFake 0.4.0 suite and a GoogleTest/gMock 1.17.0 suite also PASSED.
sources: local run 2026-09-29: %USERPROFILE%/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--xetulai/<phiên>/scratchpad/pio_native (envs native, native_dynamic, native_fake, native_gtest all PASSED)

capabilities.detail: No serial port exists. Serial/HWCDC is an in-process fake (byte queues in the PoC). A pyserial client can connect only through a TCP or pipe bridge you write yourself (not built).
Only the HWCDC API surface can be faked: available, read(buf,len), availableForWrite, write, operator bool and setTxTimeoutMs. USB enumeration, DTR/RTS resets and TX blocking are not modelled.

Checked at call level only, through fakes. The PoC asserts ledcSetup(0,50,14)/ledcAttachPin(4,0)/ledcWrite(0,1228) on 2.x and ledcAttach(4,50,14)/ledcWrite(4,1228) on 3.x. There is no waveform and no clock-source effect.

Inputs can be driven only through fakes, for example a digitalRead that returns HIGH. There is no electrical model, so the test author must encode that an open circuit reads HIGH through INPUT_PULLUP.
No device models. Wire or ESP-IDF I2C calls must be faked or mocked (ArduinoFake WireFake, a gMock interface, or an fff custom_fake register map).

Logic only. A test can capture the esp_timer callback, fire it with a fake clock and check the TWDT, shutdown and panic-hook calls. Nothing here shows real 10 ms periods, preemption, a TWDT reset, panic entry, IRAM safety, or LEDC still running after a CPU-only reset.
The `pio test -e native` CLI returns an exit status and supports -f/-i filters, --junit-output-path and --json-output-path. No account or token; runs in any CI.

Needs a host GCC on PATH (the docs point to MSYS2). Verified 2026-09-29 with WinLibs g++ 16.1.0 UCRT. Link with -static: Git Bash puts Git's older libstdc++-6.dll first on PATH, and that already segfaulted this repo's CMake host tests.

The same tool builds, uploads and runs Unity suites (and GoogleTest on Espressif 32) on a real ESP32-S3, then parses the results from test_port. 'Hybrid' suites can run in both places, but fake-based glue tests stay host-only. Issue #1733 was opened 2026-03-31 and was still open on 2026-09-29: an ESP32-S3 with ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1 and CDC_ON_BOOT=1 drops into download mode after upload, and the runner reads nothing.

candidates.fit: The best harness for this repo, because the firmware is already a PlatformIO project. An [env:native] plus a test/test_glue suite that #includes src/main.cpp with fakes gives fast, deterministic checks on this Windows PC; keeping plain CMake as in test/host works equally well. It proves glue logic and call order. It cannot replace an emulator or the board for timing, LEDC waveforms, USB CDC, watchdog or panic behaviour.
caveats: The docs mark test_build_src as 'NOT RECOMMENDED', and it needs #ifndef PIO_UNIT_TESTING around setup()/loop(). #including main.cpp into the test translation unit, as the PoC does, avoids this and reaches main.cpp's anonymous-namespace state.
Bundled runner versions lag upstream: Unity 2.6.1 vs 2.7.0, GoogleTest 1.17.0 vs 1.18.0, doctest 2.4.12 vs 2.5.3.

The host compiler and data model differ from the chip: WinLibs GCC 16.1 vs Xtensa GCC 8.4 (Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17). size_t is 64-bit on the PC. long is 32-bit on MinGW (verified), as on the ESP32, but 64-bit on Linux CI runners.
Fake signatures are hand-copied from the 2.0.17 and 3.3.1 headers, so only `pio run` against the real cores proves API compatibility.
Core 6.2.0 fixed a Windows embedded-test failure caused by Serial.end() on an RP2040 Arduino board (#5359): https://github.com/platformio/platformio-core/issues/5359
candidates.cost_notes: Free; no account needed for local or CI use. PIO Remote (running tests on a board attached to another PC) needs a free PlatformIO account.

candidates.name: fff - Fake Function Framework (header-only link-time fakes)
candidates.license: MIT
candidates.latest_version: v1.1 (tag 2019-08-21; GitHub release published 2020-12-01); last commit on master 2023-05-22
candidates.summary: A single header (fff.h) whose macros define fake C/C++ free functions. Each fake counts calls, keeps argument histories and a global call history, and returns scripted values or sequences or runs a custom_fake (lambdas allowed). It maps directly onto the free functions the glue calls: ledcWrite, esp_timer_create, esp_task_wdt_*, esp_register_shutdown_handler and esp_rom_gpio_connect_out_signal.

capabilities.detail: MIT, a single header, nothing closed.
Host-only fakes; nothing of the S3 is emulated.

It ships no ESP32 fakes, but verified 2026-09-29: fake_hw.h (122 lines), fake_hw.cpp (69 lines) and nine two-line forwarding headers, plus a 4-line esp_arduino_version.h for 3.x, let the UNMODIFIED main.cpp build and run in three variants: the 2.0.17 API with PWM off; 2.0.17 with PWM on and fake pins 4/5/6; and the 3.x API with PWM on.

Not in the PlatformIO Registry (searched 2026-09-29) and not a PlatformIO runner. Copy fff.h into test/ or lib/, or add it through a lib_deps Git URL, and pair it with Unity or doctest. This combination was not run in pio here; it was verified with CMake.
In-process fake only (the PoC's FakeHWCDC with rx/tx byte queues).
The HWCDC members are faked by hand; no USB behaviour.
The PoC checks arguments and call histories: duty 1228 = 1500 us at 50 Hz and 14 bits, addressed by channel on 2.x and by pin on 3.x. No waveform.
Inputs are set with digitalRead_fake.return_val or return_val_seq. The PoC checks pinMode(6, INPUT_PULLUP) and that E-stop HIGH latches FAULT Estop in the real core. No electrical model.
A custom_fake can emulate register maps for the AS5600, VL53L1X or BNO085 transports; there are no ready device models.

The PoC checks: (1) the captured output_guard esp_timer callback, fired with a fake clock, writes neutral only after more than 100 ms of silence; (2) TWDT init(1 s, panic) on 2.x and reconfigure{300 ms, idle mask 0, panic} on 3.x; (3) the WDT is set up before the timer; (4) esp_task_wdt_reset runs once per loop; (5) the shutdown handler, __wrap_esp_panic_handler (2.x) and the set_arduino_panic_handler hook (3.x) write bit 4 to GPIO_OUT_W1TC/GPIO_ENABLE_W1TS and call esp_rom_gpio_connect_out_signal(4, 256, false, false). It cannot prove real timing, preemption, resets, or LEDC behaviour after a CPU reset.
Plain executables plus ctest. The PoC ran 3/3 ctest targets: 21 test cases and 120 assertions in 0.38 s. No account.

Verified with WinLibs g++ 16.1.0, CMake 4.4.1 and Ninja, linked -static, with no warnings under -Wall -Wextra. The README mentions only limited support for MSVC calling conventions, which MinGW does not need.
Link-time fakes replace the real functions, so these tests are host-only; on-target tests have to be separate.

candidates.fit: The best effort-to-benefit option for this glue. Verified today: all of main.cpp (both Arduino-ESP32 API branches, PWM on and off) runs under doctest on this Windows PC with about 190 lines of fakes. It fits the existing test/host CMake flow or a PlatformIO native env. It proves call order, arguments, register-write intent and serial/protocol plumbing in simulated time, but not timing, electrical or silicon behaviour.
caveats: Upstream is quiet (last commit 2023-05-22), though the single header is stable.

main.cpp hard-codes the pins as constexpr -1 and has a static_assert when PWM is on. Testing the PWM path therefore needs a pin-patched copy (the PoC generates one in CMake) or pins that can be overridden with -D.
A faked REG_WRITE only records the address and value. Whether W1TC/ENABLE_W1TS plus routing SIG_GPIO_OUT_IDX really pulls the ESC line low during a panic is a silicon question.
Fakes encode assumptions: for example, esp_task_wdt_init takes seconds on IDF 4.4 but a config struct on 5.x. A wrong fake still gives green tests.
The PoC is in the session scratchpad, not the repo, and may be deleted.

candidates.name: GoogleTest + GoogleMock
candidates.license: BSD-3-Clause
candidates.latest_version: v1.18.0 (2026-08-10; requires C++17); PlatformIO bundles 1.17.0
candidates.summary: An xUnit runner plus gMock for mocking C++ interfaces. PlatformIO supports it as test_framework = googletest on native and on Espressif 8266/32 boards.

capabilities.detail: BSD-3-Clause; nothing closed.
Host executable. On an ESP32 it runs only on real hardware, through PlatformIO.

No Arduino or ESP-IDF fakes. The gMock cookbook says 'It is not possible to directly mock a free function', so ledcWrite, esp_timer_create, millis and the rest need an interface wrapper (refactoring main.cpp behind a HAL) or link-time fakes (fff) alongside.
Built in. Verified 2026-09-29: a gMock EXPECT_CALL test in [env:native] with test_framework = googletest PASSED (PlatformIO installed googletest 1.17.0).
No serial port; you would mock a SerialPort interface.
No USB-Serial-JTAG model.
EXPECT_CALL on a PWM interface (a small example checking write(0,1228) was verified). No waveform.
Scripted returns (WillOnce/Return) on an input interface, after refactoring.
Mock a bus interface and use InSequence to check transaction order; no device models.
Logic only, through mocked clock, timer and watchdog interfaces.
XML reports via --gtest_output=xml:<path>, ctest, or PlatformIO's --junit-output-path. No account.

Verified through PlatformIO with WinLibs g++ 16.1.0. MinGW is not in Google's official support matrix (MSVC 2022 or later; GCC 11.2+ and Clang 14+ on supported Linux distros), but MSYS2 ships gtest 1.18.0 for mingw64, ucrt64 and clang64.
The PlatformIO docs list embedded GoogleTest as 'Yes* (only for Espressif 8266 and Espressif 32)'. Not tried on ESP32-S3. gMock-based host tests stay host-only.

candidates.fit: A good choice if the glue is refactored into small C++ classes behind interfaces (Pwm, Clock, Watchdog, SerialPort). For the current free-function main.cpp it adds refactoring cost without testing anything that fff cannot.
caveats: Requires C++17 since 1.17 (fine for this repo, which already uses gnu++17).
Builds are heavier than fff/doctest: about 9-10 s per pio test run here, mostly compiling gtest.
MinGW support is community-level, not official.

candidates.name: ArduinoFake (FakeIt-based Arduino API mocks)
candidates.license: MIT (the bundled FakeIt single header is also MIT)
candidates.latest_version: 0.4.0 (2023-06-03; also the latest in the PlatformIO Registry); last commit on master 2025-09-25; bundled fakeit.hpp generated 2023-04-17 (FakeIt upstream is 2.5.0, 2025-11-14)
candidates.summary: Provides a fake Arduino.h whose functions and Serial/Stream/Print/Wire/SPI/EEPROM/Client objects forward to FakeIt mocks, so native tests can stub and verify Arduino calls.

capabilities.detail: MIT; nothing closed.
Host-only mocks.

Only the AVR/ArduinoCore-style API: pinMode, digitalRead/Write, analog*, millis/micros/delay, pulseIn, shiftIn/Out, interrupts, tone, random, map and yield. src/ contains no ledc* or esp_* symbols. Its Serial_ has read(void) but not HWCDC's read(uint8_t*, size_t) or setTxTimeoutMs, so main.cpp will not compile without extending it.
library.json targets platform native. Verified: lib_deps = fabiobatsilva/ArduinoFake@^0.4.0 with a Unity 2.6.1 suite PASSED.
Serial is a FakeIt mock; bytes come from scripted When(...).Return(...) sequences.
Models the AVR USB 'Serial_' shape, not ESP32 HWCDC.
No LEDC API, only analogWrite.
When(Method(ArduinoFake(), digitalRead)).Return(HIGH), verified in the local test.
WireFake and SPIFake mock the TwoWire/SPIClass methods; no device models.
millis/micros/delay can be stubbed, but there is no esp_timer, task watchdog, esp_restart, reset reason or panic API.
Runs under pio test or CMake + Unity; no account.
Verified with WinLibs g++ 16.1.0 (-static). The crash code in the README, 3221225477 (0xC0000005), is the Windows access violation you get when a called function is not stubbed.
Host-only by design.

candidates.fit: Works on Windows today, but covers only generic Arduino calls. Every ESP32/ESP-IDF call in main.cpp, and the HWCDC Serial shape, would still need fakes, so fff alone is simpler here. It could be useful later for small pure-Arduino helpers.
caveats: FakeIt limits: GCC -O2/-O3 are not supported, mocks are not thread-safe, and only virtual methods can be mocked (ArduinoFake gets around this by proxying free functions to a mocked interface). See https://github.com/eranpeer/FakeIt
An unstubbed call crashes instead of failing cleanly (README troubleshooting).
Slow release cadence: the last release, 0.4.0, is from 2023.

candidates.name: CppUTest (with CppUMock)
candidates.license: BSD-3-Clause
candidates.latest_version: v4.0 (2020-05-27) is the last numbered release; master is active (last commit 2026-07-30)
candidates.summary: A C/C++ xUnit framework for embedded TDD with CppUMock expectations, memory-leak detection and JUnit output. Mocks are hand-written link-time stubs that call mock().

capabilities.detail: BSD-3-Clause; nothing closed.
Host test executables.
No Arduino or ESP fakes. You write link-time stubs, for example a ledcWrite that calls mock().actualCall("ledcWrite").withParameter(...). That is the same effort as the fff PoC. Not verified.
Not one of PlatformIO's built-in runners (Unity, GoogleTest, Doctest, custom); it would need test_framework = custom or plain CMake. Not verified.
No serial model.
No USB model.
Expectation level only.
Scripted return values through CppUMock expectations.
Mock the bus calls; no device models.
Logic only.
CMake/ctest; the -ojunit option writes JUnit XML.

The project's CI builds and tests natively on Windows with MSYS2 MINGW64 (mingw-w64-x86_64-cc + cmake, LDFLAGS -static), MSVC, ClangCL and Cygwin, and also runs a MinGW cross-build under Wine. Not run on this PC.
platforms/ has ports for CCStudio, DOS, Eclipse-Cygwin, armcc and IAR; no ESP32 or Arduino recipe was found.

candidates.fit: A capable alternative to fff + doctest, with built-in mocking and leak detection. It offers nothing ESP32-specific and is not built into PlatformIO; pick it only if the team prefers its style.
caveats: No numbered release since v4.0 (2020); master is active.
Every ESP/Arduino function needs a hand-written mock stub.

candidates.name: CMock + Unity (+ Ceedling build system)
candidates.license: MIT (CMock, Unity, Ceedling)
candidates.summary: CMock parses C headers and generates mock modules (Expect/Return/Ignore/Callback) for Unity tests. Ceedling bundles Unity, CMock and CException into a Ruby build tool. ESP-IDF uses CMock for its own host mocks.

capabilities.detail: MIT; nothing closed.
Host test executables; no ESP32 emulation.

It could generate mocks for C headers such as esp_timer.h, esp_task_wdt.h and esp32-hal-ledc.h, but those headers pull in sdkconfig/FreeRTOS/soc include chains that must be stubbed, and it cannot mock C++ classes such as HWCDC. CMock is described as being 'for unit testing C' and Ceedling as 'a build system for C projects'. Not verified.
No PlatformIO integration. PlatformIO bundles Unity but not CMock; wiring it in would need custom scripting (not verified).
No serial model.
No USB model.
Expectation level, for example ledcWrite_Expect(0, 1228), provided the header parses.
ExpectAndReturn-style scripted returns for C functions such as digitalRead.
Mocks of C I2C/SPI APIs; no device models.
The Callback/Stub plugin can capture esp_timer callbacks; logic only.
Ceedling CLI with JUnit report and gcov plugins. Needs Ruby (Ceedling requires Ruby 3+).
CMock's CI matrix includes windows-latest and Ceedling's CI has a tests-windows job. Not run here because Ruby is not installed on this PC.
No ESP32 or Arduino on-target recipe was found; the Ceedling docs include a 'Basic Porting' PDF (not evaluated).

candidates.fit: Capable for ESP-IDF C code, but it adds Ruby, header-parsing friction with the IDF/Arduino include chains, and weak C++ support. For a 350-line C++ glue file, fff or hand-written fakes are simpler. Worth considering only if the project moves to pure ESP-IDF C components.
caveats: Needs Ruby on Windows.
Mocks generated from real IDF headers need a consistent include/dependency set. ESP-IDF's own idf_component_mock handles this for its linux target by declaring REQUIRES freertos hal soc.

candidates.name: ESP-IDF 'linux' host target + CMock component mocks (+ pytest-embedded target=linux)
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (ESP-IDF); CMock/Unity MIT
candidates.latest_version: ESP-IDF v6.1 (2026-08-27; this is the docs' 'stable'). The linux target is still selected with `idf.py --preview set-target linux` and is documented as experimental.
candidates.summary: Builds an ESP-IDF app as a Linux or macOS executable on a FreeRTOS POSIX simulator. Components without a Linux port can be replaced by CMock mocks from tools/mocks. pytest-embedded can run the same pytest on target=linux, on QEMU or on hardware.

capabilities.detail: Apache-2.0; part of ESP-IDF; nothing closed.
Builds for the host 'linux' target; no S3 emulation.
Arduino-ESP32's idf_component.yml lists only chip targets (esp32, c2, c3, c5, c6, c61, h2, p4, s2, s3) and no 'linux', so the Arduino glue cannot be built for this target.
idf.py/CMake only; no PlatformIO support is documented.
The console is the host process's stdio, which the pytest-embedded 'idf' service drives. No UART or USB peripheral.
There is only a CMock mock of the IDF driver API usb_serial_jtag.h. Arduino HWCDC talks to hal/usb_serial_jtag_ll.h and its own ISR, so that mock does not apply.
LEDC is neither simulated nor mocked. The driver mock covers only SPI master, I2C (legacy), RMT, USB-serial-JTAG and GPIO.
The GPIO driver mock (CMock expectations on gpio_* calls) works for IDF-API code only.
Mocks exist for the legacy driver/i2c.h and spi_master; the new i2c_master.h driver is not in the mock list. No device models.

esp_timer is mock-only (no simulation), and task_wdt is not built for linux. esp_reset_reason() always returns ESP_RST_POWERON. esp_restart_noos() prints a message and calls exit(0); esp_system_abort() calls exit(1). The FreeRTOS simulator switches context only on kernel calls.
Build with idf.py and run the host ELF, or use pytest-embedded with target linux and Unity. Mocks need Ruby. No account.
The docs require 'a recent enough Linux or macOS version'. WSL2 was not verified.
pytest-embedded can parametrize one test over target=linux, @pytest.mark.qemu and real chips. This applies to ESP-IDF apps, not to this Arduino firmware.

candidates.fit: Not usable for this firmware today: Arduino-ESP32 cannot target linux, the target does not run natively on Windows, LEDC and TWDT are absent, and esp_timer is mock-only. It becomes relevant only if future sensor drivers are written as pure ESP-IDF components and tested under Linux or WSL.
caveats: Experimental/preview, with no API-stability guarantee (per the docs).
The mocks work on the linux target only; the source comments say 'On Espressif chips, too many dependencies are missing'.

candidates.name: Arduino-Emulator (pschatzmann) - ArduinoCore-API on the desktop
candidates.license: LGPL-2.1
candidates.latest_version: v0.2.1 (2026-08-31); last commit 2026-09-14, including Windows portability work in September 2026. library.json still says 0.1.8. Not found in the PlatformIO Registry.
candidates.summary: Runs Arduino sketches on Linux, macOS and Windows by implementing the official ArduinoCore-API. GPIO/I2C/SPI back-ends are pluggable: a no-op mock, a real microcontroller over UDP or any Stream, Raspberry Pi (gpiod, i2c-dev, spidev), FTDI FT2232HL, or Firmata. Serial goes to stdio or to a real COM port via serialib.

capabilities.detail: LGPL-2.1; nothing closed.
Runs sketches as PC programs.
ArduinoCore-API only. There is no ledc*, esp_timer, esp_task_wdt, esp_system or HWCDC member (HardwareSerial has only read(void) and no setTxTimeoutMs), so main.cpp needs extra fakes.
Ships library.json (platforms: native) and an example [env:native] with Unity. It is not in the registry, so it would be added with a lib_deps Git URL. Not run in pio here.
SerialImpl (serialib) can open a physical or virtual COM port (setDevice("COM5")), so a pyserial script could talk to it through a virtual COM pair (not verified). The default Serial is stdio.
No HWCDC or USB-Serial-JTAG model.
No LEDC API; analogWrite goes to the selected GPIO back-end.
Inputs go through a HardwareGPIO back-end (no-op mock, remote board, RPi or FTDI); no built-in test-injection API was found.
Real sensors can be reached through the remote MCU, RPi or FTDI back-ends (hardware-in-the-loop); there are no simulated devices.
No ESP-IDF timer, watchdog, restart or panic API.
CMake build; the project's CI runs on ubuntu-latest only.

The README claims Windows support and there is Windows-specific code (SocketImplWindows, ws2_32). Verified 2026-09-29: the libarduino_emulator.a library builds without errors with WinLibs g++ 16.1, CMake 4.4.1 and Ninja. Examples and tests were not run.
The sketch runs on the PC while GPIO/I2C/SPI calls can be forwarded to a real board (hardware-in-the-loop). It never flashes or runs the ESP32-S3 firmware.

candidates.fit: Interesting for running generic Arduino sketches and for PC-side hardware-in-the-loop, and it does build on Windows. But it emulates the generic Arduino API rather than Arduino-ESP32, so the glue's LEDC/esp_timer/TWDT/HWCDC calls would still need fakes. Low fit.
caveats: LGPL-2.1 brings obligations if linked binaries are distributed.
Windows support is recent and not covered by the project's CI.

candidates.name: esp32emu - ESP32/Arduino API emulator for host-side testing
candidates.license: MIT
candidates.latest_version: v1.2.0 (2026-02-18); last commit 2026-09-04. The repository started 2026-02-17 (redirected from redbasecap-buiss/esp32emu) and has 2 GitHub stars.
candidates.summary: A header-based host re-implementation of many Arduino-ESP32 and ESP-IDF APIs for macOS and Linux, with board profiles including ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1. It covers GPIO state, LEDC duty tracking, esp_timer on std::thread, FreeRTOS on threads, a task-WDT object, WiFi/WebServer on real sockets, and mocks of many sensor libraries.

capabilities.detail: MIT; nothing closed.
Does not execute firmware; it emulates APIs at source level, with an ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 profile.

Has 2.x-style ledcSetup/ledcAttachPin/ledcWrite, esp_timer, esp_task_wdt, esp_reset_reason, an esp_restart flag and esp_random. Its esp_task_wdt_init treats the first argument as ms, which matches neither IDF 4.4 (seconds) nor the 5.x config struct. Missing for main.cpp: ledcAttach (3.x), HWCDC read(buf,len)/availableForWrite/setTxTimeoutMs, esp_register_shutdown_handler, esp_rom_gpio_connect_out_signal and set_arduino_panic_handler; REG_WRITE is a no-op. Assessed from the headers; not built.
library.json declares platforms native, but it is not in the PlatformIO Registry; the main build uses Makefile/CMake. Not verified.
Serial prints to stdout; available() returns 0 and read() returns -1, and esp32emu_serial.h has no RX injection.
The README lists a USB Serial/JTAG driver mock with RX injection, but it is for the IDF driver API, not Arduino's HWCDC.
Tracks duty and frequency for 16 channels (getDuty(ch)); no waveform.
GPIOController::instance().digitalWrite(pin, v) sets the level digitalRead returns and fires attached ISRs; INPUT_PULLUP is not modelled.

Library-level mocks with state setters (AS5600, BNO08x, VL53L1X, Adafruit_VL53L1X, ESP32Encoder, ADC headers). They help only if the firmware uses those exact libraries; there is no register-level I2C.
esp_timer callbacks run on real host threads, so timing is non-deterministic. The TWDT object has feed/triggered flags. esp_restart only sets a flag. No panic or reset semantics.
make test; CI runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.
The platform badge says 'macOS | Linux'; it uses POSIX sockets and has no Windows CI.
Host-only.

candidates.fit: The closest thing to 'Arduino-ESP32 on the PC', and it even mocks the AS5600, BNO08x and VL53L1X libraries. But it is Linux/macOS-only, very new with almost no adoption, lacks Serial input and several APIs main.cpp uses, and its task-WDT semantics match neither core. Not recommended as a base; at most a source of ideas (use under WSL not verified).
caveats: Tags v0.8.0 through v1.2.0 were all created on 2026-02-18; maturity is unproven.
Timers on real threads make tests timing-dependent, unlike fake clocks.

candidates.name: EpoxyDuino (+ AUnit)
candidates.license: MIT
candidates.summary: Compiles Arduino programs and AUnit tests natively on Linux, macOS and FreeBSD through a per-sketch GNU Makefile. Serial is wired to stdin/stdout, Wire/SPI/GPIO are stubbed, and a few mock libraries are included.

capabilities.detail: MIT; nothing closed.
Runs sketches as host programs.

The API is reverse-engineered from ArduinoCore-avr. EPOXY_CORE_ESP8266 adds a few ESP8266/ESP32-like features, and the README says it does not support the ESP32's idiosyncrasies. There is no ledc*, esp_timer or esp_task_wdt (checked by grep).
Uses a GNU Makefile per sketch; not in the PlatformIO Registry.
Serial is the process's stdin/stdout (raw mode when interactive), so a Python script could drive it through pipes. No TCP or PTY built in.
No HWCDC model.
No LEDC API.
digitalReadValue(pin, val) sets what digitalRead returns; digitalWriteValue(pin) reads outputs.
Wire and SPI are mock stubs ('defined but don't do anything').
millis()/micros() come from the host clock and loop() runs every 1 ms. No ESP-IDF timer, WDT or panic API.
make + AUnit, usable in GitHub Actions; no account.
The supported environments are Linux, macOS and FreeBSD only. WSL not verified.
The same AUnit test sketches also run on real boards (AUnit is tested on AVR, SAMD21, STM32, ESP8266, ESP32 and Teensy), but they are flashed by the Arduino IDE or CLI, not by EpoxyDuino.

candidates.fit: Not a fit here: it is POSIX-only (no native Windows) and has none of the ESP32-specific APIs the glue uses. Its strength, running whole AVR-style sketches on Linux or macOS, does not cover LEDC, esp_timer, TWDT or HWCDC.
caveats: The author notes the Arduino API is inferred rather than specified.
Little activity since 2025-01.

candidates.name: arduino_ci (Arduino-CI Ruby gem)
candidates.license: Apache-2.0
candidates.latest_version: 1.6.2 (2023-06-08); no commits since
candidates.summary: Unit-tests Arduino libraries with g++ against its own mocked Arduino core, whose GODMODE state covers pins, clock, serial, SPI and Wire. It compiles library examples for real cores through arduino-cli 0.29.0.

capabilities.detail: Apache-2.0; nothing closed.
Unit tests run on the PC. Examples are only compiled, by default for esp32:esp32:featheresp32 (the classic ESP32).

The 'esp32' platform entry only adds defines (ESP32, ARDUINO_ARCH_ESP32, NUM_SERIAL_PORTS=3) to AVR-flavoured mocks; the README admits 'The Arduino library is not fully mocked, nor is avr-libc'. There are no ledc*/esp_* APIs, and it expects an Arduino library layout, not an app.
Ruby + arduino-cli; no PlatformIO integration.
Serial is modelled as GODMODE serialPort[n].dataIn/dataOut strings.
No HWCDC model.
Only an analogWrite mock.
state->digitalPin[n] = HIGH sets an input; pin 'futures' queue values for successive reads and histories record outputs.
Wire mock with per-address getMosi/getMiso deques, SPI dataIn/dataOut and observer hooks; no ready sensor models.
state->micros can be set and interrupt attach/detach is recorded, but there is no esp_timer, watchdog, restart or panic.
arduino_ci.rb CLI and a Docker-based GitHub Action. Needs Ruby 2.5+ and g++; no account.

A Windows CI workflow exists (windows-latest, Ruby 2.6). The README warns that the library symlinks it auto-creates can cause a whole linked folder to be deleted on Windows. Not run here because Ruby is not installed.
Compile-only for real cores; no upload or on-target runs.

candidates.fit: A poor fit: unmaintained since June 2023, Ruby-based and library-centric, and its mock core has none of the ESP32/ESP-IDF APIs or HWCDC. Its GODMODE helpers are neat, but fff plus a small fake layer gives the same checks on the real glue.
caveats: arduino-cli is pinned to 0.29.0.
Unmaintained: no release or commit after 1.6.2 (2023-06-08).

report.notes:
No tool in this area flashes or runs the ESP32-S3 firmware. They all compile src/main.cpp for the PC against fakes. They add to an emulator (QEMU/Wokwi, covered in other areas) and to board tests; they do not replace them. All checks were made on 2026-09-29.

What was actually run on this PC (WinLibs g++ 16.1.0 UCRT, CMake 4.4.1, Ninja). The repo and the user's PlatformIO core at D:/xetulai/_platformio/core were not changed.
(1) PoC with fff + doctest 2.5.3, in %USERPROFILE%/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--xetulai/<phiên>/scratchpad/hostglue (fakes/fake_hw.h, fakes/fake_hw.cpp, test_glue.cpp, CMakeLists.txt).
- It builds the unmodified main.cpp in three variants:
  - Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17 API, PWM off;
  - 2.0.17 API, PWM on, using a copy with fake pins 4/5/6 generated by CMake;
  - 3.x API, PWM on.
- Result: 21 test cases and 120 assertions pass (ctest 3/3, 0.38 s).
- The fakes are about 190 lines.
- The test #includes main.cpp so it can reach the anonymous-namespace state.
- It stubs __real_esp_panic_handler, which the host link needs because of the 2.x --wrap hook.
(2) PlatformIO Core 6.2.0 with an isolated PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR (scratchpad/pio_core; project in scratchpad/pio_native).
- native 1.2.1 + Unity 2.6.1: PASSED, both statically and dynamically linked.
- ArduinoFake 0.4.0 + FakeIt: PASSED.
- GoogleTest/gMock 1.17.0: PASSED.
(3) The Arduino-Emulator library builds with MinGW.

Not run:
- CMock, Ceedling and arduino_ci (Ruby is not installed).
- CppUTest.
- ESP-IDF linux target, EpoxyDuino and esp32emu (these run only on Linux/macOS).

What host tests CAN prove:
- The glue compiles against the declared API shapes for both core branches.
- Call order and arguments: LEDC setup and the duty maths (1500 us → 1228), TWDT configuration, the esp_timer name and 10 ms period, and hook registration.
- The register writes the panic/shutdown hook intends to make.
- E-stop handling and the serial/protocol path through the real core: HELLO→HELLO_ACK, 20 Hz TELEMETRY in simulated time, and dropping frames when no USB host is connected.
- Deterministic edge cases: millis wraparound, output_guard's signed difference, reset-reason mapping.

What they CANNOT prove:
- Real-time behaviour: 10 ms tick jitter, esp_timer task preemption and priority, cross-core atomics.
- That the TWDT, a panic or esp_restart actually happen, or that -Wl,--wrap and the IRAM placement work. Only the real link (objdump) and the board show this.
- Real register and LEDC effects and pulse widths, including the XTAL/APB clock change after a CPU-only reset.
- HWCDC/USB behaviour.
- GPIO electrical behaviour: pull-ups, bounce, EMI.
- I2C timing and bus errors.
- Compiler and data-model differences (Xtensa GCC 8.4 vs host GCC 16.1; 64-bit size_t on the PC).

Recommendation for this project:
- Use fff, with doctest in the existing test/host CMake flow or with Unity in a PlatformIO [env:native].
- Add GoogleTest/gMock only if the glue is refactored behind interfaces.
- Use ArduinoFake only for pure Arduino-API helpers.
- On Windows, skip arduino_ci, EpoxyDuino, esp32emu and the ESP-IDF linux target.
- If the PoC is kept, copy it into the repo; the scratchpad is session-specific.

Idea, CHƯA THỬ (not built): a host 'software-in-the-loop' build. It would run setup()/loop() on a steady_clock-based millis() and expose FakeHWCDC on a TCP port. autopark.transport's SerialVehicleIO could then connect with serial.serial_for_url('socket://127.0.0.1:PORT') and exercise the Python side end to end against the real firmware logic, on Windows, with no emulator.

Other things found:
- Arduino-ESP32's own runtime tests run only on hardware, Wokwi or QEMU; there is no official host or mock layer (https://docs.espressif.com/projects/arduino-esp32/en/latest/contributing.html).
- Generic C++ alternatives, not evaluated separately: Catch2 v3.16.0 (2026-08-25, BSL-1.0), Trompeloeil v49 (2024-10-07, BSL-1.0), FakeIt 2.5.0 (2025-11-14, MIT).

missed_facts.fact: Core 6.2.0 also fixed #5183, where the test-suite status was hard-coded as PASSED: an embedded Unity run reported '91 Tests 6 Failures' but the summary said PASSED (issue opened 2025-06-20, milestone 6.2.0). Any CI gate on 'pio test' should stay on Core 6.2.0 or later. The same release added descriptive errors for Windows long-path extraction failures (#5500).

The PlatformIO Registry itself still lists Unity 2.6.1 (2025-01-01), googletest 1.17.0 (2025-04-30) and doctest 2.4.12 (2025-04-28) as the latest versions. Getting upstream Unity 2.7.0, gtest 1.18.0 or doctest 2.5.3 in pio needs a Git URL in lib_deps or test_framework = custom, not just a version bump.

Observed locally with Core 6.2.0: a failing native Unity suite is reported as ERRORED (the program exits non-zero), and 'pio test' exits with 1. That confirms it works as a CI gate on this Windows PC.

The ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 has two USB connectors: a USB-to-UART port through an on-board bridge chip, and a separate native ESP32-S3 USB port (USB OTG/Serial-JTAG). Issue #1733 was reported on a board with native USB only. For this project, a test-only env with ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=0 could send Unity output to UART0 through the bridge port and avoid the HWCDC path. This is an inference and has not been tried.

Windows support ('Add Windows support and native PlatformIO test coverage', #24) was merged 2026-09-03, after the v0.2.1 release of 2026-08-31. Windows use therefore needs main HEAD, not a tagged release. The PlatformIO support PR (#23) landed 2026-08-31.

Arduino-ESP32's contributing guide says that in its own pytest-embedded runner 'QEMU is only supported for ESP32 and ESP32-C3 targets' and that Wokwi needs a WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN. The ESP-IDF v6.1 QEMU guide for ESP32-S3, however, says Espressif's QEMU fork supports ESP32-S3. S3 support therefore depends on the tool, which matters for the emulator part of the research.

Limits of the simulator beyond those the report lists: it uses cooperative preemption, so a task that busy-loops without FreeRTOS calls is never preempted; timing granularity is one tick (for example 10 ms at 100 Hz); and it runs single-core (configNUM_CORES = 1). A 10 ms control tick could not be judged for timing there.

The PlatformIO Registry has two more small Arduino-on-native mocking libraries the report did not cover: skaygin/ArduinoNative 0.1.4 (2022-06-27, MIT, platform native) and digitaldragon/Emulation 0.1.6 (2024-04-10, GPL-3.0-or-later, platforms espressif32/arduino). Both look low-maturity; neither was checked for ledc/esp_* or HWCDC coverage.

verification.overall:
The report holds up well. I checked about 45 claims against primary sources (GitHub API and raw files, PyPI, RubyGems, the PlatformIO registry and docs, Espressif docs) and re-ran its local evidence. Nearly every version number, date, license and capability statement was confirmed.

Local re-runs:
- A fresh rebuild of the fff + doctest PoC gives exactly 21 test cases and 120 assertions, ctest 3/3, 0 warnings, WinLibs g++ 16.1.0 and CMake 4.4.1.
- `pio test` with Core 6.2.0 passes the native, ArduinoFake and gMock suites.
- A deliberately failing Unity test makes `pio test` exit with 1.

Corrections:
1. Refuted, a precision issue only: 'the UNMODIFIED main.cpp' was compiled only in the 2.0.17 / PWM-off variant. The PWM-on variant and the only 3.x variant use a CMake copy in which the three pin constants change from -1 to 4/5/6. The 3.x branch with PWM off was never built.
2. Unclear: esp32emu v1.2.0 is a tag only; the latest GitHub Release is v1.1.0.
3. Nuance: Arduino-Emulator's Windows support landed on main on 2026-09-03, after its last release (v0.2.1).

Missed facts worth adding:
- PlatformIO 6.2.0 also fixed a bug where suites showed PASSED despite failures (#5183), so keep Core 6.2.0 or later for CI.
- The PlatformIO Registry itself still lags upstream (Unity 2.6.1, gtest 1.17.0, doctest 2.4.12).
- The DevKitC-1's separate USB-to-UART port is a possible way around issue #1733 (not tried).
- Arduino-ESP32's own test runner limits QEMU to ESP32 and ESP32-C3, while ESP-IDF's QEMU does list ESP32-S3.

None of this changes the report's feasibility conclusions:
- No host-side tool here flashes or runs the ESP32-S3 firmware.
- fff with doctest or Unity (CMake or a PlatformIO [env:native]) is the best fit on Windows.
- The ESP-IDF linux target, EpoxyDuino and esp32emu do not run natively on Windows.
- Timing, LEDC waveforms, USB CDC, the watchdog and panic behaviour still need an emulator or the board.

probe.timing_observations:
Clock:
- Emulated time follows the host wall clock (no icount), but slightly slow: device ms per host ms was 0.99898 over 120 s, 0.99911 over 30 s and 0.99832 over 300 s (1.0007 over 2 s). That is about 0.1-0.17 %, or roughly 0.5 s over 5 min.
- The device millis() is NOT reset by emulated resets. After an HMP system_reset, and across panic and esp_restart reboots, it kept counting from QEMU start (for example 864657 ms about 14.4 min after QEMU start, even though a system_reset happened about 2 min in).

Latency:
- HELLO→HELLO_ACK 1.8-13.8 ms.
- REQUEST→ACK typically 1.2-1.6 ms, max 11.1 ms.
- COMMAND→first telemetry echo at most 49.7 ms (bounded by the 50 ms telemetry period).
- Telemetry 19.97-19.99 Hz; host arrival gaps p50 50 ms, p95 about 62-72 ms, max 85-88 ms (211 ms only when the host Python process itself was starved by 32 CPU burners).

Tick-gap stalls:
- The firmware latched FAULT LOOP_OVERRUN (two control ticks more than 100 ms apart) once in about 13 min of running while I was doing PlatformIO builds and running other QEMU instances in parallel. No session was open, so the gap size is unknown.
- Controlled re-tests all gave 0 overruns: 120 s quiet host; 30 s with all 32 logical CPUs busy; 300 s with a clean+rebuild, monitor register dumps and a second QEMU start/stop.
- Largest device-side telemetry interval seen was 87 ms. Stalls over 100 ms are rare tail events, not systematic.

Boot and load:
- ROM banner about 0.06 s and app running about 0.24 s after the connect.
- Reboot after panic or restart → app answering HELLO in under about 0.4 s.
- QEMU uses about 108 % of one host core (the Arduino loop busy-spins) and 55 MB RAM; the two vCPUs run on separate host threads (MTTCG).

Watchdog:
- The real firmware's registers read via HMP: TIMG0 WDTCONFIG0=0xb81f8000, prescaler 40000, stage0=0x7d0 (1 s, interrupt), stage1=0xfa0 (2 s, system reset); TIMG1 (interrupt WDT) 300/600 ms. So on Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17, esp_task_wdt_init(1, true) does reconfigure the TWDT from the 5 s default to 1 s, at least at register level.
- QEMU never fires these watchdogs. A hung loop() in the test variant produced no TWDT message and no reset for more than 16 s.
- Cause, from QEMU source hw/timer/esp_timg.c at the release tag: stage modes and timeouts are latched only on a WDTCONFIG0 write with CONF_UPDATE_EN (bit 22). ESP-IDF's S3 HAL mwdt_ll.h never sets that bit, in IDF 4.4 (Arduino 2.0.17) and also in IDF release/v5.5 (only the C3/C6 HALs do). So the model's stages stay OFF. For Arduino 3.x this is inferred from source, not run.
- Panic path works in emulation: abort() → __wrap_esp_panic_handler is called (instrumented variant) → backtrace → RTC_SW_CPU_RST reboot → esp_reset_reason() = PANIC. The panic also wrote a core dump (about 10 KB at 0x7F0000) into the emulated flash, and QEMU persisted it to the image file.
probe.usb_serial_jtag_observation:
The esp32s3 machine contains a device `misc.esp32c3.usb_serial_jtag` at MMIO 0x60038000-0x60038083 (`info qtree` / `info mtree -f`). It has no chardev or other property: `-device misc.esp32c3.usb_serial_jtag,help` lists only a memory-region child. It is therefore a register stub with no host-side endpoint, and the docs' feature table lists USB as not supported on all targets.

Unmodified repo firmware (USB CDC on boot = 1, var_cdc, 16 MB image):
- Boots normally; UART0 shows the same ROM lines plus the core-dump E line.
- Keeps running: sampled PCs include usb_serial_jtag_sof_tick_hook, FreeRTOS critical sections, systimer and esp_pm_impl_waiti.
- A HELLO sent on UART0 got 0 bytes back (HELLO_ACK timeout).

There is no way to reach the HWCDC Serial from the host in this QEMU release. For emulation, Serial must go to UART0 (-DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=0), for example as a separate PlatformIO env; the repo was not changed.
problems: Unmodified QIO build flashed as an 8 MB image (per board) boot-loops in QEMU: app asserts at esp_system/startup.c:328 because esp_flash_init_default_chip() fails. For 8 MB images QEMU emulates a GigaDevice gd25q64 in its m25p80 model, which does not implement the quad-enable bit the QIO app sets and verifies. Evidence: the same bytes as a 16 MB image (QEMU picks ISSI is25lp128, whose QE bit works) boot fine; a DIO build (var_dio, board_build.flash_mode=dio) boots fine on the 8 MB gd25q64 image. Workaround used: --fill-flash-size 16MB with the header kept at 8MB.

USB-CDC (HWCDC / USB-Serial-JTAG) is not reachable from the host: QEMU has only a register stub with no chardev, so the unmodified repo firmware runs but cannot be talked to. The QEMU test needs ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=0 (Serial on UART0).

pyserial socket:// reports in_waiting as only 0 or 1 (select readability), so SerialVehicleIO._pump reads one byte per call. A Session-style loop (poll(block=False) + send() at 50 Hz, 2 s) received only 2 of about 40 telemetry frames, raised TELEMETRY_STALE twice, and 84 send() calls were refused. A small adapter in the test script that drains the socket and reports the real byte count (CountingPort in qemu_probe.py) fixed it: 40/40 frames, 0 errors. Blocking waits (connect/arm/_wait) worked even with plain socket://.

Timer-group watchdogs (task WDT 1 s/2 s and interrupt WDT 300/600 ms) never fire on the esp32s3 machine: QEMU latches stage config only with CONF_UPDATE_EN, which ESP-IDF's S3 HAL never sets. A hung loop() just hangs, so watchdog timeout and reset behaviour cannot be tested in this emulator. The docs still name the disable property timer.esp32c3.timg, while this release's qtree shows timer.esp32s3.timg.

Not emulated for ESP32-S3 (docs feature table; the register ranges fall into QEMU's generic esp32s3.iomem region): LEDC (ESC/servo PWM cannot be observed), GPIO matrix/IOMUX (E-stop input cannot be driven), I2C (AS5600, VL53L1X, BNO085 over I2C), GP SPI (BNO085 over SPI), RMT, USB, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, ULP. ADC and PCNT (quadrature encoder) are not in the supported list. So the future sensor drivers and the PWM/E-stop paths cannot be tested in QEMU; only UART, timers/systimer, RNG, eFuse, flash, crypto, GDMA, TWAI, SD/MMC (added for S3 in the 2026-04-17 release, although the docs table still says unsupported), OpenCores Ethernet and an RGB framebuffer are emulated.

Emulation timing is wall-clock based but not real-time guaranteed: the firmware latched FAULT LOOP_OVERRUN (control-tick gap over 100 ms) once in about 13 min while the host was busy (builds and other QEMU instances). Later 120 s, 30 s and 300 s watch windows had none (max device interval 87 ms). Emulated time ran about 0.1-0.17 % slow, and millis() is not reset by emulated resets.
QEMU writes flash changes back to the -drive image file (the test variant's panic stored a core dump at 0x7F0000-0x7F299F in img\flash_wdt_16MB.bin). Use a fresh image per test run.

Harmless log noise on every boot: 'M25P80: Read id (command 0x90/0xAB) is not supported by device', 'Unknown cmd 5a' (SFDP), 'Unknown cmd 77' (burst wrap), 'Invalid read at addr 0x10200C ... region er' (Xtensa ERI/OCD debug-status probe). On a blank coredump partition the app prints 'E (..) esp_core_dump_flash: Incorrect size of core dump image: -65536'.
