probe.summary:
Yes, it works, with conditions. The project's real firmware runs in Espressif's open-source QEMU for ESP32-S3 on this Windows machine, and the project's own Python code talks to it over the emulated serial port.

- QEMU used: the latest Windows x86_64 Xtensa build, esp-develop-9.2.2-20260417 (QEMU 9.2.2). Checksum verified, no install or admin rights needed.
- Firmware: the application code is unchanged. Only in a copy, Serial was moved from USB-CDC to UART0 (-DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=0). It was built with the pinned espressif32 7.1.3 / Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17.
- Flash image: the board-default QIO build must be written as a 16 MB image. As an 8 MB image it boot-loops, because QEMU's emulated 8 MB GigaDevice flash lacks the quad-enable bit and IDF's flash init asserts. A DIO build (8 MB) was tested and also boots.
- Protocol test through the project's SerialVehicleIO over serial_for_url('socket://127.0.0.1:5555'), all as specified:
  - HELLO_ACK: boot_id, reset_reason and limits.
  - 20 Hz telemetry with 0 frame errors.
  - ARM → ARMED.
  - COMMAND with 250 ms validity → RUNNING, then ARMED on COMMAND_TIMEOUT.
  - 500 ms host silence → DISARMED on LINK_TIMEOUT.
  - COMMAND while DISARMED → rejected with BAD_STATE.
  - A 20 Hz command stream with the correct speed ramp.
  - Reconnect keeps the same boot_id.
  - Monitor reset, test-variant abort() and esp_restart() give reset_reason POWER_ON, OTHER (panic) and SOFTWARE, and the laptop raises FIRMWARE_RESET. The panic wrap hook is really called.
- Limitations:
  - The unmodified USB-CDC build cannot be reached: QEMU has only a USB-Serial-JTAG register stub.
  - LEDC PWM, GPIO input (E-stop), I2C, SPI, ADC, PCNT and USB are not emulated, so PWM, E-stop and all planned sensor drivers still need hardware or host-side tests.
  - Timer-group watchdogs never fire on the esp32s3 model: QEMU requires CONF_UPDATE_EN, which ESP-IDF's S3 HAL never sets. Register readout does show the firmware sets the task watchdog to 1 s on Arduino 2.x.
  - Emulated time runs about 0.1-0.17 % slow and does not restart on resets. Rare host stalls over 100 ms can latch LOOP_OVERRUN (seen once in about 13 min of busy-host running; none in 7.5 min of later watch windows).
  - With pyserial socket://, in_waiting is only 0 or 1, so a non-blocking poll() loop falls behind unless an adapter is used.
- Cleanup: all six QEMU processes I started are stopped (PIDs 36564, 12044, 39352, 24024, 37100, 13920). No listeners or helper processes remain. Nothing under D:\xetulai\autopark was modified (checked by mtime; Python run with -B). No PATH or env changes and no platform installs. Disk used: about 174 MB (QEMU) + 187 MB (kiem_qemu).

missing_candidates.name: autopark's own test oracle and vehicle model: FirmwareModel, vectors.json, SimVehicleIO/SimVehicle and SerialVehicleIO(clock=...)
missing_candidates.why:
These are already in the repo, but none of the five reports or the probe uses them. The pieces:
- D:/xetulai/autopark/autopark/autopark/transport/firmware_model.py: a bit-exact integer model of vehicle_core.cpp with an injected clock.
- transport/vectors.py generates D:/xetulai/autopark/autopark/firmware/esp32_vehicle/test/vectors.json: CRC, COBS and message bytes, plus state-machine scenarios (t ms + received bytes + inputs → state/fault/reason).
- transport/loopback.py: FirmwareSerialLoopback + ManualClock.
- SimVehicleIO (vehicle_io.py:1094) runs the full loop: laptop ↔ FirmwareModel → actuators → kinematic SimVehicle → sensors.

Three uses the reports miss:
(a) Replay the vectors through the compiled Xtensa build in QEMU, esp-emu or Wokwi. Today they only check the PC build of the C++ core, and the probe judged the speed ramps by eye.
(b) Run whole parking scenarios with the emulated firmware in place of FirmwareModel.
(c) SerialVehicleIO(transport, clock=...) (vehicle_io.py:789) already accepts an injected clock. Simulated time from Wokwi or esp32sim can then drive the laptop side step by step, instead of the wall clock.

Random command sequences run against both the model and the emulator (e.g. Hypothesis) would extend (a). Vector steps with non-zero sensor inputs need an injection path (GDB or a Wokwi custom chip), because no emulator has the encoder.

missing_candidates.name: GDB/OpenOCD as one inspection and fault-injection layer for every backend (xtensa-esp32s3-elf-gdb + pygdbmi; pytest-embedded-jtag + openocd-esp32 on the real board)
missing_candidates.why:
Every backend already has a GDB stub: QEMU -s, esp-emu --gdb, Wokwi gdbServerPort or wokwi-cli -g, and later the S3's built-in USB-JTAG through openocd-esp32. The S3 GDB is already installed at D:/xetulai/_platformio/core/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp32s3/bin.

On QEMU and esp-emu, which have no pin I/O, scripted breakpoints and memory writes are the only way to:
- force the E-stop state;
- trigger abort() or a hung loop() in the production build, instead of the test-only var_wdt variant;
- read the LEDC duty and GPIO_OUT registers.
On the board, the same scripts replace a relay or logic analyzer for register-level checks. A breakpoint on the 10 ms tick is a possible lock-step method that works on every backend.

The reports mention GDB per tool only, and pytest-embedded-jtag is named but never evaluated. Caveat: halting the real CPU leaves LEDC sending the last pulse width, so run these tests with the ESC unpowered.

missing_candidates.name: Serial bridges that give emulators a real COM or RFC2217 port: com0com + hub4com with QEMU's Windows-only -serial COMn, or a user-space TCP→RFC2217 bridge (the pattern of pyserial's rfc2217_server example, or the MIT @wokwi/rfc2217 server already compiled in the scratchpad)
missing_candidates.why:
pyserial's socket:// reports in_waiting as 0 or 1. That breaks the non-blocking loop of the unmodified SerialVehicleIO on QEMU and esp-emu (--uart-tcp is raw TCP). Neither emulator serves RFC2217, so the harness report's rfc2217:// fix does not apply to them.

A bridge keeps the laptop on the same COM-port code path as the real board, with no code change. The reports mention com0com only as CHƯA THỬ. com0com needs a signed kernel driver and admin rights on this Windows 11 Enterprise PC. The practical fix may therefore be a user-space bridge, or a loop in SerialVehicleIO._pump that reads until the port is empty (D:/xetulai/autopark/autopark/autopark/transport/vehicle_io.py:856-868).

missing_candidates.name: LAVA (Linaro Automated Validation Architecture; 2026.x releases)
missing_candidates.why:
The most widely used open-source board-farm/HIL framework is missing from the harness survey, which covers labgrid, OpenHTF, Robot, tbot and HardPy.
- Runs tests on QEMU and on physical devices.
- Has MCU boot methods (OpenOCD, CMSIS-DAP, J-Link) and a generic command action for custom flashing.
- Test monitors match patterns on the serial output.

It needs a Linux server plus a dispatcher and has no ESP32/esptool-native deploy method, so it will probably be dismissed as too heavy for one board. Still, a complete answer to 'is there an open-source flash-and-test framework' should name it and say why it was dismissed.

missing_candidates.name: esp-idf-monitor (Espressif, PyPI) or PlatformIO's esp32_exception_decoder monitor filter
missing_candidates.why: Both decode panic and abort backtraces against the ELF automatically. esp-idf-monitor opens pyserial URLs (idf.py qemu monitor uses socket://localhost:5555). Panic-hook and abort tests on QEMU, esp-emu, Wokwi RFC2217 and later the board would then give readable traces. The harness report says Arduino builds must be decoded by hand with addr2line, because only pytest-embedded-idf decodes backtraces.

open_questions:
Wokwi cloud engine via wokwi-cli v0.27.1, USB-Serial-JTAG with Arduino 2.0.17 (nothing has been run on Wokwi yet):
- Does the unmodified production image (espressif32 7.1.3, QIO, 8 MB header, CDC_ON_BOOT=1) boot on board-esp32-s3-devkitc-1? Check both the default `wokwi-cli init` setup (app-only firmware.bin, Wokwi's own bootloader, default 4 MB flash) and a merged image with flashSize '8'.
- With serialInterface 'USB_SERIAL_JTAG', does HWCDC's SOF-based isPlugged() stay true, so HELLO→HELLO_ACK and 20 Hz telemetry pass byte-exact through the RFC2217 bridge?
If yes, the shipped build can be tested in simulation. If no, every simulator needs the UART0 build, and Wokwi only adds LEDC, E-stop and TWDT coverage.

Wokwi cloud, timing and quota:
- What real-time factor does an S3 simulation reach with cpuFrequency 'auto' (about 8 MHz) vs '240' for this firmware, whose loop() busy-spins?
- What is the round-trip time from Vietnam?
- Do quota minutes count simulated time only, or also wall-clock and paused time?
The RFC2217 host-in-the-loop design depends on wall-clock timeouts (laptop TELEMETRY_STALE at 0.3 s). Well below real time these fire spuriously. That would force lock-step: wokwi-client pause/resume with SerialVehicleIO(clock=simulated time). There, one WebSocket round trip per 10 ms step may make minute-long scenarios impractical within the 50 free minutes.

esp-emulator 0.44.0 in WSL2, watchdog, panic and GPIO:
- Does the S3 task WDT fire and reboot on a hung loop() (1 s on Arduino 2.x)? The 0.44.0 task_wdt fix lists only C3/C5/P4.
- Without --elf, does __wrap_esp_panic_handler run and esp_reset_reason() return PANIC? With --elf, esp-emu intercepts esp_panic_handler.
- What does an INPUT_PULLUP pin read with nothing attached? If HIGH, the PWM-enabled build (E-stop pin assigned) latches the E-stop FAULT and only GDB pokes can clear it, because host GPIO injection is only requested (issue #5).
- Will pytest-embedded-espemu gain esp32s3? Its README on main (2026-09-29) lists only c3/c5/c6/h2/p4/s31.
The answers decide whether esp-emu adds WDT and E-stop coverage over QEMU, or is just a closed-source equivalent of QEMU.

esp32sim (joakimeriksson, MIT, main 4ab7e90), USB-Serial-JTAG and host serial. It must be built from Rust source in the existing WSL2; cargo is not installed.
- Does it boot this project's 7.1.3 QIO 8 MB image? Its demo uses espressif32 6.9.0 with DIO.
- Do its WebSocket 'key'/'serial' channels pass arbitrary bytes (0x00 COBS delimiters, bytes ≥0x80) into HWCDC, and return the raw TX bytes?
- What real-time factor does the x86_64 interpreter reach? The JIT is AArch64-only.
If yes, it is the only open-source way to run the unmodified HWCDC build with a scriptable E-stop GPIO and VCD capture (it still has no LEDC and no firing TIMG WDT).

Deterministic time for replaying vectors.json (ms-exact) through the compiled Xtensa firmware:
- Does QEMU's esp32s3 machine run correctly under -icount (shift=N, sleep=off)? arduino-esp32 uses -icount only for RISC-V; on S3 it is CHƯA THỬ.
- Can a GDB breakpoint on the 10 ms control tick serve as a lock-step method on every backend? QEMU's virtual clock stops while halted; behaviour on esp-emu, Wokwi and the board is unknown.
- What step size and latency do Wokwi resume(pause_after) and esp32sim's timed scripts give?
This decides whether the existing bit-exact vectors can gate emulator runs, or only checks with tolerances are possible.

Espressif QEMU esp-develop-9.2.2-20260417, CI reliability:
- Open issue #169 shifts every runtime DIO/QIO esp_flash_read by 2 bytes. The current firmware logs only; the probe's run-2 image stayed byte-identical. What breaks once flash has content, e.g. a panic core dump read back shifted, or future Preferences/NVS data re-initialising on every boot?
- Does a DOUT build or the unmerged PR #177 avoid it?
- What caused the harness agent's 5/24 stalls after the bootloader: #169, multi-threaded TCG (#175; test -accel tcg,thread=single), or host load?
The answers decide whether QEMU can gate CI unattended or needs retries.

Wokwi engine (S3), reset and panic behaviour:
- Which esp_reset_reason() values appear after esp_restart, abort and a TWDT timeout? RTC is only partially simulated, and arduino-esp32 keeps its power_management reset-reason/TWDT test off Wokwi.
- Does the -Wl,--wrap=esp_panic_handler hook run, and do its W1TC/ENABLE_W1TS writes and esp_rom_gpio_connect_out_signal call show the ESC line going low on the logic analyzer?
- Does LEDC keep pulsing across a CPU-only reset?
If Wokwi cannot show these, the panic hook's pin effect can only be tested on hardware. Reset reasons already work in QEMU and esp-emu.

Wokwi licensing and data policy for this project:
- Does a private, unlicensed thesis repo count as 'personal non-commercial' under the ToS? That tier gives a free token and 50 CI minutes, a quota stated only in the docs; the pricing page lists CI minutes only for Pro.
- Or does it need Hobby+ or Pro? The free VS Code licence requires a public, OSI-licensed GitHub repo.
- Is uploading the firmware to Wokwi's cloud acceptable for the thesis? The self-hosted server is undocumented; on-premise is by arrangement only.
If the answer is no, Wokwi drops out. LEDC, E-stop and TWDT coverage then falls to esp32sim, GDB injection and hardware.
contradictions:
Serial transport:
- Claim: PROJECT CONTEXT says SerialVehicleIO works with any pyserial URL (socket://, rfc2217://), and the QEMU report rates host serial 'yes (20 Hz, 0 frame errors)'.
- Finding: the probe and the esp-emu verification show plain socket:// breaks the non-blocking loop. pyserial reports in_waiting as 0 or 1, and SerialVehicleIO._pump reads in_waiting bytes once per call (D:/xetulai/autopark/autopark/autopark/transport/vehicle_io.py:856-868).
  - On QEMU: 2 of about 40 telemetry frames, TELEMETRY_STALE twice, 84 refused send()s.
  - On esp-emu: TELEMETRY_STALE about 1 s after arm().
- Only blocking connect/arm/_wait calls work; the good results came from test-script adapters (CountingPort, MSG_PEEK).
- The harness report's rfc2217:// fix does not apply here: QEMU and esp-emu expose raw TCP only, and only Wokwi CLI/VS Code serve RFC2217.

esp-emulator, status and fit:
- The harness report ('espemu cannot be used: RISC-V only') and the Wokwi verification rely on pytest-embedded-espemu. Its README on main still lists only c3/c5/c6/h2/p4/s31 (checked 2026-09-29).
- The QEMU report rates esp-emu 'no' on Windows and 'CHƯA THỬ' for Arduino.
- In fact, the esp-emu binary supports S3 since 0.43.0 (2026-09-18). The 'others' verification ran this project's Arduino 2.0.17 build in the WSL2 already installed here: full protocol over --uart-tcp, correct POWER_ON/SOFTWARE reset reasons.
Conversely, the QEMU report (a trial 'focused on HWCDC and TWDT') and the 'others' report ('watchdog smoke tests') overstate it:
- App-mode HWCDC is unreachable; the TCP bridge carries USB-Serial-JTAG only in ROM download strap 0x04.
- S3 TWDT firing has not been shown.
- With --elf, the emulator intercepts esp_panic_handler.

QEMU flash-image recipe:
- Harness report: a DIO build is required.
- Harness verification: padding the unmodified QIO image to 16 MB is enough.
- Probe and QEMU report: '16 MB or DIO', and 'Incorrect size of core dump image: -65536' is harmless noise.
- QEMU verification: that exact message is a symptom of open issue #169 (runtime DIO/QIO flash reads shifted by 2 bytes; the fix is in unmerged PR #177). Both recipes therefore fix boot only. 4 MB images (gd25q32, the size in Espressif's own docs example) hit the same quad-enable gap.
Still unknown: whether DOUT avoids #169.

pytest-embedded-qemu on Windows:
- The QEMU report rates it 'unknown' (the eFuse helper uses pexpect.spawn; CHƯA THỬ).
- The harness report ran it on this Windows 11 PC: an S3 image booted, the QMP hard reset worked, and a PlatformIO Unity image gave per-case JUnit results in 4 of 4 runs.
Only the --qemu-efuse-path path remains untested.

HWCDC in simulation:
- The harness report says Wokwi with --wokwi-usb-serial-jtag 'is the only backend that can exercise the unmodified HWCDC protocol ... today' and 'should be usable'.
- The Wokwi report calls 2.0.17 HWCDC on Wokwi its biggest unknown: HWCDC transmits only while the SOF tick hook sees SOF, and the passing IDF USB-Serial-JTAG test never exercises that check.
- Both verifications rate it 'unclear', and nothing was run on Wokwi.
- Meanwhile esp32sim documents its USB-Serial/JTAG as 'full (IDF console and Arduino Serial)'. Its demo is a PlatformIO Arduino 2.0.17 build for esp32-s3-devkitc-1 with USB_MODE=1 and CDC_ON_BOOT=1 (confirmed by the verification). danish9661's emulator also claims a USB-Serial-JTAG CDC model.
So 'only Wokwi' is not established either way.

QEMU boot reliability and time base:
- The harness agent saw 5 of 24 DIO-build boots stall after the bootloader's 'entry' line on a loaded host.
- The probe saw no boot stalls (app up about 0.24 s after connect, reboots under 0.4 s), but one LOOP_OVERRUN in about 13 min under load.
- The QEMU verification points to open issue #175: esp32s3 SIGSEGV under the default multi-threaded TCG when the host is busy.
These are not reconciled. The time bases also differ:
- QEMU follows the host clock (about 0.998×).
- esp-emu runs virtual time at about 0.47–0.62× wall clock.
- Wokwi keeps exact peripheral timing but caps the CPU at about 8 MHz by default.
So the same wall-clock timeouts on the laptop side do not transfer between backends.

a159x36/qemu:
- The QEMU report dismissed it partly for having 'no binary assets / no Windows binaries'.
- Its verification refutes this: v5.1.11–v5.4.1 ship win64, Linux and macOS tarballs.
It is then the only freely downloadable, native-Windows, GPL S3 QEMU build found with GPIO, LEDC and I2C models. Its gaps were never tested: no documented pin-injection API, inputs wired to the T-Display buttons on GPIO0/GPIO14, and the same USB-JTAG stub and WDT latch as Espressif QEMU. For example, can QMP/HMP toggle those button lines or read LEDC state? If so, it would be an open-source path for E-stop and PWM tests.

The reports disagree on the primary recommendation and blur the user's 'open-source' criterion:
- QEMU report: Espressif QEMU is 'the best open-source, free, native-Windows option'.
- Harness report: Wokwi leads, and QEMU is 'only useful for UART0 variant builds'.
- Wokwi report: 'only Wokwi' covers LEDC + GPIO + esp_timer + TWDT + host serial + automation; its verification calls this unverifiable.
- 'Others' verification: esp-emulator 'should now come first' within its area.
By licence: Wokwi's engine and the esp-emu binary are closed (esp-emu's source decision is pending, issue #10), and Velxio's engine source is behind a licence key. The only open-source S3 emulators with evidence of running Arduino firmware are Espressif QEMU (proven here) and esp32sim (documented, not tried here). The final answer needs a ranking per test goal, not a single winner.

answers.question: Missing candidate: autopark's own test oracle and vehicle model (FirmwareModel, vectors.json, SimVehicleIO/SimVehicle, SerialVehicleIO(clock=...))
answers.answer:
Verdict: this is the strongest missing piece. Use it as the pass/fail oracle for every emulator, instead of judging speed ramps by eye.

Repo facts (checked 2026-09-29):
- SimVehicleIO is at vehicle_io.py:1094 and SerialVehicleIO(transport, *, clock=...) at vehicle_io.py:789. ManualClock and FirmwareSerialLoopback are in loopback.py.
- vectors.json holds 10 scenarios / 616 steps, plus 5 CRC, 11 COBS, 13 message and 11 stream vectors.
- Inputs used by the steps: speed_valid (179 steps), speed_mm_s (108), estop (6). Four scenarios need inputs: estop_latch, limits_reverse_interlock_speed_loop, effort_cap_and_stall, disarm_and_hello_keep_boot_and_fault.
- Every scenario sends at least one rx byte >= 0x80.
- clock_wrap_and_loop_overrun starts at boot_ms=4294967090.
- boot_id is fixed (1592594996). The firmware uses esp_random(), which differed between two otherwise identical QEMU -icount runs.

(a) Replaying the vectors on the compiled Xtensa firmware:
- esp32sim WebAssembly build (tested today): its C ABI esp32sim_run(emu, cycles) steps an exact number of cycles, so bytes can be injected at an exact firmware millisecond. The production HWCDC image emitted frames exactly every 50.000 ms emulated.
- Blocker: esp32sim's host serial channel is JSON text. Host→device bytes >= 0x80 cannot be sent, and device→host bytes pass through from_utf8_lossy. A small patch is needed first, e.g. a hex/base64 serial event; the C6 'cooja' mode already hex-encodes serial.
- QEMU: -icount gives deterministic guest time. Injection must then be driven by GDB or QMP stop/continue, not by wall-clock TCP writes.
- Masking and injection:
  - Mask the boot_id field or poke it with GDB.
  - clock_wrap needs millis() near 2^32, so it needs time injection; keep it on the PC build.
  - read_inputs() in main.cpp hard-codes every *_valid=false, so the four input scenarios need a GDB poke or a test-hook build.
  - E-stop steps can use esp32sim 'btn', a159x36 'sendkey', or GDB.
- Replayable without injection: boot_arm_run_timeout_link_loss, sequence_and_session_rules, garbage_on_link, telemetry_period_not_multiple_of_tick, tx_overflow_gap. tx_overflow depends on HWCDC FIFO timing, so expect differences there.

(b) Whole parking scenarios:
- Add an EmulatedFirmwareIO (a VehicleIO subclass) that drives esp32sim-wasm through a Node subprocess.
- Actuator values must come from telemetry fields (effort_permille, steer_ref), at 20 Hz, because esp32sim has no LEDC waveform. The alternative is reading g_core outputs through GDB.
- Sensor feedback needs an injection path until the drivers exist.

(c) The clock parameter already exists. Feed it emulated seconds (esp32sim cycles / 240e6, or the simulated nanoseconds reported by Wokwi). This removes spurious wall-clock TELEMETRY_STALE.

Hypothesis is not installed in .venv, so it would be a new dev dependency. Run random differential tests mainly model vs PC-built core (cheap), and only a sample on an emulator.

answers.question: Missing candidate: GDB/OpenOCD as one inspection and fault-injection layer (xtensa-esp32s3-elf-gdb + pygdbmi; pytest-embedded-jtag + openocd-esp32)
answers.answer:
Worth adding as a common layer, with clear limits.

Verified today:
- The PlatformIO toolchain GDB is present: GNU gdb 9.2.90 (crosstool-NG esp-2021r2-patch5).
- It attaches to Espressif QEMU 9.2.2's gdbstub on Windows with `-gdb tcp::5823` and `target remote :5823`. The form `target remote 127.0.0.1:5813` failed with 'undocumented errno 138'.
- Both cores show up as threads, and RAM writes work (r_boots 0 → 77).
- On Espressif QEMU the GPIO and LEDC registers read 0 because there are no models, so register-level checks are meaningless there.
- a159x36 QEMU does expose LEDC state: HMP `xp /4wx 0x60019000` returned conf0=0x14, duty=0x4cc0.

Documented, not tested here:
- esp-emu 0.44.0: `--gdb PORT` and `--gdb-halt`, 'enough for scripted fault injection (breakpoint + set var=... + continue)'.
- Wokwi: `wokwi-cli -g/--gdb-server-port` or `gdbServerPort` in wokwi.toml; the simulation starts paused.
- Board: openocd-esp32 v0.12.0-esp32-20260831 (published 2026-09-03, win64 zip) with the S3's built-in USB-JTAG.
- pytest-embedded-jtag 2.9.3 (2026-08-31) provides openocd and gdb fixtures.
- pygdbmi 0.11.0.0 is from 2023-01-29; old, but GDB/MI is stable.

Caveats:
- ESP-IDF docs: OpenOCD disables the hardware timers of both the task and interrupt watchdogs at every breakpoint and does not re-enable them. So watchdog tests are invalid while OpenOCD is attached.
- On the board, LEDC keeps pulsing and HWCDC is not serviced while halted. Keep the ESC unpowered and expect TELEMETRY_STALE on the laptop.
- On Espressif QEMU and a159x36, a GDB-forced hang cannot test the TWDT, because their TIMG watchdogs never fire with Arduino 2.0.17 (measured). The abort() path does work: the hook ran and printed.

Good uses:
- Force the E-stop by poking Inputs, or the pin where it is modelled.
- Trigger abort() in the unmodified production build.
- Read core state.

Lock-step on the 10 ms tick:
- QEMU pauses its virtual clock while the VM is halted.
- esp32sim does not need it: it steps exact cycle counts natively.
- esp-emu and Wokwi: unknown.
- Board: not deterministic.

answers.question: Missing candidate: serial bridges giving emulators a real COM/RFC2217 port (com0com+hub4com with QEMU -serial COMn, or a user-space TCP→RFC2217 bridge)
answers.answer:
Verified today: a zero-code user-space bridge works, with no driver and no admin rights.

How it works:
- pyserial 3.5's examples/rfc2217_server.py opens its port with serial.serial_for_url(...). It therefore accepts a socket:// URL.
- Command used: `python rfc2217_server.py -p 2218 socket://127.0.0.1:5594`, placed in front of Espressif QEMU's raw TCP UART0. The firmware was this project's UART0 build (flash_uart0_16MB.bin).

Results (10 s runs):
- Over `rfc2217://127.0.0.1:2218`, the unmodified SerialVehicleIO non-blocking loop (poll(block=False), send() at 20 Hz) got 200/200 telemetry frames, 200/200 sends and 0 safety events.
- The same loop over plain `socket://` got only 73 of ≈200 frames. The backlog grows, and frames look fresh because age is stamped on receipt, so this is a hidden latency hazard.
- Root cause, from the pyserial 3.5 source: protocol_socket.in_waiting returns len(select(...)), i.e. 0 or 1. rfc2217.in_waiting returns the queued count.

One required code change:
- pyserial's rfc2217 client raises NotImplementedError('write_timeout is currently not supported').
- SerialVehicleIO.open()/_port_opener passes write_timeout=0.05, so it cannot open rfc2217:// unchanged.
- Either build the transport without write_timeout, or special-case URLs in _port_opener.

Alternatives:
1. Loop in SerialVehicleIO._pump until in_waiting==0 (vehicle_io.py:856-868). Small code change; reads 1 byte per call on socket://.
2. com0com + hub4com with QEMU's Windows-only `-serial COMn`:
   - Needs admin rights and a kernel driver.
   - SourceForge threads report the 'signed' com0com 3.0.0.0 package rejected under Secure Boot on Windows 11 (Code 52).
   - Pete Batard's signed 2.2.2.0 x64 build is reported to still load.
   - CHƯA THỬ on this PC.

Recommendation: the pyserial bridge, or the one-line pump loop. It serves QEMU, a159x36 QEMU and esp-emu (WSL2 --uart-tcp) alike.

answers.question: Missing candidate: LAVA (Linaro Automated Validation Architecture, 2026.x)
answers.answer:
Name it in the survey, then dismiss it for this project.

Facts (checked 2026-09-29):
- Latest tag is 2026.09 (2026-09-14). Releases were roughly monthly from 2026.01 to 2026.09.
- The install docs cover Debian only (bookworm stable, trixie, sid). There is no Windows dispatcher.
- Boot methods include cmsis-dap, jlink, openocd, pyocd, qemu, docker, fvp, avh and minimal.
- There is no ESP32 or esptool deploy/boot method.
  - Flashing an S3 would need the `command` action: dispatcher-side commands pre-defined in the device dictionary, e.g. esptool.
  - Test checks would use the `monitors` action: regex on START/STOP markers in non-interactive output. The binary COBS protocol does not fit this, so a Python harness is needed anyway.

Why dismiss:
- LAVA needs a Linux server, a dispatcher, device dictionaries and power control. That is too heavy for one board and a thesis.
- What its qemu boot would give is already covered by pytest-embedded-qemu, which works on this Windows PC.
- Revisit only if a multi-board farm appears. labgrid remains the lighter board-farm option.

answers.question: Missing candidate: esp-idf-monitor (PyPI) or PlatformIO's esp32_exception_decoder filter
answers.answer:
Verified: esp-idf-monitor decodes Arduino 2.0.17 panics from a pyserial URL on Windows.
- Version 1.10.0 (PyPI 2026-09-03), installed in a scratch venv on D:.
- Command: `python -m esp_idf_monitor --port socket://127.0.0.1:5701 --no-reset --toolchain-prefix xtensa-esp32s3-elf- --target esp32s3 firmware.elf`, run against Espressif QEMU with a probe build that calls abort().
- It printed '--- 0x420021b3: loop() at …/src/main.cpp:248', then decoded panic_abort, esp_system_abort, abort and loopTask with source lines.
- Relevant options: --decode-panic backtrace and --decode-coredumps info.
- So the harness report's 'only pytest-embedded-idf decodes; decode Arduino by hand' is wrong.

PlatformIO's esp32_exception_decoder filter with `pio device monitor --port socket://…` is documented (URL handlers are supported) but CHƯA THỬ.

Important for this firmware — where the panic text appears:
- The Arduino 2.0.17 S3 sdkconfig (local SDK header) sets CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_UART_DEFAULT=1, CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_SECONDARY_USB_SERIAL_JTAG=1 and CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_ENABLE_TO_FLASH=1.
- So panic/boot text goes to UART0 and also to the USB-Serial-JTAG CDC. In esp32sim the ROM/bootloader text of the production image did appear on the USB stream.
- On the real board, backtraces will therefore be interleaved with the binary COBS stream on the laptop's COM port, and will show up as COBS/CRC errors. Run esp-idf-monitor on UART0 (the DevKitC UART port) instead.
- On QEMU and esp-emu only UART0 is bridged, so it carries the panic text.

Core dumps:
- Unreadable on QEMU QIO builds (#169).
- After abort(), QEMU-DIO and esp-emu both report 'Core dump data check failed' (not investigated).

answers.question: Open question: Wokwi cloud (wokwi-cli v0.27.1) + USB-Serial-JTAG with Arduino 2.0.17 — does the unmodified production image boot and does HWCDC pass HELLO/HELLO_ACK and 20 Hz telemetry through RFC2217?
answers.answer:
Still unknown; not run.
- Running it needs a WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN and uploads the firmware to Wokwi's cloud. That upload is the user's decision (see the licensing question).
- The latest CLI is v0.27.1 (2026-09-16).

What the sources settle:
1. SOF dependency: HWCDC.cpp at tag 2.0.17 installs a FreeRTOS tick hook.
   - The hook reads USB_SERIAL_JTAG.int_raw.sof_int_raw on every tick.
   - Without SOF for more than 5 ticks, isPlugged() returns false and `Serial` becomes false.
   - The firmware's flush_tx() then calls tx_clear(), and write() only fills a ring buffer.
   - So Wokwi passes only if its USJ model raises SOF at ≥1 kHz of simulated time.
   - esp32sim's model does exactly that (SOF 4×/ms), and the build works there (verified today). esp-emu issue #11 reports SOF permanently asserted (on C6).
2. No public evidence either way:
   - arduino-esp32's Wokwi validation tests (master 6cddb19, 2026-09-29) all use UART0 ($serialMonitor); none sets serialInterface USB_SERIAL_JTAG.
   - Wokwi's own USJ test binary uses the IDF driver, which does not exercise the SOF check.
3. Flash size:
   - IDF 4.4 aborts at boot when the detected flash is smaller than the size in the bootloader header ('Detected size … smaller than the size in the binary image header … Probe failed').
   - The production bootloader header says 8 MB (byte 3 = 0x3f), so a merged image needs flashSize "8".
   - The default app-only setup (Wokwi's bootloader, 4 MB) should boot if Wokwi's bootloader header says ≤4 MB. CHƯA THỬ.

Decisive test (≈10 s simulated, <1 quota minute):
- Diagram: board-esp32-s3-devkitc-1 with attrs {flashSize:'8', serialInterface:'USB_SERIAL_JTAG'}, and the merged image.
- Send an ASCII-safe HELLO; the frame exists: 04 01 01 01 01 01 02 01 02 32 01 01 01 01 03 02 77 00 (session 1, seq 1, 50 ms).
- Expect a HELLO_ACK. If the ROM banner appears but no HELLO_ACK, SOF is not modelled.

The decision this answer was meant to drive is moot: esp32sim already shows the shipped HWCDC build can be tested in simulation, so Wokwi is not required for it.

answers.question: Open question: Wokwi cloud timing and quota (real-time factor with cpuFrequency auto vs 240, RTT from Vietnam, what quota minutes count, lock-step cost)
answers.answer:
Partly answered from the docs; nothing was measured on Wokwi itself.

Speed:
- guides/esp32: cpuFrequency 'auto' caps the simulated CPU at about 8 MHz. Peripheral timing is unaffected. 'max' makes the simulation 'much slower'.
- No published real-time factor exists for the S3. For this busy-spinning loop(), the cap only reduces loop iterations per ms. Actual speed: CHƯA ĐO.

Quota:
- wokwi-ci/getting-started: 'The simulation time is calculated as the sum of the simulation time of all the tests'. Limits: Free 50, Hobby/Hobby+ 200, Pro 2000 minutes per month.
- The CLI --timeout is in simulation milliseconds.
- So quota counts simulated time. Paused wall-clock time is not simulation time, although the docs do not say so explicitly.

RTT:
- wokwi.com resolves to Cloudflare (104.26.12.166/104.26.13.166).
- From this PC: TCP connect 0.14–0.37 s warm (1.43 s cold), TLS about +0.08 s, i.e. an edge RTT of about 80–130 ms.
- The location of the simulation origin is unknown. The WebSocket round trip itself: CHƯA ĐO.

Lock-step:
- wokwi-client 0.4.0 (PyPI 2026-02-19) source has resume_simulation(pause_after=<ns>), pause_simulation(), serial_write(bytes), set_control() and read_pin(). So lock-step with SerialVehicleIO(clock=simulated time) is possible.
- Cost: a 60 s scenario at 10 ms steps is 6000 round trips, roughly 10–20+ min wall at 0.1–0.2 s each, but only ≈1 quota minute. Stepping per laptop event (50 ms) cuts that about 5×.

Local alternatives with the same lock-step property and no quota:
- esp32sim wasm: exact cycle steps; 0.69× real time with JIT on this PC.
- QEMU -icount: deterministic; ≈1.35× real time.

answers.question: Open question: esp-emulator 0.44.0 in WSL2 — does the S3 TWDT fire on a hung loop(), does the panic hook run without --elf and give PANIC, what does an unconnected INPUT_PULLUP read, will pytest-embedded-espemu gain esp32s3?
answers.answer:
Measured today:
- esp-emu 0.44.0 in WSL2.
- Probe sketch built with the project's own toolchain: espressif32 7.1.3, Arduino 2.0.17, -Wl,--wrap=esp_panic_handler, UART0 console, 8 MB QIO image, --uart-tcp.

1. TWDT: yes, it fires on a hung loop().
   - Output: 'task_wdt: Task watchdog got triggered … loopTask (CPU 1) … Aborting.'
   - This came ≈1.2 s guest after the hang (2.46 s wall at the measured 0.476× rate).
   - The IWDT fires too: 'Interrupt wdt timeout on CPU1'.
   - Side finding: the IDF 4.4 header says esp_task_wdt_init() updates timeout and panic mode when the TWDT is already initialised. The probe got ESP_OK, and QEMU's TIMG0 registers show 1 s. The main.cpp comment that the call 'returns an error and keeps 5 s' is wrong.
2. Panic hook without --elf: the hook runs, but reset reasons are wrong.
   - __wrap_esp_panic_handler printed its message, and its GPIO-matrix writes are visible (outsel21=0x100, ENABLE bit 21 set).
   - Every firmware-initiated reset reboots as rst:0x9 RTCWDT_SYS_RST after about 5 s wall: abort, TWDT, IWDT and esp_restart().
   - esp_reset_reason() is therefore WDT(7), never PANIC, TASK_WDT, INT_WDT or SW.
   - The earlier 'correct SOFTWARE reason' came from the host control command `reset --soft`, not from esp_restart().
   - With --elf, esp-emu logs 'Panic intercept' for abort/esp_panic_handler and 'Firmware abort on hart1', then stops. No hook runs and there is no reboot.
3. INPUT_PULLUP with nothing attached reads HIGH.
   - INPUT_PULLDOWN and floating pins read HIGH too (GPIO_IN=0xffffffff).
   - With kEstopActiveLow=false, the PWM-enabled build would latch the E-stop FAULT.
   - Host pin injection does not exist yet (issue #5 open, no maintainer reply), so only GDB pokes remain.
4. pytest-embedded-espemu: no S3 support yet.
   - The README on main lists c3/c5/c6/h2/p4/s31.
   - Commits on 2026-09-25 added esp32c5, eFuse images and dut.serial.
   - No S3 and no public roadmap, so the answer is unknown. PyPI has 2.9.3 (2026-08-31).

Other observations:
- LEDC registers are modelled: ledcSetup works and duty reads back 0x4cc0, but pin 21 never toggles.
- No #169 flash problem: all six read modes are correct and NVS persists.

Verdict: esp-emu adds TWDT/IWDT firing, which QEMU never provides. But its reset reasons are wrong, it has no E-stop injection, it is a closed binary and it runs on Linux/WSL only at 0.48× real time.

answers.question: Open question: esp32sim (joakimeriksson, MIT, 4ab7e90) — does it boot this project's 7.1.3 QIO 8 MB image, do its WebSocket key/serial channels pass arbitrary bytes into HWCDC and return raw TX, what real-time factor on x86_64?
answers.answer:
Resolved without building Rust.
- The project's GitHub Pages serves the WebAssembly build of main 4ab7e90: esp32sim.wasm, Last-Modified 2026-09-23 19:09 GMT, plus the S3 ROM ELF.
- Its C ABI runs under Node v26 on this Windows PC. Runner: simrun.mjs.

1. Boot: yes.
   - The unmodified production build (bootloader.bin/partitions.bin/firmware.bin from the repo's .pio build: 7.1.3, QIO bootloader, 8 MB header, CDC_ON_BOOT=1) boots.
   - The QIO probe image also boots, with correct flash reads in all modes and NVS persisting.
2. HWCDC: yes.
   - A HELLO was injected at t=1.000 s. The firmware answered over USB-Serial-JTAG: 102 frames in 5 s, the first 10 ms after HELLO, then exactly every 50.000 ms (20 Hz telemetry).
   - The source shows why: the USJ model raises SOF 4×/ms while connected (the default), so isPlugged() stays true.
3. Arbitrary bytes: no, not without a patch.
   - Host→device 'key' carries a JSON string, which is sent as UTF-8. 0x00 works (the \u0000 delimiter arrived). Bytes 0x80–0xFF cannot be sent.
   - Device→host goes through String::from_utf8_lossy. All 102 HELLO_ACK/TELEMETRY frames (types 0x81/0x83) arrived containing U+FFFD.
   - The native CLI writes raw bytes to stdout (--console usb), but its input is text only (--serial, --script).
   - Fix: a small patch (a hex/base64 serial event, as the C6 cooja mode already does). The MIT licence allows it.
4. Speed on this PC:
   - wasm with its WebAssembly JIT: 0.69–0.70× real time (≈165 Minsn/s), for both the busy-looping firmware and the probe.
   - wasm interpreter (--nojit): 0.36× (88 Minsn/s).
   - A hung while(true){} dropped to 0.003×.
   - The native x86_64 interpreter was not measured: no Rust toolchain, and C: now has only 3.6 GB free.

Also measured with the probe:
- esp_restart → RTC_SW_CPU_RST, reason SW; the shutdown handler ran.
- GPIO injection works: a 'btn' on pin 14 made it read 0.
- All inputs default HIGH, even with INPUT_PULLDOWN.
- LEDC registers are accepted (ledcSetup works) but the pin shows no waveform.
- A hung loop ran 9 s emulated with no reset: the TIMG TWDT is not modelled.
- Arduino HardwareSerial on UART0 never receives single bytes (only RXFIFO_FULL is modelled, no RX timeout). UART0 test builds therefore cannot take commands.

Verdict: the only open-source path verified to run the unmodified HWCDC build, with scriptable GPIO and cycle-exact lock-step. It needs the serial patch for byte-exact protocol tests, and has no LEDC waveform and no TWDT.

answers.question: Open question: deterministic time for replaying vectors.json through the compiled Xtensa firmware (QEMU -icount on esp32s3, GDB-breakpoint lock-step, Wokwi/esp32sim step sizes)
answers.answer:
1. QEMU -icount works on esp32s3.
   - Setup: Espressif QEMU 9.2.2, DIO probe image, `-icount shift=3,sleep=off`.
   - 2/2 runs booted, and esp_restart rebooted fine.
   - Guest timestamps were identical across the two runs until the first host byte arrived: T lines at 1569002, 2569010, 3569017, 4569019 and 5569365 µs, with identical esp_timer callback counts.
   - After host input the runs diverge, because TCP input lands at a wall-clock-dependent guest time.
   - The guest ran at ≈1.35× real time.
   - esp_random() differed between runs (host RNG), so boot_id must be masked.
2. GDB-breakpoint lock-step:
   - QEMU: works in principle. The VM clock stops while halted, and GDB attach plus RAM poke is verified on Windows. Injection must happen while stopped.
   - esp32sim: not needed. The wasm ABI esp32sim_run(emu, cycles) advances an exact number of cycles and applies inputs at step boundaries. With 10 ms steps, telemetry came at exactly 50.000 ms.
   - esp-emu: behaviour while halted is unknown. It has no lock-step API; issue #5 asks for sim-time lock-step.
   - Wokwi: behaviour while halted is unknown.
   - Board: not deterministic, because USB, LEDC and timers keep running.
3. Step sizes:
   - Wokwi resume(pause_after) takes simulated nanoseconds (wokwi-client 0.4.0 source); each step costs one WebSocket round trip. Not run.
   - esp32sim wasm: any cycle count.
   - esp32sim CLI --script: actions at emulated seconds (float).

Consequence:
- Bit-exact vectors can gate emulator runs on esp32sim once the serial patch is in, and on QEMU with icount plus GDB/QMP-controlled injection.
- Otherwise, use tolerance checks.
- In every case, 4 of the 10 scenarios (sensor or E-stop inputs) and clock_wrap need GDB or a test hook.

answers.question: Open question: Espressif QEMU esp-develop-9.2.2-20260417 CI reliability (#169 effects, DOUT/PR #177, cause of the 5/24 boot stalls)
answers.answer:
Measured with a probe that compares esp_flash_read() in every read mode against the memory-mapped partition table.

#169 effects:
- In the QIO build, only quad-I/O reads (0xEB) are shifted: SLOWRD, FASTRD, DOUT, DIO and QOUT are correct, QIO is shifted +2 (00 00 aa 50 …). This is exactly #169's root cause.
- In the DIO build, the default DIO read is correct, but FASTRD/DOUT/QOUT read −1 and QIO +4. So only the build's own read mode is safe.
- What breaks in the QIO build:
  - NVS/Preferences never persist: the counter reads 0 on every boot.
  - Core dumps read back as garbage: 'Incorrect size of core dump image: -65536' on every boot, and '688128000' after a panic.
- The DIO build is fine: NVS persists (0→1→2) and there is no '-65536' message. After abort it reports 'Core dump data check failed', also seen on esp-emu (not investigated).

DOUT and PR #177:
- DOUT would avoid #169 at runtime, but Arduino 2.0.17's precompiled S3 libraries exist only as dio_qspi/qio_qspi (plus opi variants). PlatformIO maps qio to a DIO header only.
- A DIO build is therefore the practical fix.
- PR #177 (fix the dummy-cycle count across lanes) is still open.

Boot stalls:
- With the default accelerator (MTTCG), 2 of 7 DIO boots ended with a host QEMU SIGSEGV during boot. This is #175's signature, and to a TCP client it looks like a stall or reset after the bootloader.
- With -accel tcg,thread=single, 6/6 boots worked, but 3/3 software resets (esp_restart, abort) never came back.
  - The guest hit 'unrecognized opcode in slot 0 (pc = 4200cba0)' and about 658k invalid writes, then QEMU segfaulted.
- -icount (also single-threaded) restarted fine 2/2.

Also found:
- QEMU's TIMG watchdogs never fire with Arduino 2.0.17: no reset after 25–44 s of hang, in both flash modes, for the TWDT and the IWDT.
- ledcSetup() panics with IntegerDivideByZero in ledc_get_freq, because there is no LEDC model. The PWM-enabled build would crash-loop in Espressif QEMU.

Verdict: QEMU can gate CI unattended only with:
- DIO builds;
- automatic retry when the QEMU process dies (or -icount);
- UART0 builds with PWM off;
- no watchdog tests.

answers.question: Open question: Wokwi engine (S3) reset and panic behaviour (esp_reset_reason after esp_restart/abort/TWDT, panic-hook pin effect on the logic analyzer, LEDC across CPU reset)
answers.answer:
Unknown for Wokwi; not run.

Indirect evidence:
- The Wokwi docs list S3 'Watchdog ✔️' but 'RTC 🟡 only RTC pull-up/pull-down'. esp_reset_reason() depends on the RTC_CNTL reset cause and the STORE6 hint register.
- arduino-esp32 master (6cddb19, 2026-09-29) marks two tests `platforms: wokwi: false, qemu: false`, i.e. hardware only:
  - tests/validation/power_management (reset reason plus TWDT);
  - adc_pwm.
- Its gpio and i2c_master tests, by contrast, run only on Wokwi.
- The panic hook's pin effect could in principle be seen with Wokwi's logic analyzer (--vcd-file). CHƯA THỬ.

Comparison measured today with the same probe:
- a159x36 QEMU v5.4.1:
  - SW(3) after esp_restart and PANIC(4) after abort, both correct.
  - The hook ran and its GPIO-matrix write took effect.
  - LEDC registers survived the CPU reset, which is what main.cpp assumes silicon does.
- Espressif QEMU: SW and PANIC correct and the hook ran, but GPIO and LEDC are not modelled.
- esp-emu: the hook ran and the register writes are visible, but every reason reads WDT.
- esp32sim: SW correct, but LEDC registers were cleared by the CPU reset.

Conclusion:
- The hook's register-level effect can already be checked on a159x36 (open source, native Windows) and on esp-emu.
- Waveform-level proof that the ESC line goes low (and stays low across the reset) needs either Wokwi (only if the cloud upload is accepted, and untested) or hardware with a logic analyzer.

answers.question: Open question: Wokwi licensing and data policy (private thesis repo = personal non-commercial? Hobby+/Pro needed? acceptable to upload firmware?)
answers.answer:
Documentation and ToS (checked 2026-09-29):
- ToS: 'You may use the Service for your personal non-commercial purposes only'.
- The VS Code extension is free only for open-source projects, defined as public on GitHub, OSI-licensed and not commercialized.
- Pricing page:
  - Community: free, 'for open source projects'.
  - Hobby: ~$5.6/mo, personal, no VS Code.
  - Hobby+: ~$8.1/mo, includes Wokwi for VS Code.
  - Pro: $20/seat/mo, commercial, 2000 CI minutes.
- CI docs: Free 50, Hobby/Hobby+ 200, Pro 2000 minutes of simulation time. The CLI token is created on the CI dashboard, which a free account can use.
- Data: the firmware is uploaded to the cloud server and is 'not stored… deleted after the simulation'. On-premise deployment is 'contact us'.
- A Docker image wokwi/wokwi-ci-server exists. The wokwi-ci-server-action uses it in GitHub Actions; its Docker Hub page has no description, and tags are daily up to 20260927. Terms for self-hosting it outside GitHub Actions are not documented.

What the sources cannot settle:
- Whether a private university thesis counts as 'personal non-commercial' is a policy/legal decision for the student and supervisor, possibly with Wokwi by email. For the same reason, no firmware was uploaded to Wokwi in this session.

If the upload is not acceptable, Wokwi drops out, and coverage becomes:
- HWCDC, E-stop injection, lock-step: esp32sim (MIT, local, verified).
- Register-level LEDC, E-stop and panic hook: a159x36 QEMU (GPL, native Windows, verified).
- TWDT firing: esp-emu or hardware.
- Waveform-level PWM and panic-pin checks: only hardware with a logic analyzer.

answers.question: Contradiction: serial transport — does SerialVehicleIO work with any pyserial URL (socket://, rfc2217://)?
answers.answer:
Resolved. The claim is false as stated.

socket:// (pyserial 3.5):
- protocol_socket.in_waiting returns len(select(...)), i.e. 0 or 1.
- SerialVehicleIO._pump reads in_waiting bytes once per call.
- Measured today on Espressif QEMU with the UART0 build, using the unmodified non-blocking loop (poll(block=False) + send at 20 Hz): 73 of ≈200 telemetry frames in 10 s, with no stale event.
- The backlog hides the delay because age is stamped on receipt. The earlier probe, with different loop timing, did get TELEMETRY_STALE.
- Only blocking connect/arm/_wait calls are reliable. The earlier 'yes (20 Hz, 0 frame errors)' came from test adapters (CountingPort, MSG_PEEK).

rfc2217://:
- in_waiting is correct: it returns the queue size.
- But pyserial's rfc2217 client rejects write_timeout (NotImplementedError). SerialVehicleIO.open()/_port_opener passes write_timeout=0.05, so the transport must be built without it.
- QEMU and esp-emu serve raw TCP only.

Fix, verified:
- Put pyserial's own examples/rfc2217_server.py in front of the raw TCP port: `-p 2218 socket://127.0.0.1:5594`. It accepts URLs via serial_for_url.
- Result: 200/200 frames, 200/200 sends, 0 events in 10 s.
- Alternative: loop in _pump until in_waiting==0.

answers.question: Contradiction: esp-emulator status and fit (RISC-V only vs S3 since 0.43.0; HWCDC/TWDT claims; licence)
answers.answer:
Both sides were partly right. Current facts:

What is true:
- The esp-emu binary supports esp32s3 since 0.43.0 (2026-09-18). It ran this project's Arduino 2.0.17 build in WSL2 again today (probe).
- pytest-embedded-espemu's main README still lists only c3/c5/c6/h2/p4/s31.
- esp-emu is not open source. The repo contains only LICENSE (Apache-2.0), README.md, install.sh, docs/ and tools/ (79 KB, GitHub language 'Python'). Issue #10 ('Will source code be published…', 2026-09-06) is open with no answer.
- Binaries exist only for Linux x86_64/arm64 and macOS arm64. The browser WASM build covers C3/C6/P4 only. On this PC it therefore needs WSL2.

Corrections to the overstatements, measured today:
- App-mode HWCDC is unreachable: only the UART0/UART1 TCP bridges exist, and USJ is bridged only in download strap 0x04.
- The S3 TWDT and IWDT do fire.
- But every firmware-initiated reset (abort, TWDT, IWDT, esp_restart) becomes rst:0x9 RTCWDT_SYS_RST, so esp_reset_reason() returns WDT(7).
- The earlier 'correct SOFTWARE' reason came from the host control command `reset --soft`, not from esp_restart().
- With --elf, esp-emu intercepts abort/esp_panic_handler and halts the run.
- All GPIO inputs read HIGH.
- LEDC is modelled at register level only, with no pin waveform.
- 0.476× real time.

Fit: optional, useful only for checking that the TWDT/IWDT actually fire. It is closed source and cannot run on Windows without WSL2.

answers.question: Contradiction: QEMU flash-image recipe (DIO build required vs 16 MB padding enough; '-65536' harmless?)
answers.answer:
Resolved by measurement. A probe compared esp_flash_read() in each read mode against the memory-mapped copy.

QIO build padded to 16 MB:
- Boots, and the app runs from cache.
- Runtime QIO reads are shifted +2 bytes.
- NVS/Preferences never persist: the counter reads 0 on every boot.
- The core dump partition reads as -65536 on every boot, and as 688128000 after a panic.
- So '-65536' is not harmless noise: it is #169 showing through, and it breaks anything that reads flash at runtime.

DIO build (8 MB):
- Runtime DIO reads are correct.
- NVS persists across esp_restart and abort (0→1→2).
- No '-65536'.

Conclusions:
- The harness report's 'DIO build required' is the right recipe. '16 MB padding' fixes boot only.
- In the DIO build, reads switched to FASTRD/DOUT/QOUT at runtime are shifted −1 and QIO +4. Only the build's own mode is safe.
- DOUT is not available as a precompiled Arduino 2.0.17 S3 variant, so it is not a practical route.
- Separately, 2 of 7 default-accelerator DIO boots crashed QEMU (#175), so CI needs retries.
- PR #177 would fix #169 upstream; it is still open.

answers.question: Contradiction: pytest-embedded-qemu on Windows ('unknown' because of pexpect.spawn vs 4/4 runs on this PC)
answers.answer:
Resolved from source; both reports are compatible.
- In pytest-embedded-qemu 2.9.3 (PyPI 2026-08-31), only Qemu.execute_efuse_command() imports pexpect and calls pexpect.spawn. That call is POSIX-only and runs espefuse against QEMU.
- --qemu-efuse-path on its own does two things:
  - writes the default eFuse blob;
  - adds `-drive file=…,if=none,format=raw,id=efuse -global driver=nvram.<target>.efuse,property=drive,value=efuse`.
  Neither needs pexpect.
- The harness report's native-Windows result stands: S3 boot, QMP hard reset, and PlatformIO Unity JUnit results in 4/4 runs.
- The only piece that will fail on Windows is burning eFuses through execute_efuse_command, which this project does not need.

answers.question: Contradiction: HWCDC in simulation ('only Wokwi can exercise the unmodified HWCDC protocol' vs Wokwi unverified vs esp32sim/danish9661 claims)
answers.answer:
Resolved. 'Only Wokwi' is false.

esp32sim (MIT, main 4ab7e90, WebAssembly build under Node on Windows) ran the unmodified production image today (Arduino 2.0.17, CDC_ON_BOOT=1, USB_MODE=1 → HWCDC):
- After an injected HELLO, the firmware sent a HELLO_ACK and then telemetry frames exactly every 50.000 ms emulated.
- The source explains why: its USJ model raises SOF 4×/ms, so HWCDC's tick-hook isPlugged() stays true.
- Remaining gap: its host serial channel is JSON text. Bytes ≥0x80 cannot be injected, and output bytes ≥0x80 become U+FFFD. So byte-exact protocol checks need a small patch.

Other candidates:
- Wokwi: still untested for 2.0.17 HWCDC. It depends on whether its USJ model raises SOF, and it needs the cloud upload.
- danish9661's emulator: its README claims USB-CDC, validated with arduino-cli and the esp32 core 3.3.10 (Arduino 3.x). Not tried here; no 2.0.17 evidence.
- Espressif QEMU, a159x36 QEMU and esp-emu: none has an app-mode USB-Serial-JTAG data path.

answers.question: Contradiction: QEMU boot reliability and time base (5/24 stalls vs none; #175; different time bases across backends)
answers.answer:
Partly reconciled by measurement on this PC today.

Boot reliability:
- Default accelerator (MTTCG): 2 of 7 DIO boots ended with a host QEMU 'Segmentation fault' during boot. That matches #175 ('SIGSEGV … thread=multi … only during guest boot'). To a TCP client it looks like a stall or reset after the bootloader, which most likely explains the harness agent's 5/24.
- -accel tcg,thread=single removed the boot crashes (6/6) but broke software resets (3/3). After esp_restart or abort the guest hit 'unrecognized opcode (pc = 4200cba0)' and QEMU then segfaulted.
- -icount shift=3,sleep=off restarted fine (2/2).
- The single LOOP_OVERRUN in 13 min fits QEMU following the host clock under load.
- Recommendation: retry when the QEMU process dies, or use -icount.

Time bases (guest time / wall time, from 1 Hz probe lines):
- Espressif QEMU: 0.996 median (0.981–1.009).
- a159x36 QEMU: 0.995.
- esp-emu: 0.476 (0.457–0.491).
- esp32sim wasm: 0.69–0.70 with JIT, 0.36 without, but host-steppable.
- QEMU -icount shift=3: ≈1.35×, deterministic until host input.
- Wokwi: CPU capped at ~8 MHz with exact peripheral timing; overall rate not measured.

Wall-clock timeouts on the laptop (TELEMETRY_STALE 0.3 s) therefore do not transfer between backends. Use SerialVehicleIO(clock=...) with emulated time wherever it is available.

answers.question: Contradiction: a159x36/qemu (dismissed for 'no Windows binaries' vs win64 tarballs exist; GPIO/LEDC/I2C models untested)
answers.answer:
Resolved and tested today.
- Downloaded qemu-xtensa-softmmu-v5.4.1-x86_64-w64-mingw32.tar.gz (21 MB, release 2026-06-29) to D:\xetulai\_platformio\a159_qemu.
- It runs natively on Windows: 'QEMU emulator version 9.2.2 (v5.4.1)', machine esp32s3.
- Source checked at 03be9af (v5.4.2 tag, 2026-07-07, no binaries). It is GPL-licensed.

With the same probe (QIO image, UART0):
- ledcSetup works: LEDC is modelled, timer config reads back, duty_r=0x4cc0, and outsel21=0x49 routes LEDC to the pin.
- LEDC state is readable headless via HMP `xp /4wx 0x60019000`.
- LEDC registers survive esp_restart and abort.
- A servo device on GPIO21 converts pulse width to an angle, but only on the display; GPIO_IN sampling saw no edges.
- Pulls are modelled: pullup14=1, pulldown5=0, floating=0.
- GPIO injection works headless: HMP `sendkey 2 2500` drove GPIO14 low (pin14 1→0→1). Key '1' maps to GPIO0 (a strap pin, avoid it).
- No #169: all six read modes are correct and NVS persists.
- Reset reasons are correct: SW(3) after esp_restart, PANIC(4) after abort. The panic hook's GPIO-matrix write took effect.
- The TWDT did not fire (3/3), like Espressif QEMU.
- I2C0 has fixed tmp105@0x48 and mpu6050@0x68 only.
- 1 of 5 runs exited right after the bootloader (not diagnosed).
- USB-JTAG was not tested (UART0 builds only).

Verdict: the best free, open-source, native-Windows backend for register-level E-stop, PWM and panic-hook tests. It needs a test build with E-stop on GPIO14 (and PWM on GPIO21 to use the servo view), and a UART0 console.

answers.question: Contradiction: primary recommendation and the 'open-source' criterion (QEMU vs Wokwi vs esp-emu as winner)
answers.answer:
There is no single winner. Ranking per test goal, open source first (evidence from today's runs):

1. Protocol and state machine, bit-exact: the PC build of the C++ core (703 checks), FirmwareModel and vectors.json, which already exist. Add random differential tests (Hypothesis is not installed yet).
2. Unmodified production image (HWCDC) with the laptop stack: esp32sim (MIT).
   - Verified: WebAssembly build on Windows via Node, HELLO→HELLO_ACK plus 20 Hz telemetry, exact cycle-stepped lock-step, GPIO injection.
   - Needs: a small serial patch for bytes ≥0x80.
   - Missing: LEDC waveform and TWDT.
3. Real SerialVehicleIO over a serial port (UART0 variant): Espressif QEMU (GPL, native Windows).
   - Use a DIO build (#169), the pyserial rfc2217_server bridge (200/200 frames), retry on QEMU crash (#175) or -icount, and esp-idf-monitor for backtraces.
   - Keep PWM off: ledcSetup panics. GPIO reads 0, and the TWDT/IWDT never fire.
4. E-stop, LEDC registers and panic-hook register effect: a159x36/qemu v5.4.1 (GPL, native Windows).
   - Verified: LEDC model, pull resistors, GPIO14 via HMP sendkey, correct reset reasons, no #169.
   - Needs a test pin map (E-stop on GPIO14).
5. Watchdog firing: esp-emu 0.44.0 (closed binary, WSL2).
   - TWDT and IWDT fire, but the reset reason always reads WDT.
   - Final check on hardware without OpenOCD attached.
6. PWM waveform, ESC line low on panic, true reset reasons: hardware plus a logic analyzer. Wokwi only if the cloud upload is accepted (untested: HWCDC SOF dependency, RTC partial).
7. Future I2C sensors: Wokwi custom chips (cloud) or an esp32sim board model (Rust, local). QEMU and esp-emu have no useful devices; a159x36 has fixed tmp105/mpu6050.

Licences:
- Open source: Espressif QEMU (GPL-2.0), a159x36 QEMU (GPL), esp32sim (MIT), PICSimLab (GPL).
- Velxio is AGPLv3 plus commercial. Its self-hosted ESP32-S3 engine is the lcgamboa QEMU fork (open); only its STM32/Raspberry Pi engines need licensed binaries. Its docs target Arduino 3.x, DIO and 4 MB images.
- Closed: the Wokwi engine (cloud) and the esp-emu binary (repo holds docs/scripts only; issue #10 open).

Open-source S3 emulators now proven here with Arduino firmware: Espressif QEMU, a159x36 QEMU and esp32sim.
